Meta-backed 250 MW solar farm breaks ground in Arkansas

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arkansas is getting another 250 megawatts (MW) of solar power, and Meta has signed up to buy it.
  • In a recent development, EDP Renewables North America (EDPR NA) broke ground on Cypress Knee Solar in Chicot County, in the southeastern corner of the state, on November 4.
  • Meta’s long-term power purchase agreement helps it work toward its pledge to match 100% of its annual electricity use with renewable energy generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arkansas is getting another 250 megawatts (MW) of solar power, and Meta has signed up to buy it.

In a recent development, EDP Renewables North America (EDPR NA) broke ground on Cypress Knee Solar in Chicot County, in the southeastern corner of the state, on November 4. The solar farm is expected to be completed by 2028, bringing several hundred construction jobs and an estimated $25 million in county revenue over its lifetime.

Meta’s long-term power purchase agreement helps it work toward its pledge to match 100% of its annual electricity use with renewable energy generation. Don’t confuse that pledge with Meta powering its data centers with renewables around the clock, though – Facebook and Instagram’s parent tech giant is also backing new gas plants to meet its growing power demand.

According to recent reports, the companies announced the deal in May. Cypress Knee is their third clean-energy agreement, bringing the total capacity covered by Meta’s deals with EDPR NA to 545 MW.

“As energy demand continues to rise, projects like Cypress Knee Solar help strengthen grid reliability while creating jobs, generating meaningful local revenue, and delivering long-term benefits to the communities that host them,” mentioned EDPR NA CEO Sandhya Ganapathy.

EDPR NA claims it has already contributed more than $77,000 during project development, including money to restore the Lakeside High School greenhouse, resources for the Lakeside Robotics team, and funding for the Lake Village food pantry.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Data Center revenue surged 110% to $107.6 billion, while adjusted EPS reached $2.68.
  • Nvidia projected $130 billion in Q4 revenue, sending NVDA shares approximately 2.5% higher in premarket trading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia reported Q3 FY2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, beating Wall Street expectations.

Data Center revenue surged 110% to $107.6 billion, while adjusted EPS reached $2.68.

Nvidia projected $130 billion in Q4 revenue, sending NVDA shares approximately 2.5% higher in premarket trading.

In a recent development, nvidia stock (NASDAQ: NVDA) is showing signs of a potential rebound after delivering another blockbuster quarterly earnings report, with strong AI demand and an upbeat revenue forecast giving investors fresh reasons to turn bullish. The chipmaker exceeded Wall Street expectations across its latest results and projected another quarter of substantial growth.

It has been revealed that nvidia shares gained approximately 2.5% in premarket trading on November 18, following the company’s third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings announcement after Tuesday’s closing bell. The stock had ended the previous session at $155.46, down 0.44%, as investors remained cautious ahead of the results.

However, the earnings release shifted attention back to Nvidia’s business momentum, with revenue growth exceeding 100% and management offering a stronger-than-expected outlook for the next quarter.

The initial reaction suggests investors are responding positively to continued demand for AI computing infrastructure. Nvidia’s results also provide fresh evidence that major technology companies are continuing to invest heavily in data centers and advanced processors.

Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from $57 billion in the same quarter last year. Revenue also increased 20% from the previous quarter, highlighting the continued acceleration in demand for its computing platforms.

Industry observers note that the firm reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.68, compared with $1.27 a year earlier. GAAP diluted EPS reached $2.70, while net income climbed 105% year over year to $65.3 billion. The Data Center division remained the primary growth engine, generating $107.6 billion in revenue, up 110% year over year. The segment accounted for the overwhelming majority of Nvidia’s quarterly sales, reflecting continued demand for AI accelerators, networking systems and data-center infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the quarterly earnings beat, Nvidia’s forward guidance is another major factor supporting the positive market reaction. The company expects fourth-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. This compares with analyst expectations of slightly more than $125 billion, suggesting Nvidia sees demand continuing to expand into the next quarter.

Industry observers note that nvidia also confirmed that its next-generation Vera Rubin NVL72 platform has entered production shipments. The systems are already operating with several infrastructure partners, including Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and CoreWeave.

Nvidia expects fourth-quarter gross margins of 71% to 72%, below the 74.8% GAAP margin reported in Q3. The decline suggests that revenue growth and margin performance will both remain notable measures of the company’s execution.

Nvidia’s latest results reinforce the strength of AI infrastructure demand, but the stock’s outlook is not without challenges. Technology companies continue to invest in advanced computing capacity to support AI models, cloud services and enterprise applications. Nvidia’s Data Center growth demonstrates that these investments are still translating into significant chip demand.

Industry observers note that leadership uncertainty adds another consideration. Nvidia’s results arrived amid a major transition following Jensen Huang’s departure, with interim CEO Colette Kress leading the firm while the board searches for a permanent successor. The transition could become an notable factor in investor confidence, particularly given Huang’s central role in Nvidia’s strategy and product roadmap.

Nvidia’s earnings beat and $130 billion revenue forecast have strengthened the bullish case, but the stock needs to reclaim key key levels to confirm a meaningful recovery.

On the upside, $158–$159 is the first resistance zone to watch. A sustained breakout above this region could open the door toward $170–$171, followed by a stronger resistance area near $181–$182. These levels could become key if post-earnings buying continues.

On the downside, $154 is the immediate support level, followed by $149 and the recent 52-week low near $148.80. A break below this zone could weaken the recovery attempt and expose NVDA to further selling pressure.

Sources indicate that overall, a sustained move above $159 would strengthen the bullish setup, while failure to hold $154 could bring sellers back into control. The earnings reaction needs confirmation through regular-session volume and price action.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kia’s Sportage-sized electric SUV, the EV5, was spotted with a distinct latest style and an overhauled interior, including a huge widescreen infotainment screen.
  • The EV5 is the fully electric SUV we want, but can’t have in the US.
  • It has already been a significant part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia’s Sportage-sized electric SUV, the EV5, was spotted with a distinct latest style and an overhauled interior, including a huge widescreen infotainment screen.

The EV5 is the fully electric SUV we want, but can’t have in the US. After launching it in China in 2023, Kia introduced the global version last year, which is now on sale in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other markets.

It has already been a significant part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.

Kia appears to be preparing an updated version. A upcoming EV5 model was recently spotted by ShortsCar in a South Korean parking garage without camouflage, and it’s expected to be the updated version.

You can see in the video that the design has changed quite a bit. Up front, the hood and headlights remain about the same, but new design elements like a black accent light are added.

It also features a unique bumper design, similar to that of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

According to recent reports, the biggest changes are inside, where the interior appears to be completely overhauled. Instead of the current large display screen spanning from the driver to the center, the newly introduced EV5 features a display that extends from the center to the passenger side.

According to recent reports, there also appears to be an added slim display in front of the steering wheel. Since Hyundai has recently added a slim display to vehicles equipped with its Pleos infotainment system, the updated Kia EV5 is expected to feature the upcoming setup.

However, this is still speculation and has not been confirmed. The center console has also changed. Instead of the physical buttons, it now has a cover, giving it a cleaner overall look.

According to a sticker on the back, the updated EV5 is set to launch in the Philippines. Given Kia initially released the EV5 in China in 2023, it will be due for a facelift around 2027.

In a recent development, kia has yet to confirm whether and when it will launch the updated EV5 in other global markets, such as Europe or Korea. It will likely arrive after the China-made version, like the current EV5. We should learn more details soon.

Ledger, a crypto wallet firm, mentioned it had experienced a security incident related to Optimizely, a third-party service used on its official website, but reassured its users about the security of their devices and private keys.

In a post, Ledger remarked it was aware of a security incident impacting Optimizely, a third-party service provider used by many other sites as well.

We are aware of a security incident affecting Optimizely, a third-party service used on https://t.co/d2pWxdG49X, alongside numerous other websites. Our team has remediated the problem, and the malicious code is no longer being served through our website. This incident does not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices. Your private keys remain protected by your Ledger device. For more information from Optimizely: https://t.co/CxzmBxYadb.

Website optimization platform Optimizely stated it had discovered and contained a security incident affecting some of its Web Experimentation customers on November 16, 2026. Optimizely stated that the vulnerable path has now been blocked, the injected code has been removed, and customers have been contacted directly.

Along these lines, Ledger confirmed that its team had remediated the issue and that the malicious code was no longer being served through its website.

Ledger emphasizes that the incident did not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices and that user private keys remain protected by their Ledger device, thus reassuring customers that the incident had not compromised the core security of its wallet products.

Sources indicate that according to researcher Scott Helme, on November 16, 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organizations' websites across several sectors through the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform. The websites included Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger, and Peacock.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed, with only 1 of the 188 infected snippets found, down from 169.

Industry observers note that the main point is that trusted JavaScript is not always trustworthy. A third-party dependency can exploit a website without ever breaking the website's own code or infrastructure.

#29606. Tech Report: NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

Tech Report: NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1289 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.
  • Most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number.
  • Recent findings suggest that house of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

Recent findings suggest that house of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:.

cap(t) = 2.5% − 0.9% × min(t, 24) / 24.

Industry observers note that here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:.

Sources indicate that the yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

Industry observers note that newly introduced tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:.

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio.

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

According to recent reports, the formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Industry observers note that stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

In a recent development, holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every upcoming token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Recent findings suggest that validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics noted the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Industry observers note that two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a new proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to patch their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

It has been revealed that three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Recent findings suggest that price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

Once America’s most popular electric pickup, the Ford F-150 Lightning is finding a second life on the used market.

Sources indicate that the F-150 Lightning is hard to pass up at 50% to 60% off sticker price, even used. With latest models no longer available, Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes on the used market.

After the last model rolled off the assembly line last December, CEO Jim Farley mentioned the decision to end production came as the “very high-end EVs, the $50K, 70K, $80,000 vehicles, they just weren’t selling.”.

Industry observers note that at 50% to 60% off, it now looks like a bargain in the used market. “When Ford was selling it brand upcoming, the math was complicated,” Jimmy Douglas, CEO of Plug, a wholesale EV dealer, recently told Bloomberg.

On the used market, however, “the Lightning is 50% to 60% of the sticker price and that is really a sweet spot,” he added.

Used Ford F-150 Lightnings are selling in about 20 days, less than half the 44-day average for used vehicles in the US. According to Edmunds.com, prices are now up 4% to about $50,000 since the start of the year.

Douglass mentioned that close to one-third of used models are sold by rival dealerships that would normally flip them back to Ford. However, many are opting to sell them directly because of demand.

Sources indicate that chase Norris from Colorado called the electric pickup a bargain. He purchased a used Lightning for around $40,000 and considers it a major upgrade from his previous gas F-150.

EV Group CEO and cofounder Alex Lawrence, which sells pre-owned electric vehicles, remarked he can’t get his hands on any reasonably priced used F-150 Lightnings at the moment.

He said many Lightning buyers use it as a second truck to save money during their weekly commute.

It looks essentially the same as the gas-powered F-150, offers instant torque, and produces zero tailpipe emissions, but the electric pickup failed to meet Ford’s expectations because of its higher price.

The base F-150 Lightning Pro debuted in 2021 with a starting MSRP of $39,974, but that was promptly raised to around $60,000 a year or so later.

According to Edmunds.com, the average transaction price for the F-150 Lightning in its first year of sales was $79,000 because Ford focused on higher-priced trims. The gas version’s ATP was about $19,000 less.

Industry observers note that even with the higher sticker price, Ford was losing a considerable amount on each Lightning it produced. In Q1 2024, Ford lost more than $100,000 on every EV it built.

Next year, Ford will take another crack at the electric pickup market with the Fathom, the first vehicle based on its “groundbreaking” upcoming Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform.

Ford said the Fathom will start at $28,350 for the standard-range version. Even with the $1,595 delivery fee included, the electric pickup will start at under $30,000.

As the first vehicle built on its UEV platform, Ford promises the Fathom will be a step-change from its first-generation EVs.

According to Ford, the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4 and will be the first vehicle with Apple Maps directly integrated into the navigation system.

We also know the electric pickup will have a NACS port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger this summer.

Ford reportedly aims to sell around 100,000 Fathoms in its first year. CEO Jim Farley said on the organization’s third-quarter earnings call last week that the launch remains on track for Q4 2027.

Farley called the Fathom a “breakthrough product” and said that the MSRP under $30,000 is perfect for today’s market.

At least some F-150 owners are already trading in for lower-priced options. A member of the Ford F-150 Lightning Owners Group, JF, said that although it was a great ride, “Carvana gave us just a little less than we paid upcoming,” adding, “R2, here we come!”.

When Torque News reached out, JF said he “really liked the Lightning,” but wanted something smaller. “With the current increase in resale value, the time to trade seemed right,” JF added.

In a recent development, the Rivian R2 (see our review) Performance with the Launch Package is now available to order starting at $57,990 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 330 miles and 656 hp. The R2 Premium will go on sale later this year, starting at $53,990.

In Spring 2027, Rivian will launch the R2 Standard, starting at $44,990 with an estimated range of up to 275 miles and 350 hp.

So were they losing $100k / truck, or the average loss when all development was included ended up being $100k? Major difference. I don't believe the cost to build each one was $170k+. That makes no sense. They just priced them too high to amortize the development costs over enough vehicles to make them profitable. Every vehicle has to sell a minimum # before they start to make a profit.

In a recent development, surging F-150 Lightning sales on the used market show buyers want electric pickups. But at the right price.

It has been revealed that at $60,000 to $70,000, the Lightning wasn’t so attractive, but at $40,000 used, it suddenly is. Perhaps Ford is on to something with its next-gen EV pickup, the Fathom, set to go on sale starting at under $30,000.

Will it deliver on its promise? Ford has yet to reveal battery specs, towing capacity, range, or any other specs. We should learn more soon.

Ripple’s XRP has climbed 4% in the past 24 hours, reclaiming the $1 level, while outperforming Bitcoin and the overall crypto market. The rally also put pressure on leveraged traders, as XRP saw around $6 million in liquidations, including $3.56 million from short traders. For short-term price moves, spot trading and whale activity can therefore have a bigger impact.

Sources indicate that although U.S. spot XRP ETFs recorded $19.13 million in outflows over the past week, their largest weekly withdrawal in eight months, spot market buyers have continued to support XRP near key price levels. Grayscale and Bitwise led the outflows.

ETF holdings also represent only around 1.6% of XRP’s circulating supply.

For a stronger recovery, XRP needs to close above $1.00 on the daily chart. A break above this level could open the way toward $1.09–$1.15.

On the downside, if XRP falls below $0.97 and loses the key $0.90 support, the price could drop further toward $0.80.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like many equipment brands, German forklift maker Jungheinrich has been struggling to crack the Asian industrial markets – but the firm is set to change all that with the launch of a new line of 1.6- to 3-ton class electric forklifts designed specifically to navigate the region’s tight warehouses and factories.

Jungheinrich launched the next generation of its EFG MB and MC electric counterbalance forklifts, giving businesses more flexibility to match truck performance with the battery options, charging systems, and operator features that meet their specific needs.

“Different operations have different requirements,” stated Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant, China. “With the EFG M series, customers can configure the (forklift) truck around their application, workload and operators – whether they need greater maneuverability for confined warehouse spaces, or a stable, powerful truck for demanding transport and stacking work.”.

In a recent development, forklift buyers can choose between two performance packages, prioritizing energy efficiency for everyday material handling or more driving and lifting muscle for more demanding, high-throughput operations. The higher-performance package comes standard on models rated for 2.5-3.0 tons, with a choice of either lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries with 346 or 690 Ah of capacity available to suit different workloads and shift patterns. Both ship with regenerative braking tech that can recover up to 30% of the energy used in stopping and lowering loads, too, helping to keep these machines running longer between charging sessions.

“We carried out extensive customer research to understand what the market needs,” added Jing Xue. “Customers can invest in the performance required today and add further capabilities as their application demands.”.

Optional features include fingertip controls, a larger 4″ digital display, upgraded LED lighting, and operator-assistance (ADAS) systems, while flexible seating and cabin configurations are designed to keep drivers comfortable through long shifts. A slim B-pillar and glass roof help visibility in busy warehouses, while the four-wheel EFG MC gets automatic cornering speed reduction as standard. Integrated telematics are also standard, giving fleet managers access to utilization data, maintenance planning and pre-operational checks from day one.

Jungheinrich claims the order books for both the three- and four-wheel electric forklifts are open now, ready to be supported by the company’s 6,000+ person strong service network across the Asia-Pacific region.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question.
  • It has been revealed that the concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders.
  • According to recent reports, janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question. Now, we have an answer: Electrovaya will supply the batteries.

It has been revealed that the concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders. That is, rolling body and chassis without an engine and transmission that’s ready to receive power from Cummins, Detroit, International, or Volvo Penta. That’s the role that Janus Electric sees itself occupying, and it seems to be working.

According to recent reports, janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants. When the HVIP voucher is combined with the Port of Los Angeles’ “Plus” support, customers can received up to $166,000 per truck conversion. Factor in the massive fuel savings of electric and the classic good looks of square-nose Western Star truck body, and it’s easy to see why they’d be a popular choice.

In a recent development, as Jerry Seinfeld taught us however, it’s one thing to take a reservation – it’s another thing to deliver. To help make it happen, Janus has inked a battery supply deal with Electrovaya that will see a $26 million initial purchase orders for Electrovaya battery packs to demand for Janus’ products in the US and Canada, along with the battery company purchasing approximately $1.4 million in Janus stock with (what seems to be) actual money.

Sources indicate that “Electrovaya is an notable partner to Janus Electric, and we’re particularly pleased it has decided to invest directly in our business,” explains Ben Hutt, Managing Director and CEO of Janus Electric. “The investment is a strong vote of confidence in our technology and approach to electrifying heavy transport.”.

The Janus Electric-repowered trucks carry a stout, 480 hp electric motor drawing power from a standard 310 kWh battery pack, with up to two battery packs (one on each side) of the truck. In practice, that gives the Janus trucks up to 370 miles of loaded range. After that, the batteries can be DC fast charged in under 90 minutes, or swapped for fresh ones in about four minutes without too much in the way of specialized equipment. That’s not just Janus’ killer app, it means that a battery supply deal like this one with a strategic partner who’s invested in the fledgling tech giant’s success is such a huge deal.

Sources indicate that “Reliable battery supply is critical to our growth,” adds Hutt, “and Electrovaya’s expanding North American manufacturing capabilities will be important as we scale. Both companies see considerable opportunity in this market, and we look forward to building on our partnership.”.

Sources indicate that for their part, Electrovoya executives seem to know their role here, and seem excited to be a part of what Janus is doing. “Class 8 trucking is one of the most exciting and demanding frontiers in electrification, and Janus has demonstrated real commercial traction with fleets in the US, Canada and Australia,” noted Dr. Raj Das Gupta, CEO of Electrovaya. “Janus has developed a practical solution to one of the major challenges facing heavy transport, enabling diesel-powered trucks to be converted to electric without compromising their commercial operations.”.

Electrovaya will be expanding its American manufacturing capacity with lithium-ion cell, module, and battery pack production at its new, potentially BABA-compliant facility in Jamestown, New York, which is expected to come online in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin has achieved another milestone. Its total market supply has reached $2.7 billion, making a fresh high level in circulation, according to data reported on the X platform. RLUSD supply climbed to the $2.7 billion record on Sunday, Nov. 15, a 57% rise from the $1.72 billion mark seen on Sept. 14, data revealed.

Industry observers note that the market supply of the Ripple-backed stablecoin has surged to a new ATH, exceeding the previous $1.72 billion milestone set in September. According to the data, RLUSD’s circulating supply currently stands at $2.7 billion, up from the $1.2 billion level reached in January. This rise signals an expansion of RLUSD’s liquidity across the wider blockchain ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the supply expansion indicates rising demand for RLUSD as global customers gradually embrace the stablecoin for payments and DeFi applications. This surge positions RLUSD as a ‘digital dollar’ that allows owners to execute cross-border payments and on-chain settlements.

Industry observers note that the growth is pushing RLUSD higher into the stablecoin market. Now, the asset ranks as the 7th-largest stablecoin by market supply. The more supply means deeper liquidity across the public blockchain ecosystem, supporting cross-border payments and on-chain utility.

The Ripple-focused institutional stablecoin has reached another milestone, increasing its market supply to $2.7 billion. Interestingly, a large amount of this freshly issued liquidity operates on external public blockchains, not within the XRP Ledger network.

Recent findings suggest that metrics show that a large share of the fresh RLUSD supply sits on Ethereum, with Ethereum holding more than those in the XRP Ledger. This indicates rising use of Ethereum as a liquidity and settlement network for the stablecoin, while RLUSD continues to expand across protocols.

Recent findings suggest that on-chain data indicates that out of the $2.7 billion in RLUSD circulation, about $1.73 billion runs on Ethereum. The XRP Ledger holds around $855 million, representing about 30% of the circulation.

In a recent development, over time, Ethereum’s share of the supply has risen to about 60%. This shift is because Ethereum offers a deeper DeFi market, including lending and more. XRP Ledger is closer to activating its native lending infrastructure.

Although Shiba Inu has continued to struggle amid the persisting market volatility, showing substantial daily losses, the leading meme token has just reached a major milestone in its holder count.

The latest on-chain data from Etherscan reveals that Shiba Inu has seen a rapid surge in adoption, with its number of on-chain holders surpassing 1.7 million for the first time.

While this has been a long-anticipated milestone in the SHIB community, the data has drawn attention across the market as it shows that SHIB now has about 1,700,247 holders as of Tuesday, November 17.

Reaching a 1.7 million holder count at a time like this, when the market is facing extreme volatility, marks a major milestone for the SHIB ecosystem as it signals its growing appeal despite unfavorable market conditions.

Nonetheless, it is notable to note that the number of holders alone does not necessarily indicate an increase in unique individual investors, as existing investors could be opening newly introduced accounts.

However, each additional wallet holding SHIB tends to bolster its growing on-chain presence, positioning the asset for potential demand that could eventually bolster its price movement.

Although increases in holder count do not automatically trigger a price rally for the concerned asset, market participants expect that the fresh holder milestone could further drive demand for SHIB and potentially drive a relief rally for the asset following the extreme volatility facing the market.

Shiba Inu’s 1.7 million holder milestone arrived when SHIB was trading at about $0.00000382, following a 0.78% decline over the last day.

With its price trading far below local support levels, its user activity has flashed a brief bullish signal that is expected to help the asset stabilize its price movement.

Energica rises from the ashes with looks for cheaper electric motorcycles

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has unveiled a major revival under fresh international ownership.
  • Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
  • Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has unveiled a major revival under fresh international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the manufacturer behind it is going to look quite different this time around.

Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.

That could be a major deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

Industry observers note that the revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica indicates its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

According to recent reports, the first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia, the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica intends to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely latest machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Industry observers note that energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

For anyone who followed the electric motorcycle industry over the last decade, Energica’s disappearance was a particularly painful one. This wasn’t some startup with a couple of renderings and a dream. Energica built some of the highest-performance electric motorcycles on the road and spent four seasons supplying the motorcycles for the FIM MotoE World Cup, experience that helped develop its high-voltage and DC fast-charging technology.

Now the company gets something relatively rare in the motorcycle industry: a second chance.

And if moving production to Asia really can knock around 20% off Energica’s prices while retaining the Italian engineering that made the bikes special in the first place, Energica 2.0 might have a considerably better shot at turning great electric motorcycles into a sustainable business.

Industry observers note that it seems like moving toward Asian manufacturing is all but inevitable here. It was the expensive European manufacturing of low-volume motorcycles that weighed so heavily on Energica’s balance sheets in the years up to their financial troubles, and so shifting production to countries with both the expertise and the cost benefits for motorcycle manufacturing simply makes sense.

It has been revealed that energica isn’t alone in discovering the economics of moving electric motorcycle production to Asia. Zero Motorcycles spent years manufacturing its bikes in California before beginning a major shift toward production in the Philippines in 2023, including both complete motorcycles and major subassemblies. Now the company works with multiple factories, including major manufacturers like Zongshen in China, to reduce production costs for its electric motorcycles while still maintaining the ‘designed in California’ marketing angle.

It’s too early to tell how the new strategy will play out for Energica, but the fact that the tech giant is now following a more well-worn trail is a positive sign for those who have spent the last two years hoping for a revival.

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1018 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla to end Cybertruck production as sales stall at ~10% of blueprint

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that tesla is ending Cybertruck production.
  • Recent findings suggest that musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production.
  • Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tesla is ending Cybertruck production. CEO Elon Musk unveiled early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries.

Recent findings suggest that musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production. But Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck is short on buyers, and it sells at roughly a tenth of the 250,000 units a year Tesla built its line for.

Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.

That’s all he noted. Nothing yet on how long Tesla will keep selling inventory or what happens to parts and service for existing owners.

Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries. It lumps them into “Other Models,” along with the Model S, Model X, and now the Semi.

That bucket tells the story anyway. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, down 48% year-over-year and the lowest since Q2 2021. With Model S and Model X production over since April, we estimated that 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks.

According to recent reports, that’s a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. Tesla planned the Cybertruck line for 250,000 units annually, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. So the truck is selling at about 12% of plan, and roughly a quarter of what’s actually installed.

It has been revealed that the US numbers from Cox Automotive are worse. Cox estimates 3,519 Cybertruck sales in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2, down from 14,416 in Q3 2024.

And not all of those were real customers. S&P Global Mobility data showed SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, and Musk’s companies took 1,339 in total, about 19% of US registrations that quarter. If it wasn’t for Musk’s self-dealing, the Cybertruck would probably be dead already.

Tesla tried to fix demand. It launched a cheaper rear-wheel-drive version in 2025 and pulled it months later, then brought a cheaper dual-motor trim to customers this summer. And then it raised prices by $5,000 in August. The dual-motor now starts at $74,990.

The “make room” explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of factory floor, by Tesla’s own count, and the Cybertruck line is already running at about a quarter of its installed capacity. Most of it is sitting idle.

The Cybercab also isn’t at a volume where it’s fighting anyone for floor space. Texas had 463 Cybercabs registered as of late October, and Tesla built a separate line for its “unboxed” manufacturing process.

If Tesla needs more Cybercab capacity down the road, it has the space. What it doesn’t want is to keep paying for a truck with its own stainless steel body, its own castings, and its own supply chain at 30,000 units a year.

Recent findings suggest that let’s call this what it is. Tesla isn’t ending the Cybertruck because the Cybercab needs room. It’s ending it because nobody’s buying it at anything close to the volume Tesla planned, and supporting a low-volume vehicle this unique is expensive.

In a recent development, I wouldn’t be surprised if Tesla lost a couple of billions on the Cybertruck experiment. Between R&D, pushing suppliers to produce 250,000 trucks per year, and deploying its own production line capable of 125,000 trucks per year, Tesla has invested billions. And with only ~70,000 trucks delivered in roughly 3 years, it probably never made any positive cash flow from the program.

It has been revealed that they are just in-between growth phases. No need to panic just because they have discontinued three vehicles and the last successful vehicle they rolled out was the Model Y in early 2020.

The Cybercab line gives Musk a forward-looking reason to wrap a product failure in. Tesla did the same thing when it ended Model S and Model X production this year to free up Fremont for Optimus. It’s a lot easier to say “we need room for the future” than “this didn’t sell.”.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve noted it many times: the Cybertruck is genuinely impressive to drive. Steer-by-wire and rear-wheel steering are real engineering, and nobody else has put them in a production pickup. But Tesla built a 250,000-unit factory for a polarizing $75,000+ truck that can’t be sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets. It just cancelled it for Australia and Fresh Zealand two weeks ago. The math was never going to work.

It’s truly a sign of Tesla today. Musk used to talk about having a more traditional electric truck design if Cybertruck fails, but I doubt we will see that. Again, Elon is betting the house on autonomy.

Industry News: BYD’s electric hypercar hits 312 mph, first production car over 500 km/h

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1063 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.
  • According to recent reports, the FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run.
  • BYD unveiled the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.

According to recent reports, the FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run. It’s the all-electric hypercar’s second top-speed record in just over a year, and the one it broke was its own.

BYD unveiled the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”.

In a recent development, abu Dhabi closed a 10 km section of the Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road (E11), in the emirate’s Al Dhafra Region, for the attempt. That gave the team a 7 km straight. Marc Basseng, the German racing driver who set the car’s previous record, was behind the wheel again.

According to recent reports, it took two days. Basseng maxed out at 490 km/h on the first day, per the FIA. After an overnight round of changes to the rear wing, damping, and tire pressures, he got to 503.17 km/h on his second attempt of November 1.

Sources indicate that the previous mark was 496.22 km/h (308 mph), set at Germany’s ATP Papenburg proving ground in September 2025. That run had already pushed the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ and its 490.48 km/h from 2019 off the top of the list.

Sources indicate that and it comes just days after BYD released footage of a U9 Xtreme crashing into a guardrail at about 280 mph during an earlier high-speed test. The driver walked away unharmed. BYD went right back out and hit 457.89 km/h on the next run.

According to recent reports, the U9 Xtreme is the track-focused version of the Yangwang U9, the flagship supercar from BYD’s luxury brand. It uses four electric motors, each rated at 555 kW and spinning up to 30,000 rpm, for 2,220 kW combined. That’s over 3,000 PS, or nearly 3,000 hp.

In a recent development, it runs on a 1,200-volt architecture with a track-grade version of BYD’s Blade Battery. Those are LFP cells, the same chemistry BYD puts in its cheapest city cars.

Industry observers note that for context, the Rimac Nevera R, which snagged a pile of EV world records last year, tops out at 431.45 km/h. The U9 Xtreme also holds the production EV lap record at the Nürburgring Nordschleife at 6:59.157.

In a recent development, only 30 will be built, and BYD is charging around $3 million apiece. Don’t expect to see one in the US, where BYD doesn’t sell passenger cars.

Sources indicate that the biggest one: this is a single-direction run. The two Guinness titles listed for the attempt, highest speed by a production car and by an electric production car, are both specified as “single direction.” BYD’s post claims four Guinness records, but the FIA’s announcement only lists those two for this run.

Industry observers note that production car top speed records have traditionally been the average of two runs in opposite directions, within an hour, to cancel out wind and road grade. That’s how Koenigsegg got its 447.19 km/h record with the Agera RS in 2017.

In a recent development, bugatti took heat for exactly this in 2019, when the Chiron hit 490 km/h one way on a pre-production car. Bugatti itself remarked it wasn’t an official record.

In a recent development, the car also ran on bespoke semi-slick tires developed with Giti Tire. It’s not clear whether the 30 customer cars will get them.

Recent findings suggest that A Chinese automaker best known for $10,000 city cars now builds the fastest production car in the world, and it’s electric. Not long ago, the conventional wisdom was that EVs couldn’t sustain high top speeds because the battery and motors would overheat long before the car ran out of road. BYD just ran 503 km/h on LFP cells. LFP cells!

In a recent development, but we’d hold BYD to the same standard we held Bugatti to. A one-way run on a highway with a 7 km straight is a great demo, not a definitive record, but impressive nonetheless.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chinese equipment brand Zoomlion indicated up to this week’s China International Agricultural Machinery Exhibition with a fresh ultra-high-horsepower hybrid tractor that sets a new benchmark, offering more than 1,600 hp while cutting back on both fuel and fumes.

Zoomlion calls its newly introduced 9DX hybrid tractor a radical rethink of what a modern ag unit can be, combining the all-day pulling power of a conventional diesel machine with the efficiency, accuracy, and instant torque benefits of electric drive. The tech giant claims its hybrid setup can reducing fuel consumption, emissions, and deliver lower operating costs, without asking massive industrial farming operations to walk away from diesel entirely.

The tractor itself gets a headline-grabbing 1,600 hp Zoomlion 9DX features an 800V hybrid electric powertrain and continuously variable transmission that delivering a peak torque of 7,200 Nm (~5,300 lb-ft) of torque. Getting all that power to the ground is a four track tank-drive system riding on Zoomlion’s in-house developed 762 mm (~30 inch) wide tracks that are designed to distribute the tractor’s considerable weight for maximum traction and minimum soil compaction. What’s more, the high-traction treads can push the massive machine to hit a maximum speed of 40 km/h across grades and slopes of up to 12 degrees.

The 9DX also gets a high-capacity hydraulic system capable of delivering 636 liters per minute of flow (~170 GPM), allowing it to work with some seriously heavy duty implements like ultra-wide seeders and variable-rate fertilizer applicators.

The Zoomlion 9DX was one of several new machines at this year’s exhibition, which hosted more than 3,000 exhibitors and vendors – but the massive hp numbers all over the show made an even bigger impression, leading AGCO’s director of global electronic and electrical engineering, Nicolas Meunier, to tell Chinese State news agency Xinhua that the country had moved on from producing mostly low-horsepower tractors to building some seriously large machines.

There’s no official word on specs and batteries, but the company has developed an 800V modular battery pack system for its other equipment offerings that can scale from 140-800 kWh of capacity while other top-shelf Zoomlion tractors featuring an ag version of Cummins’ 15 liter turbodiesel.

The 9DX tops off what’s sure to be another record year for Zoomlion, which is coming off strong early export quarters shipping into Germany, Australia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

AI Bubble Warning: Peter Schiff Sees Crisis Risk as Fed Flags $3 Trillion

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Coinpedia

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the AI bubble debate is getting harder to dismiss as the Federal Reserve highlights more than $3 trillion in potential financial commitments tied to the advanced-computing buildout.
  • It has been revealed that in a November 17 warning, Peter Schiff compared the artificial intelligence boom with the subprime mortgage market, arguing that easy monetary conditions have helped inflate asset valuations.
  • Housing market index: 25, lowest since 2012.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the AI bubble debate is getting harder to dismiss as the Federal Reserve highlights more than $3 trillion in potential financial commitments tied to the advanced-computing buildout. Peter Schiff believes the boom could end in a crisis worse than 2008. But the Fed’s findings reveal a more complicated risk beneath the technology rally.

It has been revealed that in a November 17 warning, Peter Schiff compared the artificial intelligence boom with the subprime mortgage market, arguing that easy monetary conditions have helped inflate asset valuations. His prediction is severe, but the financing figures now emerging from the Federal Reserve give investors a reason to examine the risks more closely.

Housing market index: 25, lowest since 2012. Nasdaq: down 12.25%. CoreWeave: down 64%. Bitcoin: down 33.5% from its 2026 high. Still think this is just about AI?Newly introduced Episode: https://t.co/DGp4OQqtu1https://t.co/DGp4OQqtu1.

The Federal Reserve’s November 13 Financial Stability Report demonstrates how rapidly financing for advanced computing has expanded.

Recent findings suggest that debt issuance linked to advanced computing infrastructure exceeded $680 billion by October 2026, roughly five times the $130 billion recorded in 2023. It also represented around 31% of nonfinancial investment-grade corporate debt issuance in 2026, compared with less than 6% three years earlier.

Outstanding public debt connected to advanced computing exceeded $1.1 trillion.

Those figures do not prove an AI bubble is about to burst. They do show how much capital is flowing into the infrastructure supporting the technology boom.

The more striking figure involves obligations beyond conventional borrowing.

Sources indicate that the Fed’s report describes more than $1 trillion in undiscounted values for leases that have not yet commenced. It also identifies more than $2 trillion in other obligations, including take-or-pay contracts and residual-value guarantees.

In a recent development, that distinction matters. These commitments should not be described as $3 trillion in outstanding loans or realized losses. They represent future financial obligations and guarantees that could become more difficult to manage if demand or expected returns disappoint.

Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr also discussed the potential scale of AI-related leases, contracts and guarantees in a November 16 speech, putting their maximum nominal value above $3 trillion.

Another concern is the growing financial connection between major technology companies and AI startups.

Large technology firms and chipmakers have invested heavily in AI labs and cloud-computing businesses. Some recipients then spend money on computing services or hardware supplied by those same investors.

That creates a complicated relationship between investment, customer demand and reported business growth. It does not automatically mean the revenue is artificial, but it raises questions about how sustainable demand would be if outside funding slowed.

Recent findings suggest that the Fed also highlights guarantees tied to data-center equipment and computing infrastructure. If hardware depreciates swiftly or demand falls short, the value supporting some financing arrangements could weaken.

Schiff’s warning deserves attention, but it should not be mistaken for a Federal Reserve forecast.

The Fed identifies vulnerabilities involving elevated valuations, complex financing and the possibility of a sharp correction in AI-related equities. Its report also notes that market contacts are concerned about circular financing and heavy reliance on debt.

However, the report does not declare that a crisis is inevitable. It also describes the broader financial system’s resilience, including capital and liquidity buffers at large banks.

For investors, the real question is whether future AI earnings can justify the enormous investment now being made in infrastructure.

A sharp reversal in AI valuations could extend beyond technology stocks. Companies, lenders and investors connected through financing arrangements could face pressure if expected returns weaken.

Industry observers note that that could also affect other risk assets if investors reduce exposure, sell leveraged positions or become more cautious about growth investments. Crypto markets could feel that pressure through broader risk aversion and leveraged liquidations, although the Fed’s findings do not establish that an AI downturn would cause a specific Bitcoin price decline.

According to recent reports, the AI bubble warning is worth taking seriously, but a crash is not a foregone conclusion. Investors should watch earnings, infrastructure spending, debt issuance and the ability of AI businesses to turn enormous capital commitments into sustainable cash flows. That’s a more useful test than simply betting on Peter Schiff’s prediction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little, but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.

Sources indicate that liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024, and electric power has proven to be effective – moving millions of tons of dirt while saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs. Now, the tech giant is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a latest, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.

Recent findings suggest that based on the proven R 9300 G8 platform, the new Liebherr R 9300 G8-E packs an 850 kW (~1,140 hp) electric drivetrain designed to IEC standards and supports 6-6.6 kV power supplies. The firm claims its electric setup offers customers the same hydraulic power and bucket capacity (1.8 tonnes/cubic meter, or ~1.5 short tons/cubic yard) as the diesel version.

All that electric power ships with advanced electronics and operator assistance systems designed to maximize both efficiency and safety while giving mine operators more data to work and blueprint with. Liebherr describes its take on ADAS thusly:.

It has been revealed that the R 9300 G8-E comes with Liebherr Power Efficiency – Hydraulic Control as standard, which adapts hydraulic power to suit the machine’s load profile, reducing overall engine load factor. Thanks to its Generation 8 electronic architecture, the R 9300 G8-E is compatible with a range of Liebherr’s IoMine technology products, including its range of excavator Assistance Systems, the semi-autonomous Bucket Filling Assistant, the Skyview vision system as well as the data visualisation tool, Data View. Customers also have the option of installing Liebherr’s autonomous cable reel solution onto the excavator to assist with cable management and support machine mobility on site.

Like its repowered cousins, the major electric excavator does seem to have on-board batteries, but is primarily driven and operated with grid power, reducing charging and re-charging concerns and enabling round-the-clock operations for as long as grid power holds.

According to recent reports, liebherr touts the benefits of latest R 9300 G8-E’s quiet, emissions-free running throughout its official announcement, but doesn’t stop there. The company states its EV, which makes do with thousands of fewer moving parts in its drivetrain, can also reduce maintenance requirements and associated operating costs in certain applications and site conditions while improving workplace conditions for the people who work in and around the machine.

Operating electric machinery inside mines must be mindblowingly good. Location is quite fixed, so you can just lay a HV cable to the grid with a spool at the vehicle end for local mobility. No noise, no vibration, no dirty emissions that have to be ventilated out for you not to die, instant torque, massive power and less maintenance on top?

The electric drivetrain also reduces vibration inside the cab, improving operator comfort, limiting fatigue, and potentially contributing to a safer working environment.

Recent findings suggest that for the better part of this year, Zcash (ZEC) gained notable traction, which enabled it to rise from a low of $188 (witnessed on Feb.6) to a massive multi-year high of $1,684 (recorded on Sept.26). Linking further possibilities, capital market analyst Matt Hougan highlighted a connection between Bitcoin and the privacy-focused cryptocurrency. In a podcast aired Sunday, the Bitwise CIO (chief investment officer) outlined a possible case for rotating Bitcoin capital into Zcash.

In the interview, Hougan revealed that privacy is the latest notable component in on-chain finance. According to him, this element is becoming increasingly crucial, particularly in the crypto landscape where data can be visible on-chain.

As traditional assets move on-chain, institutional investors may miss the element of confidentiality in the DeFi world, he narrated. He said this pursuit may prompt institutions to adopt privacy-focused crypto solutions like Zcash, Monero, and others.

Talk of a potential Bitcoin-to-Zcash rotation picked up momentum this week from the Bitwise executive, sparking further excitement in the already optimistic crypto narrative. The basis of this call is that as institutions continue moving RWAs onchain, they will require privacy-preserving DeFi protocols to protect user data. That’s where Zcash comes into the spotlight.

Hougan anticipates that as OG crypto holders diversify from older crypto assets into privacy solutions, institutional investors, especially Bitcoin whales, will join the wave. He, however, foresees a selective rotation rather than a complete institutional surrender.

Hougan’s optimistic views signal significant market shifts. His comments show that as institutional capital enters the on-chain space, the complete transparency of public blockchains may pose a major obstacle for serious players.

The well-known analyst highlighted the importance of confidential mechanisms, specifically Zcash.

Sources indicate that the Bitcoin-to-Zcash rotation narrative appears to be on the horizon. Recently, several early Bitcoin whales urged early Bitcoin investor Dan Held to buy Zcash months before ZEC topped $1,000 in September. Also, earlier last month, recognized Bitcoin whales, the Winklevoss brothers, pointed out their radical shift to Zcash.

Sources indicate that another day, another security scare. This time, Etherscan is warning users after detecting unauthorized access attempts against its customer support system that might have been hacked. But the timing could hardly be worse for an industry already dealing with a growing list of cyberattacks.

The warning comes just days after hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely, injecting malicious code into websites operated by 178 organizations. The affected names included HSBC, BBC, Ledger, IKEA, Salesforce, Zoom, and CNN.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, crypto platforms have faced separate attacks involving compromised API keys, protocol vulnerabilities, and stolen customer information. Traditional banking has not escaped either, with a French bank recently losing approximately €100 million to hackers.

So what kind of security era are we entering? The problem is no longer confined to crypto exchanges or experimental DeFi protocols. Banks, technology companies, payment providers and blockchain businesses are increasingly exposed to the same interconnected digital infrastructure.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

Etherscan disclosed just a few minutes ago that attackers had attempted to gain unauthorized access to its Freshworks customer support and ticketing system. The firm is investigating and has introduced precautionary measures. It has not confirmed that customer records were successfully accessed, but warned customers about suspicious support communications, unexpected links, and requests for sensitive information.

Security Notice: Reminder Regarding Etherscan Support CommunicationsEarlier today, we detected attempts to gain unauthorized access to our customer support and ticketing system (Freshworks).We are at the moment investigating the situation and taking precautionary measures.In….

The concern is particularly relevant because support impersonation remains an effective way to steal crypto and your money. An attacker posing as an Etherscan representative could exploit a user’s existing support request to make a phishing message appear legitimate.

It has been revealed that but Etherscan is hardly the only name facing security questions this week. Just two days ago, hackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s Web Experimentation signup process. They injected malicious JavaScript into customer projects, allowing the code to run on websites using the affected software.

Sources indicate that optimizely confirmed the vulnerability and noted it had removed the injected code and fixed the flaw. Its November 17 incident report said the unauthorized party exploited the signup process rather than stealing customer administrator passwords.

The financial damage remains unclear. It is reported that investigators could not establish how many visitors were affected or whether the attempted thefts succeeded.

The uncomfortable takeaway is that attackers did not need to breach 178 separate companies. They exploited one software provider whose code was embedded across hundreds of websites.

Crypto’s security problems extend beyond Etherscan and the Optimizely incident. DeFiLlama’s hack tracker recorded several attacks during the week, including a $10.39 million incident involving Lighter Perps on November 16. The attacker exploited a compromised trader API key, enabling unauthorized withdrawals.

Lighter said its protocol and smart contracts were not compromised. It temporarily suspended withdrawals and activated Guardian mode to prevent further unauthorized activity.

Another incident hit MORE Markets, where an attacker exploited a lending mechanism to drain approximately $308,000 in WFLOW. B18 TimeBank also suffered an exploit on November 17, losing $404,540 in USDC through its reward voucher redemption mechanism.

Sources indicate that these incidents show different weaknesses across crypto infrastructure. Not every loss comes from a broken smart contract. Compromised credentials, vulnerable applications and flawed authorization mechanisms can be equally damaging.

In a recent development, traditional finance faces its own problems. French lender Crédit Mutuel Arkéa disclosed a cyber heist earlier in November, with hackers stealing approximately €100 million through fraudulent transactions originating from the bank’s own accounts. The bank noted customer assets were not affected, although some transactions were temporarily suspended.

Deutsche Bank also made headlines on November 17 after confidential internal documents surfaced through an international journalistic investigation. It was a document leak, not a confirmed breach of its current banking systems.

Deutsche Bank said security testing found no indication that its current IT environment, account information, login credentials, or payment data had been compromised. Yet, it has greater effects to geopolitics.

Industry observers note that germany’s BIGGEST bank just had its secrets leaked.15 MILLION files. Epstein. Trump. Russia. Colombia. Nearly $600 MILLION in suspicious payments.And almost NOBODY is talking about it…Deutsche Bank states the matters “date back many years and in some cases as much as two….

Banking institutions are not immune to major security incidents simply because they operate under traditional financial regulations.

Sources indicate that crypto has suffered enormous losses. The October Binance incident alone involved $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, making it one of the largest cryptocurrency heists on record. Yet, traditional finance also faces attacks involving payment infrastructure, third-party service providers, and internal transaction systems.

According to recent reports, the Optimizely incident is particularly revealing. Both HSBC and Ledger appeared among the affected organizations. The vulnerability did not care whether visitors were interacting with a traditional financial institution or a crypto manufacturer.

Sources indicate that neither system offers complete protection. The real question is whether companies can secure the increasingly complex infrastructure connecting their services. A single compromised vendor can expose hundreds of organizations, while one stolen credential can bypass otherwise sophisticated security systems.

Crypto users have every reason to demand stronger protections. But traditional banking customers should not mistake regulation and familiar branding for immunity.

With Etherscan possibly being hacked, the data provider is now joining the growing list of companies investigating security incidents.

The Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth has suffered substantial losses on its XRP ventures amid the persistent volatility facing the broad crypto market since the third quarter of 2026.

The firm has reported a massive write-down of its XRP holdings for Q3 2026 in a recent filing with the U.S. SEC, drawing attention from the broader crypto community.

On Tuesday, November 17, Evernorth reported a substantial decline in the value of its XRP holdings after the firm wrote down over $505 million in its latest financial filing with the SEC.

Notably, Evernorth issued a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, disclosing that it holds around 346 million XRP, now valued at about $342 million.

This has drawn attention across the XRP community and sparked discussions about the growing impact of persistent volatility on investors’ funds, as Evernorth’s XRP report marks a sharp drop from its initial valuation of $847 million.

Apparently, the firm reported that the tokens are now valued at about 40 cents per dollar of their initial worth. This means that the leading XRP treasury firm has reduced the value of its XRP holdings by nearly 60%.

Industry observers note that it is crucial to note that the massive drop in the value of Evernorth’s XRP holdings does not mean that the firm has sold off its XRP. Rather, it marks a write-down in its previously listed XRP value.

The move may have been influenced by the persistent market drawdown, especially after XRP lost support at the key $1 level, closing steadily around $0.90 over the past few days.

Furthermore, Evernorth has specified that it has no intention of reversing the write-downs, even if the price of XRP later recovers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lucid has released a latest teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.
  • Recent findings suggest that the clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings.
  • Recent findings suggest that lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video on X yesterday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lucid has released a latest teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.

Recent findings suggest that the clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.

Recent findings suggest that lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video on X yesterday. The caption talks about “elevating the experience of movement” and says Lucid can’t wait “to share this feeling with even more people.” It doesn’t name the vehicle, but “even more people” is about as subtle a hint at a cheaper model as you can get.

Industry observers note that two frames from the film show the vehicle at dusk. At the rear, “LUCID” is spelled out in red illuminated letters across the tailgate, flanked by thin red light strips, with a spoiler cutting across the base of the rear glass. Up front, a sculpted LED headlight with a row of vertical segments sweeps across a red body panel.

According to recent reports, that rear end matches the Cosmos design Lucid registered with the EU Intellectual Property Office in May, which demonstrated the same spelled-out “LUCID” tailgate and rear-glass spoiler. It also lines up with the thin red light strips on the camouflaged Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101 in California last month.

In a recent development, lucid unveiled its plans for Cosmos and Earth at its first Investor Day in March. Both ride on the newly introduced midsize platform and start under $50,000, roughly half the price of the Gravity.

On paper, the Cosmos is impressive. Lucid claims about 300 miles of range from a 69 kWh pack, thanks to efficiency of up to 4.5 mi/kWh, which it indicates is 10% better than its closest competitor. It also claims 200 miles of range in 14 minutes of charging, and its upcoming Atlas drive unit has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the Zeus unit in the Gravity.

Sources indicate that the problem is timing. Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, CEO Silvio Napoli pushed the Cosmos to 2027, “most likely the second half.”.

That puts it on the same schedule as Rivian’s $45,000 base R2, and well after the Tesla Model Y it was caught testing next to in Arizona back in May.

Industry observers note that lucid needs this car badly. It delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while building only 2,954 after cutting the second shift at its Arizona factory.

I want Lucid to succeed. Period. I love the Air Pure and would like to get one at some point, but the cost is out of my budget while the tech is more than I want or need.

But I think what impresses me more than anything with Lucid is that they are one of the few who actually speak efficiency. It seems that they actually care about being efficient where companies like GM and others just build vehicles with bigger batteries in order to get more range. So for that, I give Lucid much credit.

Industry observers note that the company is building hype a year out. It has nothing else newly introduced to sell until the Cosmos arrives, and the company reports Q3 earnings on Monday. They need to remind everyone what they are working toward.

In a recent development, A midsize SUV doing 4.5 mi/kWh would be best in class by a wide margin, and Lucid’s efficiency claims have held up on the Air. If it really lands under $50,000 with 300 miles of range, it’s a very compelling alternative to the Model Y and the R2, which still have room to take over market shares from ICE vehicles.

But Lucid has already slipped this car once; it claims its cash lasts “well into 2027,” and the Cosmos is due in the second half of 2027. That’s a tight overlap. I think the Cosmos will be a good car, but can Lucid fund it all the way to customers’ driveways?

Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (755 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek
