📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim.
  • The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.

The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.

Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:.

Sources indicate that the Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.

According to recent reports, this is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August, when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.

Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.

For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.

The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.

Tesla also tried the opposite approach earlier this year. It offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 in February for “only the next 10 days,” then pulled it. A single-motor RWD version was discontinued after just 173 sales. None of it moved the needle.

The Cybertruck isn’t sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets, and Tesla canceled it for Australia and Latest Zealand last month.

So, Tesla has now discontinued more models than it at the moment offers. Looks like the great leader isn’t particularly good at writing product specs. And the hype has been over for quite a while anyway. In Europe, owning a Tesla has actually become something of an image liability.

Recent findings suggest that this is what a wind-down looks like. Tesla isn’t trying to sell more Cybertrucks anymore. It’s trying to make as much money as possible on the last ones, with the hope that announcing the end of production will encourage some people to secure their order.

In a recent development, once you’ve decided to end a program, volume stops mattering. You have a set number of build slots left, a parts supply you want to burn down, and probably a small group of fans who’ll want one before it’s gone. Pausing the cheapest trim and charging $7,500 more for the rest is the obvious play. You push everyone into higher-margin configurations and stop pretending the base truck is a real product.

But it does say a lot about the last two years of Cybertruck pricing. Tesla went from a $59,990 “limited-time” offer in February to a $92,490 entry price in November. That’s a tech giant that never figured out who the truck was for.

A Bitcoin address that had not moved coins since February 2011 transferred 75 BTC on Nov. 17, according to Galaxy Research. At the current price of $64,935 per BTC, the coins are worth around $4.87 million.

The address is listed as a defendant in a $250 billion lawsuit in Latest York Supreme Court, in which the plaintiffs are trying to have early Bitcoin wallets declared "lost." Galaxy Research mentioned that several other addresses from the same list have also moved coins in 2026.

According to recent reports, according to Galaxy Research analysts, early on Nov. 17, in block 976,209, the address 1ALpEWtXApR19hLXvcG8NfkPyGsUMhFPMS sent coins for the first time. It was first funded on Feb. 8, 2011. At that time, Bitcoin was trading at about $0.90. After 15.8 years, the coins went to an unknown address with a 399-satoshi fee, or about 26 cents, for a paper gain of more than 7,000,000%.

According to recent reports, onchain databases list the wallet as Noah Doe #3409 (Salomon Client Dusted). That label is how it ended up among the defendants in the high-profile case ABC Company, XYZ Company, and Noah Doe v. John Does 1–39,069.

Industry observers note that according to the lawsuit, an anonymous plaintiff using the pseudonym Noah Doe and two companies want the rights to 39,069 Bitcoin wallets that have not moved coins for more than five years. The plaintiffs said that these wallets hold about 3.8 million BTC, and at the current price, the coins are worth around $250 billion.

The plaintiffs filed the lawsuit under Upcoming York's lost-and-found law, Article 7-B of the Personal Property Law. Under the law, a person who finds lost property has to give it to the police, and the property goes to the finder if the owner does not claim it in time. In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs valued each address at less than $10, and they argued that the waiting period for such items was one year.

They "found" dormant addresses with an algorithm, saved them onto USB flash drives and took them to the Upcoming York Police Department (NYPD). Then they served the owners on the blockchain, through microtransactions with embedded messages (OP_RETURN). The practice is known as "dusting," and the campaign is tied to Salomon Brothers Strategic Advisors. Once the waiting period ran out, the plaintiffs asked the court to recognize the coins as theirs.

The case has been put on hold several times over motions to dismiss and amicus curiae briefs from outside experts. At a hearing on Sept. 8, the Bitcoin Policy Institute asked to intervene as a defendant, and The Digital Chamber asked to join the case as amicus curiae. Galaxy Research described it as a case "in which anonymous plaintiffs are seeking to claim legal title over Satoshi's coins.".

Galaxy Research's Will Owens, who attended the hearing, said that The Digital Chamber's arguments were "well pleaded" and that "the judge sounded sympathetic to them.".

Sources indicate that critics of the lawsuit argue that Article 7-B was written for things you can pick up and hand over for safekeeping. It wasn't written for blockchain records when the "finder" doesn't hold the private keys.

In September, Galaxy head of research Alex Thorn also noted that the Lost and Found Property Law includes "protection from 'Noah Doe-style' dormancy attacks on legal ownership.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A US judge acquitted two brothers accused of causing $25 million in losses to Ethereum trading bots.
  • The Ultrasound relay released transaction data without checking two zeroed block-header fields.
  • Prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentation required for wire fraud.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A US judge acquitted two brothers accused of causing $25 million in losses to Ethereum trading bots.

The Ultrasound relay released transaction data without checking two zeroed block-header fields.

Prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentation required for wire fraud.

The Ethereum MEV exploit case has ended in acquittal after a US federal judge cleared two brothers accused of causing approximately $25 million in losses to automated trading bots. The deciding detail? The relay released transaction data without checking two critical fields in a block header.

US District Judge Jessica Clarke acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno on November 16, 2026, ruling that prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentation required for wire fraud. The decision closes the government’s first criminal prosecution centred on an Ethereum MEV exploit.

The alleged operation took place in April 2023. Prosecutors noted the brothers used eight bait transactions to attract sandwich-trading bots, which profit by placing trades around other users’ orders.

It has been revealed that when their validator received a proposed block through the Ultrasound relay, it signed a block header with two critical fields set to zero. Those values described a block that couldn’t be valid.

But the relay didn’t check them. It released the block’s transaction contents anyway, allowing the brothers to construct a different block and replace the bait transactions with trades that worked against the bots.

The operation caused approximately $25 million in bot losses in around 12 seconds.

🚨 BREAKING: U.S. JUDGE ACQUITS TWO BROTHERS IN $25 MILLION ETHEREUM EXPLOIT CASEA major legal development in the cryptocurrency industry.A U.S. federal judge has acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, two MIT-educated brothers accused of extracting approximately $25… pic.twitter.com/LYZipaQP1r.

Sources indicate that the judge found that prosecutors hadn’t shown the disputed fields influenced the relay’s decision. Without that connection, the alleged false information couldn’t establish the material misrepresentation required for the wire fraud case.

In a recent development, clarke also rejected the argument that bait transactions promised bots a particular execution order. Ethereum‘s public mempool doesn’t guarantee that pending transactions will be included or executed in a specific sequence.

It has been revealed that the brothers were indicted in May 2024. Their first trial ended in a mistrial in November 2025 after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict.

The November 16 acquittal covered wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Recent findings suggest that it doesn’t make every MEV strategy or exploit legal. But this Ethereum MEV exploit ruling draws a clear distinction between questionable trading conduct and the specific deception prosecutors must prove in a criminal fraud case.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple-backed XRP treasury manufacturer Evernorth Holdings has disclosed a significant decrease in the book value of its crypto asset holdings, with total impairment charges amounting to around $505 million before going public on Nasdaq.

Recent findings suggest that per an SEC filing on Nov. 13, the 346.3 million XRP tokens that Evernorth Holdings owned had a book value of just $341.9 million as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This is compared to the firm's initial accounting of the crypto assets at roughly $846.6 million, with an average acquisition or contribution price of $2.44 per XRP. This represents a nearly 60% decline in book value.

In a recent development, as per the latest filing, Evernorth recorded around $271 million in XRP impairment charges in the first nine months of 2026. This is in addition to the $233.7 million in impairment charges recorded in 2025.

Interestingly, only $6.9 million of the recent impairment charges occurred in the third quarter.

This also explains why Evernorth's XRP assets had a book value so far below their market value at the end of September.

Recent findings suggest that evernorth calculates impairments based on the lowest observable intraday price of XRP for each batch of tokens acquired. Once the assets are written down, the company is unable to reverse the previous losses if the price rises.

For reference, on Sept. 30, XRP closed the day trading at around $1.49 on Coinbase. At that price, Evernorth's 346.3 million XRP tokens would have been worth roughly $516 million, much higher than the disclosed book value of $341.9 million.

The recent disclosure comes around a month after Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9. It started trading on Nasdaq under the symbol XRPN on Oct. 12.

Following the business combination, Evernorth held around 473 million XRP tokens and had also raised gross cash proceeds of around $300 million.

Its investors include Ripple, SBI Group, Arrington Capital, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

According to recent reports, on Oct. 14, Evernorth confirmed collaborations with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo to implement institutional investment strategies starting in Q4 2026.

Meanwhile, its latest SEC filing did not include details on the amount of XRP deployed to generate yield or the returns generated from it.

Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in 10 minutes.

BMW’s newly introduced iX3 checks all the boxes. Based on BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive 800V system, the 2027 iX3 50 xDrive delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles (with 20″ summer tires).

Industry observers note that with the 22″ summer tires, the iX3 50 xDrive has an EPA-estimated range of up to 392 miles. Still, plenty for at least a week of commuting.

It can also add 170-185 miles of range in 10 minutes with up to 400 kW DC fast charging. In everyday, real-world driving, it may drive even further than its official EPA numbers suggest.

During Edmunds‘ EV Range test, the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive (with 22″ summer tires) drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles.

In a recent development, the electric SUV was also more efficient than advertised. The iX3 achieved an energy consumption of 28.3 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles by roughly 11.6%.

BMW’s newly introduced iX3 is now the longest-range luxury electric SUV that Edmunds has tested, outperforming rivals including the 2027 Volvo EX60 (352 miles) and Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric (392 miles).

The Edmunds real-world range test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions.

It consists of 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

The 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive is available to order in Sport, M Sport, and M Sport Professional trims, priced from $61,500, $64,000, and $65,500, respectively.

According to recent reports, average speed of 40 mph in perfect weather is an absolute best case scenario for EVs. I think cold weather 70 mph would be the worst case and it should be tested.

That said, I think BMW and Mercedes tend to underrate their cars published range (I think they publish worst case condition range). BMW iX and Mercedes have historically outperformed EPA ratings according to various articles and reddits posts.

But I think regardless of what we think of Edmunds tests, these are some crazy range figures and with roughly 100kwh usable battery capacity, you are still looking at close to 4 miles per kwh. As an example across the Ultium platform anything from Chevy or Cadillac barely breaches 300 miles. The big Escalade and pickup trucks have 225+ kwh battery so I am not counting them.

If the depreciation rate for luxury EVs holds up, in 2-3 years, they will be awesome value.

Powered by a 108.7 kWh battery, the new iX3 with 20″ Summer Tires delivers up to 434 miles of range on a single charge.

With a charging rate of up to 400 kW, the new BMW iX3 can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 21 minutes, or add about 185 miles in 10 minutes.

Home » Cryptopedia » 5 Tokens That Held Up Post-TGE.

While most crypto tokens struggle to maintain their launch valuations, these five projects have demonstrated varying degrees of post-TGE price resilience.

For almost all crypto tokens, the Token Generation Event (TGE) is the best day they will ever have.

Industry observers note that for 2026, so far only about 28% of tokens introduced remained above their TGE closing price after 60 days. The median token was trading at just 0.64x its launch close.

Tokens surviving and rising in price for days, hours, and even minutes post-launch is not an easy feat. Here are five tokens that have so far avoided the typical post-TGE collapse:.

Today, $1WIN is trading around $0.045, roughly 50% above its public sale price.

Industry observers note that it is too early to compare that performance with tokens that have been trading for months or years. What makes $1WIN worth paying attention to is that its held steady in the post-TGE price rise and has a substantial business behind it. 1win has operated since 2016 with 100 million players and its gaming business is profitable independently of the token.

It has been revealed that the organization also intends revenue-funded open-market buybacks, while 10% of $1WIN spent through supported products will be burned. Supply is capped at one billion tokens with no additional minting.

Hyperliquid’s HYPE remains one of the clearest examples of a token that did considerably more than survive launch.

HYPE began trading in 2024 and today is hitting over $73, leaving it several multiples above its earliest market prices nearly two years later.

The underlying exchange also gives the token an economic connection to platform activity. Trading fees flow into Hyperliquid’s Assistance Fund, which acquires HYPE, with accumulated tokens subsequently burned.

That combination of product usage, revenue and token demand makes HYPE one of the stronger examples of the kind of pre-TGE traction highlighted in Decasonic’s research.

Aster rolled out ASTER in September 2025 as the token behind its decentralized spot and perpetuals trading platform.

Sources indicate that despite substantial volatility since then, ASTER was trading around $0.65. It remains well below its $2.42 all-time high, but also far above its earliest trading levels.

ASTER has not gone up in a straight line. But more than a year after launch, the token has retained a substantial part of the value created during its early growth rather than fading toward zero after TGE.

Backpack’s BP demonstrates another type of post-TGE resilience.

Sources indicate that the token released in March and subsequently fell as low as roughly $0.12 in May. By this month, BP had recovered to around $0.90, after reaching an all-time high of $1.66 in October.

That makes BP interesting because its strength did not come immediately after TGE. The token went through a deep early correction before rebuilding.

It also sits inside an established exchange and wallet ecosystem, with utility including trading-fee discounts, rewards, staking and access to other Backpack products.

ZAMA is trading around $0.067, approximately one-third above that public auction price.

The token also has direct utility within the Zama Protocol, where it is used to pay for encryption and decryption services and reward operators and stakers securing the network.

Stronger 2026 debuts generally arrived with real usage, paying people, revenue, TVL or another measurable source of pre-TGE traction. The token was being added to something that already worked.

Industry observers note that hyperliquid had trading volume and fees. Backpack had its exchange and wallet. Zama had working privacy infrastructure. Aster had an operating trading platform. 1win entered TGE with a gaming business with 100 million players and has been operating since 2016.

Industry observers note that A strong launch can be created by hype. Holding up once the launch is over usually requires much more.

Sources indicate that bank of America has disclosed a position in an XRP exchange-traded fund in its latest quarterly 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing, dated Nov. 16, highlights that the bank held 13,260 shares of the futures-based Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI), worth about $106,600, at the end of the third quarter.

Bank of America held 13,000 shares of the fund in the first quarter and 13,260 shares in the second quarter, according to its earlier 13F filings. The same filing lists more than $685 million in BlackRock's IBIT, $13.58 million in Bitwise and $950,000 in VanEck.

Seven major banks disclosed XRP fund holdings worth a total of $29.4 million in filings published between Nov. 9 and Nov. 16. Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed the largest stake among them, at $27.21 million. The bank held 712,319 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF, worth about $20.52 million, and it also opened a new position of 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF, worth about $6.7 million.

UBS and Morgan Stanley disclosed XRP fund holdings of $1.91 million and $116,000, respectively. Most of the UBS position was in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF, and Morgan Stanley held funds from Franklin, REX-Osprey and Bitwise.

JPMorgan Chase held 539 shares of the Bitwise fund, worth about $9,000, and National Bank of Canada held 330 shares of the same fund, worth about $5,500. Bank of Montreal held REX-Osprey and ProShares Ultra XRP shares worth $4,300.

The crypto portfolio of Goldman Sachs grew to $2.64 billion by the end of September, according to its 13F filing. The bank held about $1.28 billion in Bitcoin ETFs, and BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC accounted for $778 million and $398 million of that amount, respectively. Goldman also held about $1.22 billion in Ether funds, and BlackRock's ETHA accounted for $603 million of that amount.

Recent findings suggest that goldman held $144 million in XRP ETFs at the end of the third quarter, up from $87 million at the end of the second quarter. The bank's 13F filing for the first quarter showed no XRP or Solana ETF holdings, and Goldman still held no Solana funds at the end of September.

The bank held shares of five spot XRP funds from Franklin Templeton, Bitwise, Canary, Grayscale and 21Shares, and its Franklin Templeton position was worth almost $48 million.

It has been revealed that besides, trading firm Jane Street reported $23.5 million in XRP funds, and Simplex Trading disclosed a $14 million stake in the Grayscale fund. EP Wealth Advisors raised its Volatility Shares XRP ETF holding by 37% to 18,400 shares, worth about $148,000.

A 13F filing only reveals long positions as of Sept. 30. It doesn't show whether the banks hedge those holdings with shorts, or what they did with the shares in October and November. Since then, XRP has fallen below $1, and on Tuesday morning, XRP was trading at $0.966.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the XRP rich list indicates that smaller holders continued accumulating XRP even as the price dropped below $1. Wallets holding between 10,000 and 100,000 XRP added around 504 million coins over the past year as per XRPScan data.

The number of wallets holding at least 10,000 XRP reached 343,897 on November 14, 2026, up around 5% since February, based on Santiment data.

It has been revealed that however, the total XRP held by these wallets remained almost unchanged at 65.5 billion. This suggests that some existing holders may have spread their coins across multiple wallets rather than making fresh purchases.

The growth in the XRP rich list is mainly coming from wallets holding between 10,000 and 100,000 XRP.

This group added nearly 25,000 accounts over the past year. Its total holdings also increased by around 504 million XRP. During the November price decline, these wallets added another 39 million XRP.

The trend is different among holders with 100,000 to 1 million XRP. Their wallet count declined slightly from 30,500 in November 2025 to 30,300 on November 14, 2026.

This indicates that smaller holders are adding XRP, while the mid-sized holder group has remained largely unchanged.

Also Read : Ripple (XRP) Price Prediction 2026, 2027-2030.

Between November 6 and November 12, around 440 million XRP moved into three newly introduced or nearly empty wallets.

It has been revealed that none of the receiving wallets had an exchange label on XRPScan. However, their owners remain unknown.

Recent findings suggest that the transfers could represent existing holders moving their coins, a custodian managing assets for clients or a fund reorganizing its holdings. Therefore, the movement does not confirm fresh buying.

Exchange and firm wallets account for a large share of the XRP rich list.

According to analyst cheeky crypto, at least half of the XRP held in wallets containing 10,000 coins or more belongs to accounts labeled as exchanges, companies or known individuals. Exchanges and companies alone account for more than 40%.

The concentration is higher among the largest wallets holding at least 100 million XRP, where around 84% of the coins are linked to exchanges and insiders, including Upbit, Coinbase, Binance and Ripple.

By comparison, only around 5% of the holdings in the 100,000 to 1 million XRP category are linked to labeled entities.

Sources indicate that this difference is notable because exchange wallets can hold XRP for many customers. Their balances do not necessarily represent the investments of individual whales.

Between November 4 and November 15, labeled exchange and company wallets outside Ripple added approximately 18 million XRP to their combined holdings.

During the same period, Binance-labeled wallets decreased by around 126 million XRP, while Upbit and Coinbase each added approximately 50 million XRP.

The figures suggest that coins moved between exchanges rather than showing a major overall increase in exchange holdings.

Previous market declines show that XRP has recovered after periods of increasing wallet numbers, but the trend does not guarantee a price rise.

During the April 2025 sell-off, XRP gained around 30% within 30 days of reaching its low while the number of wallets holding at least 10,000 XRP continued to increase.

According to recent reports, A similar pattern occurred in August 2026. XRP recovered approximately 29% in the month after reaching a low of around $0.99 on August 16.

However, the token later lost those gains and declined further.

In November 2024, XRP gained around 174% in a month even though the 10,000 XRP wallet count remained relatively flat.

These examples show that changes in wallet numbers alone cannot explain or predict XRP price movements.

The analysis identifies three indicators for tracking the next change in holder activity:.

For now, the XRP rich list points to continued accumulation among smaller holders, while mid-sized wallet activity remains flat. The 440 million XRP transfer into fresh wallets adds another development to watch, but it does not establish whether new investors are entering the market.

The 2027 i7 also incorporates elements and tech from BMW’s Neue Klasse platform, with up to 362 miles of range.

Meanwhile, the 2027 i5, which still offers up to 310 miles of range, is not built on the dedicated Neue Klasse platform.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz said that the odds of Bitcoin hitting $90,000 by the end of 2026 are slim in light of prevailing macroeconomic headwinds and the growing likelihood that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates.

During a live event with Anthony Scaramucci at the Digital Assets Forum in Fresh York City, Novogratz was asked if Bitcoin could get back to $90,000 by the end of this year.

"Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," Novogratz said.

Industry observers note that his gloomy outlook comes as Bitcoin has struggled to rebound after a devastating drop that saw its price dip as low as $62,000 over the weekend. Bitcoin's price stood at around $64,600 on Nov. 17. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization has declined for six consecutive weeks.

Sources indicate that A shift in the U.S. monetary policy outlook, namely the prospect of more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, has been largely to blame for Bitcoin's decline, according to Novogratz.

"At the start of the year, everybody thought the Fed was going to be cutting now," he stated.

But high inflation and ongoing supply shocks have forced investors to readjust their expectations.

According to recent reports, "Inflation's going up. We've got inflation going up," Novogratz stated, warning that inflationary pressures could become increasingly entrenched.

"The Fed's going to hike. At least two more, probably three more," he said.

Novogratz predicted that the Fed would raise rates by 25 basis points in December and then hike again at its next meeting.

Industry observers note that he remarked that higher rates, at least in the near term, tend to weigh on Bitcoin. But the higher cost of government borrowing could eventually provide support for the cryptocurrency.

"Yeah, later," he noted in response to the suggestion that higher borrowing costs could be a tailwind for Bitcoin.

"First, you're gonna hike rates. Oh, sell gold, right? You're going to go to the dollar. It's so ingrained in peoples' heads," he said.

Sources indicate that "Carry costs going up," he noted. Bitcoin doesn't offer the same yield as interest-bearing dollar assets.

"You don't make any interest on Bitcoin in dollars," he said.

In particular, Novogratz noted that the massive rise in Treasury yields has been particularly detrimental to the crypto market.

"Literally 40 basis points in like four days of trading. So that's why crypto's down," he mentioned.

He also said that the massive crypto hack could still be weighing on investors' minds, adding to market jitters.

"I think in the back of their minds is the hack," he said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that stablecoins started as a way to hold dollars on-chain.
  • Tokenized stocks are heading down the same route now, and the resemblance is uncanny.
  • What’s worth noting here is how much of it is actually being used.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that stablecoins started as a way to hold dollars on-chain. Then people started lending, trading, and earning with them. In time, DeFi grew up around them.

Tokenized stocks are heading down the same route now, and the resemblance is uncanny.

What’s worth noting here is how much of it is actually being used.

In a recent development, according to data from Token Terminal, tokenized stocks deposited into DeFi are now worth about $300 million. A year ago, that was at approx. $12.5 million.

This number didn’t move at all through late 2025. Things picked up in the spring, blasted through $100 million by around August, and then shot past a quarter million in September.

Sources indicate that it’s also a bigger share of the market now. That $300 million is 6.3% of the $4.8 billion tokenized stock market cap. Last year, only 2.4% was being put to work.

So, why move stocks into DeFi at all?

Because once they’re there, holders can borrow against them, earn fees by providing liquidity, or chase yield.

And every latest way to use them, is essentially one more reason not to cash out.

It has been revealed that tokenized stocks now have a market cap of about $4.8 billion. Stablecoins crossed that exact number in March 2020. Since then, stablecoins have grown, 59 times over! The number is at $285 billion now.

It has been revealed that tokenized stocks are moving fast too. They were worth only a few tens of millions in early 2025.

Sources indicate that but why? A blockchain is basically a ledger for assets, and it gets more useful when it holds things people really want. U.S Stocks are about as in-demand as it gets.

Stablecoins didn’t get to where they are without the effort.

They made it through the COVID crash, the Terra collapse, FTX, and the USDC de-peg after SVB failed. Market cap fell by 28% between February 2022 and October 2023, then spiked up to a high by September 2024.

According to recent reports, what kept them going though? Cash and T-bill reserves backed every token, plus people who actually wanted to use them.

Tokenized stocks follow the same 1:1 idea.

Sources indicate that except the risk factor is higher. So is the potential for gains.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Stellar Floats XLM Rewards Pool After 1,000% Payments Jump.

Stellar is exploring an XLM rewards pool funded by network fees as monthly payment volume rises tenfold.

Recent findings suggest that stellar is considering a proposal to reward XLM holders who lock tokens and contribute utility to the network. Crypto market commentator All In Crypto highlights the idea in a video reviewing Stellar’s third-quarter webinar, asking whether rising network activity can translate into stronger demand for XLM.

The proposal would put network-generated fees into an XLM rewards pool. But Dixon, speaking during the webinar, stresses that it remains an early concept open to feedback, not an approved change or a promised payout.

“I’m not sure this is the right proposal,” she says, urging participants to read the accompanying paper and explore its interactive dashboard before commenting. Her central argument is that “utility should drive XLM.”.

According to recent reports, the webinar reports that monthly payment volume on Stellar rose from roughly $1.8 billion in January to $18.5 billion in October. October’s figure was 89% higher than September’s, following eight consecutive months of growth.

Sources indicate that another $7.5 billion reportedly moved during November’s first 10 days. Those figures describe money moving across the network, however, not purchases of XLM or returns accruing to token holders.

According to recent reports, all In Crypto is openly bullish but acknowledges uncertainty over the token’s future value. That distinction matters: greater use of Stellar’s infrastructure does not, by itself, establish how much additional XLM customers need to hold.

The webinar also describes a U.S. Bank pilot in which the bank issued a dollar-backed stablecoin called USBDC and used it to settle a cross-border payment between its North American and European entities. According to the presentation, minting, redemption, freezing and claw-back controls operated at the protocol level, without custom contract logic.

Stellar’s Project Throughput offers another glimpse of its ambitions. The webinar cites early benchmarks of roughly 1.2 million payments per second on one machine and about seven million across eight machines.

Sources indicate that those are technology-preview results, not reported production-network throughput. The project is available on Futurenet with open-source code for developers to test.

Now, the unresolved question is less whether Stellar can process more activity than how that activity benefits XLM.

The rewards proposal could create another connection between network use and token ownership, but its design, eligibility requirements and eventual adoption remain unsettled.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Charles Hoskinson made sure to clear up misunderstandings about whether he thought the work on Cardano was done.
  • "I never once said Cardano is finished," Hoskinson said in a Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson, there is plenty more to come for Cardano, as the blockchain's privacy-preserving sister chain, Midnight, reaches a huge milestone as its ecosystem continues to expand.

Charles Hoskinson made sure to clear up misunderstandings about whether he thought the work on Cardano was done.

"I never once said Cardano is finished," Hoskinson said in a Nov. 15 post on X.

The comments came after he talked about the completion of Cardano's original roadmap, which raised some questions about his role in the blockchain's future.

He also called out the CEO of the Cardano Foundation, Frederik Gregaard, for not mentioning the Midnight chain when discussing everything the network has accomplished.

Industry observers note that in his latest video, uploaded on Nov. 17, Hoskinson celebrated the fact that Midnight had just brought on board its first UK-based banking partner, Monument Bank.

Monument Bank is the first UK bank to offer interest-bearing tokenized retail deposits on a public blockchain, according to an announcement from the Midnight Foundation.

Up to £250 million in customer deposits will be added to Midnight in the first phase, and each tokenized deposit will be backed 1:1 by sterling cash held at the bank.

Monument Bank customers can now earn a fixed 5.2% annual equivalent rate on deposits for 12 months, all without having to deal with cryptocurrencies directly.

Hoskinson was very excited about the scale of the initiative, comparing the planned amount of deposits with the current decentralized finance ecosystem on Cardano.

"It's five times the TVL of Cardano," he mentioned.

The £250 million is the planned initial size of the banking product, not a verified figure for how much is right now deposited on Midnight.

Hoskinson called this one of the most important milestones in his career.

"This is just one of the many things to come, but I think it's one of the most significant things of at least my career," he mentioned.

He added that the team behind Midnight had moved the originally scheduled hard fork from December to November to accommodate the technical needs of Monument Bank.

Despite the milestone, Hoskinson emphasized that it's only the first step in a much larger mission: bringing traditional financial assets onto Midnight.

"This mission is not done if these assets are just strictly staying on Midnight. Needs to be expanded to Web3. But inherit from Midnight in terms of safety, security, privacy, simplicity," he said.

Industry observers note that hoskinson thinks the main barrier to cryptocurrency adoption is the lack of trust among consumers. He believes that simplifying the user experience without compromising regulatory requirements will allow billions of people to join the blockchain economy.

It has been revealed that hoskinson also shared that there's a massive event coming up for the Midnight Foundation on Dec. 15. Developers will showcase future products and technological advancements scheduled for 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Data leaks happen almost weekly now. Consumers watch their identities, driver’s licenses, and utility bills spill onto dark-web marketplaces after routine corporate breaches. Because centralized databases remain vulnerable honey pots, users increasingly resent uploading intimate personal documentation just to access routine web services. In Canada, this privacy fatigue has sparked a quiet exodus from invasive platforms. Web3 purists and everyday digital asset owners alike reject mandatory surveillance, insisting on cryptographic verification instead of bureaucratic paper trails.

It has been revealed that this growing appetite for digital autonomy drives remarkable momentum across on-chain entertainment hubs. Rather than tolerating intrusive identity interrogations before trying their luck, savvy players actively migrate toward the best crypto no KYC casino Canada portals to protect their digital footprints. Rocketplay’s dedicated crypto guides provide an exceptional compass here, outlining how privacy-first architectures protect user sovereignty while keeping transaction processing lightning fast. Their breakdowns showcase platforms that settle withdrawals on-chain without arbitrary identity verification stalls, earning well-deserved praise from safety-minded participants. Why should anyone hand over sensitive passport scans just to place a digital wager when cryptographic wallet signatures prove account custody instantly?

Critics claim Know-Your-Customer processes are the only way to prevent fraud. Blockchain architecture proves them wrong every single day. Decentralized protocols substitute trust in centralized operators with unassailable mathematical consensus.

The technical architecture behind private, verification-first environments relies on three robust pillars:.

Canadians take pride in practical common sense – we skate to where the puck is going, and the future of consumer internet tech lies squarely in self-custody and algorithmic verification.

Sources indicate that the push toward sovereign, pseudonymous platforms creates an undeniable friction with conventional oversight models. Financial regulators continually debate how to monitor transaction flows without trampling fundamental civil privacy.

Research published by the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada constantly stresses that data minimization remains paramount for consumer protection in the digital era. Storing massive troves of citizen identity records exposes consumers to catastrophic identity theft risks. Forward-thinking decentralized systems honor that principle by collecting zero identity records in the first place, ensuring that a server breach yields zero sensitive personal data.

Skipping identity verification must never mean skipping personal diligence. Rogue operators sometimes disguise shoddy infrastructure behind an anonymous facade, hoping unsuspecting users will overlook missing licenses or slow payment protocols.

Industry observers note that astute players examine transaction latency first. Top-tier non-custodial portals automate payout execution straight to the mempool, rejecting manual morning approvals that trap user liquidity. Furthermore, legitimate no-ID platforms support provably fair algorithms that let you inspect every single outcome on an immutable public ledger.

No-KYC entertainment networks represent much more than a convenient shortcut; they signal a permanent cultural pushback against constant digital surveillance. Owners across Canada have realized that true cybersecurity starts by refusing to share unnecessary private data. As decentralized payment rails and cryptographic tools evolve, the demand for anonymous, lightning-fast interactive experiences will only accelerate. The future belongs to platforms that respect personal boundaries, safeguard sovereignty, and let mathematics do the heavy lifting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s luxury brand, Denza, calls it “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles.” The upcoming Denza N8 electric SUV will launch next week, offering an impressive CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles), massive digital screens, and plenty of premium extras.

After opening pre-orders for the new 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, remarked the results so far “have been excellent.”.

According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.

That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

While Li confirmed last week that the latest EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.

Now, it’s official. Denza announced on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.

BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.

According to recent reports, the Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

According to recent reports, it’s available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).

Sources indicate that the tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will use either a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) and 800 km (497 miles), respectively.

The Denza N8 also features BYD’s latest Flash Charging technology, letting it recharge from 10% to 80% in just five minutes. It takes just nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

Like most of its new luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.

Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.

The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.

BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot.
  • Sources indicate that the 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue.
  • According to recent reports, the Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo intends to add across the US.

Sources indicate that the 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.

According to recent reports, the Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.

“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” said Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.

EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

Sources indicate that smart move on EVGo's part. More reliable charger at a lower cost than they can build themselves, and Tesla takes on all the maintenance and network operations for a slice of the sales.

In a recent development, EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The organization aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it looks to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

Moon Lambo presents several arguments for recovery, but its own weekly-RSI discussion leaves a clear risk unresolved: XRP price could remain under pressure before any broader market rebound takes hold.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On-chain reporters have identified massive flows from the wallet of the recent Binance hacker.
  • While a considerable amount of their exploits has been frozen in place, especially USDT and USDC, on-chain BTC and ETH transfers are virtually impossible to block.
  • The move marks the end of a relatively quiet period for the stolen Ethereum, which was seized during a 3-hour hacking episode that rocked Binance and the crypto world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On-chain reporters have identified massive flows from the wallet of the recent Binance hacker. The exploiter recently moved 74,880 ETH ($136.8M) via THORchain and swapped it for Bitcoin. The move is essentially a sizeable ETH dump, which can cause further trouble for the programmable digital currency amidst the ongoing slump in the crypto market.

While a considerable amount of their exploits has been frozen in place, especially USDT and USDC, on-chain BTC and ETH transfers are virtually impossible to block. Still, trackers are actively pursuing them. The total ETH holdings belonging to this hacker were initially 602,402 $ETH, but it now appears he is actively looking to swap it for Bitcoin.

The move marks the end of a relatively quiet period for the stolen Ethereum, which was seized during a 3-hour hacking episode that rocked Binance and the crypto world. All in all, $6.3 billion was stolen from the exchange’s hot wallets, and a huge chunk of it still lies in the wallets tied to the hacking entity. It was the largest crypto exploit in history by dollar value and has caused the market to lose more than 20% of its value since.

It has been revealed that the use of cross-chain bridges like THORChain has reignited the debate around these automated, decentralized services. Broader industry scrutiny means these services could come under pressure in the near future. Already, US agencies like the FBI have urged the chain’s node operators to block addresses associated with the hack.

It has been revealed that however, there is no solution to this loophole in sight. Critics argue that even if the Bitcoin and Ethereum connected to these exploit wallets cannot be touched in a decentralized economy, they should be prevented from using platforms like THORChain to try to mix and legitimize their illegitimate funds. Eventually, the crypto will end up in centralized exchanges, where it can be blocked and returned to the affected Binance exchange.

Furthermore, the popular use of these cross-chain bridges is influencing liquidity in THORChain pools and contributing to a broader market price squeeze. Initially, it was predicted that a large chunk of the stolen crypto would be frozen for some time, but the sudden exodus has put further pressure on the market, affecting smaller digital currencies more than larger ones.

Hopes of recovering the funds are not lost, as trackers continue to pursue them with the help of automation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hyundai IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in America outside of Tesla, but its larger three-row sibling looks like the better deal right now.

Through September, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 was the third top-selling EV in the US, behind the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.

Hyundai’s electric SUV is outselling rivals like the Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, and Toyota bZ.

Recent findings suggest that why? For one, it’s one of the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at about $35,000, and Hyundai has been offering some of the most attractive lease deals.

After the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September last year, Hyundai responded by reducing prices on the IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims.

Industry observers note that the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250. That’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model adds $2,500, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, starts at $58,955, or nearly $24,000 more than the base IONIQ 5 SE.

Recent findings suggest that on Hyundai’s website, the 2027 IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range is available to lease from $359 a month. The offer is for a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing for an effective cost of $567 per month.

The extended-range Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE RWD can be leased from $369 a month. The offer is also a 24-month lease with $4,999 due at signing, for an effective cost of $577 per month.

According to recent reports, hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9, meanwhile, is available to lease from $419 a month. That deal also includes $4,999 due at signing, but is for a 36-month lease, so the effective cost is $557 per month.

Sources indicate that using Hyundai’s payment calculator, it would cost about $412 a month to lease the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE for 36 months with $4,999 due at signing. With an effective cost of $550 per month, it’s only $7 less than the three-row IONIQ 9.

The Hyundai IONIQ 9 offers more range than its smaller sibling, with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles for the base SE trim.

The IONIQ 5 is a midsize electric SUV, about the same size as a Tesla Model Y, with two rows and enough room for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating and six- or seven-seat configurations.

With an added row of seating, the IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with the IONIQ 5, which offers up to 106.5 cubic feet.

While the IONIQ 9 may be the better deal right now, the IONIQ 5 is still a good fit for those looking for a smaller, more efficient SUV that doesn’t necessarily need the added space.

In comparison, the standard Tesla Model Y RWD is listed for lease starting at $499 a month with an EPA range of up to 321 miles. That’s for a 36-month lease with $3,000 down.

Using Tesla’s payment calculator, if you put the same $4,999 down for a 24-month lease like the IONIQ 5, the Model Y RWD’s monthly rate is $549.

Which one would you choose? The IONIQ 5, IONIQ 9, or Tesla Model Y? Let us know why in the comments.

Both the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are built at Hyundai’s Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

Recent findings suggest that I really haven’t seen much value in leasing. I’d rather buy the car outright using cash, with the goal of keeping the car for 10+ years.

Industry observers note that my family recently bought a Hyundai IONIQ 5, and it is an outstanding car. Loaded with great features — both on the EV side and then for safety and comfort.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told us that its electric SUVs are attracting newly introduced buyers to the brand at a higher rate than its gas or hybrid vehicles.

Sources indicate that the IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

Following multiple technical outages at major U.S. banks that left thousands of people unable to access banking services or make transactions, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley has urged Americans to keep some of their funds in crypto or stablecoins as a backup initiative.

In a recent X post, Horsley pointed to the weaknesses of traditional financial systems, especially in the context of the world's growing reliance on technology.

"Rolling bank outages in the AI era," he stated.

"Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.".

Large U.S. financial institutions such as JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo experienced widespread complaints about technical outages on Nov. 16.

Customers remarked they were having trouble logging into their online accounts, viewing their balances and conducting transactions.

Sources indicate that according to Fox News, the incident affected some of the biggest banking names in the U.S. Thousands of people reported the matter via the outage-tracking platform Downdetector.

Zelle, a popular payment service that people use in the U.S. to transfer funds between bank accounts, was also reportedly affected.

Sources indicate that as of the evening of Nov. 16, Chase had fixed the technical issue, according to the bank. It said transactions were back to normal.

Recent findings suggest that the outage reports initially pointed to multiple banking systems going down at the same time. But further investigation revealed that problems at Chase spilled over into transactions with other banks. However, the Zelle app itself continued to work.

Recent findings suggest that stablecoins such as USDT and USDC aim to track the value of the U.S. dollar as closely as possible. They can be an option for those looking to hold digital funds without the extreme price fluctuations of crypto assets like Bitcoin.

For instance, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, participants in blockchain networks can transfer dollar-based stablecoins 24/7. However, cashing them out into traditional money may still require access to traditional financial institutions.

Breaking: Apollo’s newest electric scooter is also its lowest-cost yet

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market.
  • The fresh Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the manufacturer’s Black Friday sale running through November 30.
  • The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the company is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.

The fresh Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the manufacturer’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo says the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.

The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.

Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.

Recent findings suggest that at 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an vital compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.

Despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.

Industry observers note that apollo says it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance complications. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.

It has been revealed that perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The manufacturer states 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.

At $599, the Dash appears designed to get those riders into Apollo’s ecosystem much earlier – while also putting the company squarely into competition with the mass-market scooters it previously sat above.

And for those wanting a bit more power or features, Apollo’s more upmarket models are on sale now as part of early Black Friday promotions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the 16th of November, Lighter reopened withdrawals after an attacker gained control of a trader’s API keys.

In a recent development, in its report, the perpetual futures exchange said its Security Council returned about 5 million USDC to the affected trader. Interestingly, deposits and withdrawals were “back to normal” after the council switched off Guardian mode.

The exchange traced the leak to unofficial signing software and remarked its protocol and smart contracts were, fortunately enough, unaffected.

According to recent reports, lighter stated it had paused withdrawals through Guardian mode. That basically allowed its Security Council to return around 5 million USDC.

According to recent reports, the exchange stated it was also working to recover funds linked to “an additional withdrawal attempt by the attacker.” However, a separate withdrawal of 10.39 million USDC had already gone through on Ethereum [ETH] before the pause was announced. Bubblemaps later traced some of those funds to Hyperliquid [HYPE].

It has been revealed that kevin Wang, a former market maker at Lighter, also weighed in on the incident. He wrote,.

Lighter said it now required a wallet signature to move funds into public pools.

It has been revealed that at the time of writing, Lighter [LIT] traded near $3, about 8% above its pre-incident range of $2.77–$2.78. LIT had rebounded about 29% from a brief wick near $2.33.

According to recent reports, the rebound had already stalled near $3.07 on the hourly chart. An hourly close above that level would extend the recovery.

It has been revealed that with LIT recovering, the dollar value of assets held on Lighter did not react the same way. On the 17th of November 2026, DeFiLlama demonstrated Total Value Locked (TVL) of $671.04 million. That was down about 14% from $777.33 million before the incident.

Recent findings suggest that of course, derivatives activity also cooled around the incident. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple CTO Emeritus Reveals Why XRP Took BTC’s Code.
  • Here’s why XRP’s Ledger still supports the original elliptic curve that Bitcoin uses for signatures.
  • David Schwartz, Ripple’s CTO Emeritus and one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger, explained a deliberate early design choice this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple CTO Emeritus Reveals Why XRP Took BTC’s Code.

Here’s why XRP’s Ledger still supports the original elliptic curve that Bitcoin uses for signatures.

David Schwartz, Ripple’s CTO Emeritus and one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger, explained a deliberate early design choice this week.

Responding to a post about the ledger’s technical roots, he wrote: “We did things that way in the very early days because we didn’t want to face potential criticism that our choices of those core crypto functions were less secure than bitcoin’s.”.

The discussion began with XRPL validator Vet, who noted that the ledger’s earliest code included helper functions and comments from Bitcoin’s original client, written by Satoshi Nakamoto and copied by early developer Jed McCaleb.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily?15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote.Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including… pic.twitter.com/IZOaa4w0bz.

Most of that code was removed by the end of 2014; in December of that year, then-engineering lead Nik Bougalis deleted the last of the timekeeping routines along with one of Satoshi’s comments.

Industry observers note that two design choices remain. The XRP Ledger still supports the secp256k1 elliptic curve that Bitcoin uses for signatures (it also supports the newer Ed25519 curve, so not every account relies on secp256k1).

Separately, every XRPL address is still generated the Bitcoin way: the public key is hashed with SHA-256 and then with RIPEMD-160 before encoding. Those steps are used by every account on the network today.

Sources indicate that david Schwartz’s explanation is straightforward. In the network’s first years, the team preferred to reuse cryptographic primitives already proven in Bitcoin rather than introduce untested alternatives that crypto critics, particularly in the Bitcoin community, could attack as weaker or experimental.

We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to face potential criticism that our choices of those core crypto functions were less secure than bitcoin's.

Using the same curve and address-generation method removed one potential line of criticism before it could be raised. Ripple CTO Emeritus has noted it is impossible to know whether different choices would actually have drawn that criticism; the point was to avoid having to defend the cryptography at all.

The early code sharing was limited and temporary. The consensus mechanism, transaction model, and most of the ledger’s architecture were built independently.

Industry observers note that it's hard to say. Obviously, we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have. I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway.

According to recent reports, what survived are two well-understood cryptographic building blocks that have remained secure and widely implemented for more than a decade. Later additions, including Ed25519 support, gave users and developers additional options without removing the original path.

The exchange is a small window into how the XRP Ledger was constructed: deliberately conservative on core cryptography in its first years, then gradually cleaned of borrowed code once the project had its footing. The two pieces are still in daily use by everyone on-chain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that amazon isn’t just electrifying its American delivery operations. The virtual substantial box stores that Bezos built understands the benefits of EVs as well as anyone, and they’re working hard to deploy electric vehicles everywhere they can. And now, that global push is extending to India.

According to recent reports, indian automaker TATA Motors has declared a deal with Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India. When it goes live, it will be the largest electric truck deployment by in India and mark Amazon’s most significant move to extend its Indian fleet electrification beyond last-mile logistics.

Sources indicate that “India is accelerating towards electric mobility and the realization of Viksit Bharat 2047,” claims Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy, Hon’ble Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Government of India. “The collaboration between TATA Motors and Amazon shows what that looks like in practice: sustained demand from a nationwide logistics network met by electric trucks manufactured in India. Through PM E-DRIVE, the Government will continue to support this transition, and I look forward to more such efforts in powering green logistics.”.

In addition to being a significant deal for TATA, the 3,000 electric truck deal represents a serous bump to India’s deployed electric truck fleet, and are a major step towards the wide-scale electrification of freight transportation across the country – that’s not just good for Amazon’s fuel bills, it’s good for everyone and everything that breathes air, too.

It has been revealed that “Electrifying our logistics and transportation network is an vital part of Amazon’s goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040,” claims Abhinav Singh, Vice President, Operations, Amazon, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkey. “We have made significant progress in India, with more than 15,000 electric vehicles operating across 500-plus cities. To enable this transition, we are also supporting the development of infrastructure and solutions that make EV adoption easier for our carrier partners and drivers. We are now setting a bold vision to scale electric trucking, addressing one of the toughest challenges in decarbonizing transportation. Our collaboration with TATA Motors marks an important step towards realizing this vision. By combining our strengths, we aim to accelerate the deployment of electric trucks across more routes, starting with intracity operations and expanding to India’s major freight corridors.”.

In a recent development, the truck Amazon will be deploying in these record numbers is a version of the Tata Ultra E.7, a 7.5-tonne (~16,000 lb.) straight truck powered by a 240 kW (~320 hp) electric motor drawing power from a 96 kWh LFP battery pack. The truck’s makers claim a loaded range of up to 130 km (~80 miles) on a single charge, with DC fast-charging that’s capable enough to keep the trucks charged up between deliveries.

Amazon’s new TATA electric delivery trucks will support the transport of goods between warehouse facilities – which means traveling across cities and along India’s national freight corridors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin mining giant MARA Holdings, formerly known as Marathon Digital, continues to offload its Bitcoin holdings, with another multimillion-dollar transfer spotted as the firm's selling spree demonstrates no signs of slowing down.

In a recent development, according to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, MARA transferred another 366 BTC, worth approximately $23.33 million, from its wallets on Nov. 18.

The latest transaction follows a series of substantial Bitcoin sales by the mining manufacturer throughout 2026.

Lookonchain estimates that MARA has already sold a staggering 40,581 BTC this year, generating approximately $3.03 billion at an average selling price of $74,446 per coin.

However, it remains unclear whether the latest 366 BTC transfer represents another completed sale or an internal movement of funds.

MARA's aggressive selling strategy is confirmed by its latest quarterly financial disclosures.

In a recent development, according to its Nov. 9 SEC filing, the company sold approximately 26,984 BTC for $1.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026.

Following the end of September, MARA liquidated another 13,597 BTC at an average price of approximately $81,039, raising an additional $1.1 billion.

These transactions bring its total disclosed Bitcoin sales to 40,581 BTC.

Notably, the company used $750 million from its latest sales to fully repay Bitcoin-backed loans, releasing 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral.

Interestingly, MARA has explicitly signaled that it intends to continue selling Bitcoin as part of a broader shift in its corporate strategy.

However, it began allowing sales of newly mined Bitcoin in 2025 before expanding the policy in 2026 to include coins already held on its balance sheet.

In its latest shareholder letter, MARA stated it plans to continue monetizing Bitcoin to strengthen its financial flexibility.

The tech giant specifically identified artificial intelligence infrastructure, upcoming convertible debt obligations and potential share repurchases as reasons for building up cash reserves.

The selling comes as MARA faces considerable pressure on its core mining business.

Third-quarter revenue declined 35% year over year to $164.2 million, compared to $252.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

  • Recent findings suggest that unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the newly introduced Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market.
  • The RN0 was jointly developed with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes. Now the Japanese giant is adding another electrified vehicle to the list – a premium electric mountain bike.

Recent findings suggest that unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the newly introduced Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market. And unlike many automotive-branded e-bikes that amount to little more than a licensing deal and a familiar logo slapped on someone else’s frame, Honda appears to have actually put some engineering muscle behind this one.

The RN0 was jointly developed with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.

In a recent development, there’s actually some real history behind that connection. Honda experimented with mountain bike development in the early 2000s, culminating in its wild RN01 downhill racing bike. In 2005, that project won the overall series championship in the UCI Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup. Honda never turned the RN01 into a consumer bicycle, but more than two decades later, the RN0 is effectively picking up where the firm previously left off.

According to recent reports, the roughly 24 kg (53 lb) RN0 is set up as a multi-role electric mountain bike, featuring 160 mm FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima front suspension paired with a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima rear shock. DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE wheels use a mullet setup with a 29-inch wheel up front and 27.5-inch wheel in the rear, while Shimano DEORE XT four-piston brakes handle stopping duties.

Those are some quality components, but the drivetrain may be even more interesting.

Honda is using Shimano’s new 2.3 kg drive unit, rated for up to 100 Nm of torque and 750 watts of maximum output, paired with a sizeable 720 Wh battery.

Shimano’s AUTO ASSIST can automatically vary motor assistance based on terrain and rider input, while AUTO SHIFT handles gear changes to maintain an appropriate cadence.

There’s even an Assist Carryover function that briefly continues providing power after pedaling stops, potentially making it easier to clear rocks, roots, and other technical obstacles that normally would see the assist grind to a halt right when it is needed most.

A 2.2-inch color display is integrated directly into the top tube, and there’s USB-C charging plus Shimano app connectivity for adjusting motor settings and electronically locking the bike.

Honda hasn’t yet announced pricing in its release, but with a carbon chassis, Factory-level FOX suspension, XT brakes, and premium Shimano electronics, don’t expect this to be the everyman’s electric bike.

If anything, the RN0 looks much more like Honda is finally bringing its motorcycle engineering mentality back to mountain bikes – this time with a battery and motor along for the ride.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck brand Workhorse is bringing its W56 Class 5 and 6 electric trucks to Canada thanks to a new agreement with a Canadian dealer group and fleet management provider offering truck and trailer sales, parts, repair, and 24/7 roadside assistance and towing services across the Northern nation.

Building on years of electric step van deployments in Canada and underscoring the organization’s commitment to Canada as a growth region, the newly introduced dealer agreement with Tristan Fleet Management marks the first-ever Canadian dealer partnership for Workhorse.

“Canadian fleets need proven electric trucks that deliver on quality and performance in any condition,” said James Griffin, Chief Revenue Officer at Workhorse. “The W56 has already proven itself on this front in real-world fleet service across Canada. Tristan’s strong reputation, its extensive network, and ability to provide around-the-clock roadside support will be extremely valuable as Workhorse continues to grow our presence in the country.”.

According to recent reports, workhorse has been selling and supporting electric trucks in Canada since 2021 through its partnership with Purolator, a Canadian-owned leading integrated freight, package and logistics solutions provider that has grown alongside the rapid expansion of online shopping for everything from groceries to car parts and road-ready motorcycles has also seen the expansion of last-mile delivery contractors. These fleet operators and drivers are essential workers who keep the online economy rolling, and they are getting positively pummeled by this year’s record fuel prices, a product of America’s latest “dumb oil war” in Iran.

And, after Workhorse’ fleet logged its 20 millionth mile driven with zero tailpipe emissions, you could hardly claim that it’s an unknown quantity – a fact that Tristan understands.

“Our customers have been exploring electrification for some time now,” explains Daniel Barbu, Tristan’s Vice President and General Manager. “With generous incentives from Écocamionnage, as well as the current extremely high cost of fuel, the business case for going electric has never been stronger … we’re looking forward to helping Workhorse expand its customer base across Canada and supporting our customers meet their own goals for sustainability and vehicle performance.”.

Tristan operates out of seven locations throughout Québec and Ontario. In addition to its Workhorse offerings, the organization is also an authorized Michelin tire, Cummins engine, and Vanguard trailer dealer.
