💡 Key Takeaways
  • 12 found that stronger AI models could repeat forged answers when weaker helpers read the evidence, exposing a reliability risk in systems that split work across models.
  • In their November paper, researchers Keegan Wang and Anantika Mannby tested agents on fictional records and two-option questions.
  • They measured harmful revisions: adoption of the attacker's wrong answer against a correct baseline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A study submitted to arXiv on Nov. 12 found that stronger AI models could repeat forged answers when weaker helpers read the evidence, exposing a reliability risk in systems that split work across models.

In their November paper, researchers Keegan Wang and Anantika Mannby tested agents on fictional records and two-option questions.

They measured harmful revisions: adoption of the attacker's wrong answer against a correct baseline.

In one Anthropic's Claude Code test, an Opus 5 supervisor chose the planted wrong answer in 1 of 180 trials when reading files itself, compared with 75 of 180 when it delegated reading to Haiku 4.5. This stacked-forgery condition combined several forms of false evidence.

A separate OpenAI's Codex test used a forged annotation claiming authority, and GPT-5.6-sol made no harmful revisions in 180 direct-reading trials, versus 44 in 180 when it relied on GPT-5.6-terra. The Claude Code and Codex comparisons used different attacks, limiting comparisons between the products.

Delegated Claude Code trials mechanically limited the supervisor to its Task tool, removing direct file access, while Codex's delegation restriction was instructional and checked per trial.

In a Nov. 12 study using fictional records, a stronger supervisor could repeat a weaker reader's error. Compare the tested configurations.

Opus 5: 1/180 reading directly, 75/180 with Haiku 4.5, and 0/180 with a same-tier helper, under stacked forgeries.

GPT-5.6-sol: 0/180 reading directly, 44/180 with GPT-5.6-terra, and 1/180 with a same-tier helper, under an authority gloss.

The model handling the evidence can determine whether a stronger supervisor repeats a forged answer.

Sandbox tasks with planted forgeries. Claude Code delegation was Task-only; Codex restriction was instructional and checked per trial. The two selected products used different attacks. Rates describe those configurations, not customer prevalence.

Reported harmful-revision counts from Table 1. Each arm uses 180 fictional facts. Bar lengths are count / 180 on a shared scale; zero is an outlined marker. Conditions are separate tests, not a timeline or product ranking.

Recent findings suggest that sandbox tasks with planted forgeries. Claude Code delegation was Task-only; Codex restriction was instructional and checked per trial. The two selected products used different attacks. Rates describe those configurations, not customer prevalence.

The stacked attack placed five forged documents in a 35-file store, combining correction notices, an authoritative annotation and repeated false accounts. Detectable forgeries carried two clues: they predated the records they purported to correct and lacked genuine accession lines.

According to recent reports, instructions directed at automated readers were resisted wherever the researchers tested them. Some successful attacks instead looked like factual records, allowing a helper's report to carry a false conclusion upward.

Results also varied by attack: a correction-notice condition fooled Codex in 172 of 180 direct-reading trials.

Using same-tier helpers reduced failures in the tested comparisons. Claude Code recorded no harmful revisions in 180 trials per condition under the annotation and stacked attacks, while Codex recorded 1 in 180 under the annotation attack.

Clean-store delegation also produced no harmful revisions in 180 trials for each product.

Sources indicate that in one real-harness test with 40 trials per arm, requiring original-record quotations reduced harmful revisions from 15 to 3. A verifier told to be skeptical reduced them to 1.

The authors identify lost provenance and reduced checking as possible contributors. Their evidence about fewer tool turns is correlational, leaving suppressed verification as a hypothesis.

In a recent development, the experiments measure performance on generated fictional tasks in a sandbox. Their rates apply to the tested configurations, with variation across repeated runs, but they offer no estimate of ordinary customer failures.

The practical warning is that evaluating a supervisor alone can miss failures introduced by the model handling its evidence.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said that crypto needs some of the features that made housing a safe investment for earlier generations. "We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets," Buterin wrote in a post on X on Nov. 18.

The post came a day after economist Peter Tulip published his own post on housing in Raleigh, North Carolina. According to Tulip, looser zoning rules in the city set off a construction boom and pushed real rents down 15% between 2022 and 2025.

In his post, Buterin first pointed to a benefit of young people putting their savings into stocks and crypto instead of real estate.

"One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities," he wrote.

Still, the Ethereum co-founder stated that housing has had one advantage over stocks and crypto. He described it as "a culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can't easily liquidate.".

"Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior," Buterin added.

Ether was trading at $1,808 on Wednesday.

Industry observers note that buterin has written about housing and urban planning before. He has supported the YIMBY movement for denser development in cities for several years.

In a recent development, in 2022, Buterin argued for a land value tax. According to him, such a tax would lower the upfront cost of buying a home and discourage speculation on vacant lots.

In 2025, the Ethereum co-founder called the housing market a "confusing market of peculiar NFTs." According to Buterin, what is really being sold under the label of square footage is the right to live in a particular city. At the time, he also said that legalizing dense development speeds up the economy and benefits even people who prefer single-family homes.

  • So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the 16th of November, Ledger’s public website was infected with malware designed to swap crypto addresses and steal card details. Security researcher Scott Helme traced the code to Optimizely, a website testing provider. His team found compromised scripts tied to 178 organizations, including Ledger, the BBC, and Zoom.

In practice, the malware could swap a copied crypto address for one belonging to the attacker. So if a visitor pasted that address and approved the payment, their crypto could go to the attacker instead.

So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website. Whether it also affected Ledger’s hardware wallets or the Ledger Wallet app remains unclear.

Recent findings suggest that just over a month earlier, though, Ledger had faced a separate attack involving physical devices. In that case, Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold through a reseller contained unauthorized hardware.

At the time, AMBCrypto reported that the October theft had reached $91 million across more than 470 crypto addresses.

Industry observers note that report URI recorded the cleanup of Ledger’s script at 20:41 UTC that day. Early on the 17th of November, Optimizely mentioned,.

We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.

Recent findings suggest that report URI traced about $7,040 in crypto to addresses linked to the attack on the 16th of November. When Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn looked at where the money came from, he estimated that victims sent about $2,300. He said,.

Industry observers note that most of the rest was the attacker’s own money. The attacker appears to have been very sloppy with their onchain hygiene.

However, the number of Ledger visitors who lost funds remains unclear.

Industry observers note that A similar breach had hit Polymarket a few weeks earlier. In that case, the malicious code could act on behalf of traders who were already signed in.

On the 29th of October, it sold some traders’ positions and moved funds out of their wallets.

In a recent development, polymarket paused international trading to stop further losses. It later announced $3.9 million in reimbursements, including about $1.2 million for losses during the pause. By the 30th of October, the company stated it had fully refunded 689 of the 726 affected wallets.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter lineup with the new XENTER E, a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter designed specifically with European city riding in mind.
  • Unveiled around EICMA 2026 in Milan alongside the latest NMAX E, the XENTER E is a high-wheel scooter riding on 16-inch wheels front and rear.
  • That’s an important distinction in European cities, where larger wheels can make quick work of the cobblestones, potholes, and tram tracks that can turn smaller-wheeled scooters into teeth-rattling experiences.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter lineup with the new XENTER E, a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter designed specifically with European city riding in mind.

Unveiled around EICMA 2026 in Milan alongside the latest NMAX E, the XENTER E is a high-wheel scooter riding on 16-inch wheels front and rear.

That’s an important distinction in European cities, where larger wheels can make quick work of the cobblestones, potholes, and tram tracks that can turn smaller-wheeled scooters into teeth-rattling experiences.

Industry observers note that the XENTER E uses Yamaha’s upcoming eAxle powertrain, combining the motor, controller, and reduction gearbox into a compact frame-mounted unit. The motor produces 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power and 33.3 Nm of torque, putting the scooter into Europe’s A1 license category.

Sources indicate that mounting the motor to the frame also means Yamaha can use a more conventional motorcycle-style swingarm rather than hanging the motor on the rear suspension like many scooters. That reduces unsprung weight and should help improve handling and ride quality.

Sources indicate that power is supplied from an integrated 3.5 kWh battery mounted low in the chassis. Yamaha claims 108 km (67 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, though real-world range is expected to be somewhat lower.

An 800W onboard charger can refill the battery in around 5.5 hours from a public charging station. Yamaha will also offer a cable for charging from a household outlet.

Other niceties include three riding modes, traction control, regenerative braking, a reverse mode for maneuvering at low speeds, smart-key operation, and a 5-inch TFT display. Smartphone connectivity adds navigation, battery information, maintenance reminders, and parking-location tracking.

Sources indicate that for about four days now, I am thinking this could be my next ride. A 4 or 4,5 Kwh battery would be a real nice. But for now, it fits perfectly in my daily commute and I could trade in my 2024 Honda supercub. However, € 7800 is too much.. for this kind of money, or just a tad more, there are several low mileage BMW's CE04 on the market.

There’s also enough underseat storage for a full-face helmet, depending on its size, plus USB-C charging and provisions for accessories such as a windscreen and 34-liter top case.

The XENTER E shares its powertrain and battery with Yamaha’s newly introduced NMAX E, but the high-wheel layout gives it a distinctly more European commuter flavor.

Yamaha hasn’t officially announced pricing for each market, though early reports from Milan point to €7,799 in Germany. Deliveries are expected to begin in spring 2027.

It’s certainly not cheap, but the XENTER E looks like Yamaha is finally getting serious about building electric scooters that can replace its bread-and-butter 125cc urban machines, rather than simply supplement them.

MEXC confirmed that its Global Card service will be discontinued on November 18, according to the exchange's announcement. The firm cites service adjustments by its third-party card issuer. From the deadline, existing cards can no longer be used for transactions, and new card applications are suspended.

Owners have two things to take care of before the service ends.

First, the remaining card balance has to be withdrawn: the Withdraw button on the Global Card page sends the funds to the Fiat account.

Second, subscriptions linked to the card should be cancelled or switched to another payment method. Unfortunately for cardholders, recurring payments will most likely fail if they stay on the old card.

In a recent development, if there's still a balance when the service ends, MEXC will credit it to the Spot account, so owners will simply receive their funds back. It's vital to keep in mind that pending card transactions need time to settle, which is why the balance snapshot comes on November 21, three days after the shutdown. The amount will be credited within three business days of the snapshot. Users do not need to take any action.

Refunds for previous card transactions will be credited to the Fiat account once MEXC receives them. Pending cashback will be credited automatically as scheduled. Elite VVIP users with zero-fee benefits will be refunded too, though the eligible fees return to their Spot accounts only before December 15.

Transaction history, card orders and cashback records stay available on the Global Card page for three months after the service ends, so it's worth saving anything needed before access ends.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain types of services to third parties all the time, so witnessing a similar situation is more than a possibility here. Realistically, the shutdown is somewhat inconvenient rather than dangerous, as the balances are returned automatically. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The power-law model links Bitcoin's price to its age, but the recovery forecasts in a Nov.
  • Authors Carlos Baquero and Raquel Menezes argued that Bitcoin's long-run growth rate has slowed under the conditions their test allows.
  • The study's price record ends on Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The power-law model links Bitcoin's price to its age, but the recovery forecasts in a Nov. 10 preprint also assume that departures from the long-run curve reverse, a tendency its historical analysis leaves unresolved.

Authors Carlos Baquero and Raquel Menezes argued that Bitcoin's long-run growth rate has slowed under the conditions their test allows.

The study's price record ends on Sept. 19, so its results do not explain November's selling.

Model advocate Stephen Perrenod made the attractor argument explicit in a June 5 analysis, arguing that tests of price deviations supported an attractor around which bubbles and bear markets occur.

He also cautioned that those tests did not predict next month's price or prove the relationship must continue indefinitely.

Reports on power-law likewise described an attractor framework while leaving the force sustaining it unsettled.

Baquero and Menezes used 820 weekly observations from January 2011 through September 2026. Within a declared family of possible price deviations, their test found evidence of a slowing long-run growth rate.

It rejected constant drift in expected log price at a nominal 5% significance level, compatible with a power-law trend, but does not identify it uniquely.

Their main family allowed shocks to persist as much as a random walk, where a shock need never fade. When a prespecified sensitivity check allowed even more persistent changes, the rejection disappeared, showing how the conclusion depended on the persistence assumption.

The paper also found that a Gompertz curve, which approaches a ceiling, described the historical record almost as well as the power law.

The authors said the fitted models for price deviations revert toward their trends, so most forecasts anticipate a rise from the approximately $81,000 September endpoint.

The restoring tendency entered through the chosen models even though the historical analysis cannot establish it within the evaluated approach.

For Dec. 28, 2030, the power-law model produced a $383,000 median and a 90% interval of $150,000 to $1,015,000. Across all five trend models, the medians ranged from $85,000 to $1,011,000.

The authors warned that their predictive intervals are probably too narrow and are not calibrated. Each forecast combines the fitted distribution with simulated and refitted alternatives, but the refits explore only neighboring choices for how deviations behave.

That leaves broader uncertainty about persistence only partly represented.

The result is a model that assumes a pull toward trend and cannot use its projected rebound as evidence that the pull exists.

Recent findings suggest that the study separates the historical trend question from the reversion its forecasts assume. Compare the two parts of the reasoning.

In a recent development, the slowdown finding holds within the declared shock family; allowing more persistent changes removes it. Reversion remains unresolved.

The fitted forecast models supply reversion, so most project a rise from the September endpoint. This assumption is not established by the historical analysis.

A forecast that assumes a pull toward trend cannot establish that pull through its projected rebound.

The paper's historical conclusion depends on its persistence family. Reversion remains unresolved within the evaluated models and six-feature method. Diagrams show reasoning, not measured causal forces or guaranteed price paths.

It has been revealed that conceptual dependency diagrams, not price charts. The historical view separates the conditional slowdown result from unresolved reversion; the forecast view shows the fitted trend and assumed reversion feeding a projected rise. No numerical extrapolation or arithmetic.

The paper's historical conclusion depends on its persistence family. Reversion remains unresolved within the evaluated models and six-feature method. Diagrams show reasoning, not measured causal forces or guaranteed price paths.

The paper describes itself as a preregistered reanalysis of a record the authors had already studied. They reported freezing the protocol and posting its hash on Oct. 6, applying the historical test once on Oct. 7, then registering the results and forecasts later that morning.

Those forecasts target the last Saturday of each year from 2027 through 2030 and will be assessed jointly using a log-density score, which measures how well the predicted distributions match the eventual prices.

In a recent development, better performance would demonstrate better prediction of those four observations. The distinction remains consequential for a Bitcoin recovery case: a historical growth curve can frame a forecast, but an assumed return toward it is still a proposition for future prices to test.

Cardano-based stablecoin DJED has announced its sunset, as DJED and SHEN services will wind down on December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC.

DJED represents a crypto-backed, overcollateralized stablecoin protocol on Cardano whose US-dollar peg is maintained algorithmically against an ADA reserve (with SHEN as the reserve coin), rather than by fiat reserves.

"DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC," a DJED-focused X account wrote.

According to recent reports, ATTN: DJED & SHEN Holders DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Please redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN you hold before then. All redemptions are subject to the reserve ratio.

Users are urged to redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN they hold before this deadline. Users are to redeem on the protocol and convert their DJED and SHEN back to ADA on the official Djed page. Users who hold DJED or SHEN in liquidity pools, lending markets, or other DeFi platforms are urged to withdraw those positions first, then redeem or swap.

The Djed team noted all systems are fully operational and redemptions are now open, subject to the reserve ratio. It further added that the Djed protocol will be maintained and remain available until December 31, 2026. After this date, all remaining funds will be allocated to the outstanding DJED/SHEN holders once the wind-down is complete.

It has been revealed that djed’s shutdown comes almost three years after its launch, which came in 2023. The stablecoin was officially rolled out on the Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023, and was developed by COTI in collaboration with the Cardano ecosystem to be used on DeFi protocols on Cardano as a stable alternative to volatile cryptocurrencies.

In positive news for the Cardano ecosystem, Monument Bank Limited has introduced tokenized deposits on the Midnight network, marking a milestone for the network and the decentralized finance ecosystem.

At present, Monument is the first UK bank to tokenize retail deposits on a public blockchain, offering clients a 5.2% AER fixed-term return on savings directly through its existing banking app, delivering institutional onchain finance through a familiar and user-friendly banking experience.

Up to £250 million of client deposits will be represented on Midnight in this opening phase, with deposits recorded one-to-one in sterling.

According to recent reports, straying from the broader market trend, PEPE climbed by 2.41% in 24 hours. With no clear catalyst driving the surge, the rally appeared to be specific to the memecoin rather than part of a wider market recovery.

It has been revealed that in fact, Bitcoin was down 0.25% over the same period, while the total crypto market capitalization edged up by just 0.22%. With PEPE still down 27.28% over the last 7 days and its 24-hour trading volume falling by 6.60%, the rebound could prove short-lived.

#29508. Tesla deemed liable for fraud after Solar Roof ‘experiment’ on a home

📅 07 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1620 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla deemed liable for fraud after Solar Roof ‘experiment’ on a home

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the tech giant repeatedly failed to hand over evidence.
  • The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.
  • Tesla, filed in 2022 in San Diego Superior Court’s North County division (case No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the tech giant repeatedly failed to hand over evidence. Tesla had already admitted it breached the contract, broke its warranty, and was negligent on the job.

The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.

The case is Conroy v. Tesla, filed in 2022 in San Diego Superior Court’s North County division (case No. 37-2022-00043670). Electrek reviewed the court orders, the complaint, and the parties’ joint trial readiness report. Here’s what’s in them.

In a recent development, ambrose Conroy, who lives in Rancho Santa Fe, signed up for a Tesla Solar Roof in March 2020. The original contract was $82,210 for a 13.1 kW system. By February 2021, after two amendments, it had grown to roughly $110,000 for an 18.2 kW roof and six Powerwalls.

According to recent reports, the roof was never finished. It never passed a county inspection, and it never produced a single kWh for the house.

Sources indicate that tesla isn’t contesting most of that anymore. In the joint report filed by both sides last month, Tesla stipulated to liability on three of the five claims.

The other two claims, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, are where things went badly for Tesla.

According to recent reports, judge Cynthia Freeland sanctioned Tesla twice over discovery before going further. She ordered it to pay $15,467.50 in February and another $13,500 in June, both times for failing to produce a proper privilege log and responsive documents, and both times warning that issue sanctions could follow.

It has been revealed that tesla missed the next deadline anyway. So on September 11, the court deemed Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation, limiting the trial on those claims to compensatory and punitive damages.

The judge found “ample evidence to support that Defendants have acted willfully.” Among the missing records were Microsoft Teams messages (Tesla’s own corporate witness testified they’re kept “for infinity”), OSHA logs, emails with San Diego County inspectors, and more than 20 quality, install, and safety reports from Tesla’s internal Bolt system.

Recent findings suggest that tesla asked her to reconsider, arguing it had since produced everything. She stated no in a ruling dated October 27, writing that the late documents could support Conroy’s theory that Tesla “knowingly used Plaintiff’s home as an experiment while knowing they lacked the experience to perform as promised.”.

Recent findings suggest that and the “experiment” word reveals up in Tesla’s own messages, according to the trial exhibit list. Exhibit 224 is described as text messages from January 13, 2021, between Tesla’s director of model engineering Bobby Yang and other Tesla employees.

To be clear, that’s how Conroy’s side describes the messages on the exhibit list. We haven’t seen the texts themselves. But Elon Musk is on Conroy’s witness list, and internal emails quoted in the complaint point the same way.

On February 9, 2021, Yang wrote internally that the house was in the “99.5 percentile in terms of complexity” and that “if we can do this job well, we should be able to do any job well.” RJ Johnson, then head of Tesla’s energy business, replied that the project would “skew numbers” but that Tesla needed “to make it right.”.

Industry observers note that johnson was fired in April 2021. The roof had at least 59 mounting planes, and one employee called it the largest job Tesla had attempted at the time, according to the complaint.

Conroy’s account of the installation reads like a list of everything that can go wrong on a roof. These are his allegations, but Tesla has now conceded breach and negligence.

It has been revealed that the tear-off was supposed to take two days and took two weeks. Tesla left in November 2020 with bare roof decking exposed, then had crews work overtime on December 27 to get underlayment down before a storm. Tiles arrived scratched and damaged and went on the roof anyway. Glass tiles shattered in the driveway and lawn, and the family says they still can’t walk there barefoot.

By March 2021, Johnson had agreed in writing that paying “when you’re happy with the outcome is completely reasonable.” Tesla’s billing department kept calling anyway.

In August 2021, an internal email weighed just leaving.

The project went through at least seven project managers. In November 2021, Tesla told Conroy the people behind its repair plan were gone and it had nobody in the area to do the work.

In April 2022, Tesla offered $5,000 to settle everything.

Industry observers note that it didn’t end there. In February 2025, more than two years into the lawsuit, Tesla failed another San Diego County inspection after showing up without the prepares for the venting system. And this summer, Conroy’s electrical expert opened up part of the roof and concluded that the way Tesla ran wiring and conduit under the tiles created a short-circuit and fire risk in heavy rain. The roof is now coming off. Tesla’s lawyers point out that even Conroy’s counsel called that fire risk “counterintuitive.”.

Tesla is fighting the sanction hard. In an October 29 filing, it asked the court to freeze the case while it petitions the California Court of Appeal, arguing the order is “unduly punitive,” violates due process, and amounts to a directed verdict on fraud before trial.

In a recent development, tesla also says the discovery fight had no connection to the fraud claims and that it has now produced everything relevant. The judge already rejected that argument once.

The November 20 trial date is off. A trial readiness conference is set for December 4, and Conroy’s lawyers want to go to trial in December.

Recent findings suggest that this isn’t the first Solar Roof horror story in this case file. Conroy’s complaint attaches our 2020 report on a Solar Roof buyer left with tarps over his house after Tesla tried an untested underlayment on his home. It also cites a 2025 California Contractors State License Board action seeking to revoke Tesla’s contractor licenses over abandoned Solar Roof jobs.

What a nightmare. This is the most damaging Solar Roof case I’ve seen, and I’ve been covering this product since Elon Musk unveiled it on a Universal Studios backlot in 2016.

A botched install isn’t news on its own. Tesla only installed about 3,000 of these roofs before killing the product this year, and plenty of them went sideways. What’s different here is the paper trail: internal emails calling a customer’s home a test of whether Tesla could do “any job,” texts describing the job as an “experiment” with daily reports going to Musk, and then years of Tesla failing to hand over its own records until a judge ran out of patience.

And Tesla’s response to all of it was $5,000.

Look, it’s normal for things not to go as planned with a newly introduced product, and early adopters need to be flexible. However, we are talking about someone’s literal roof over their head here and a trillion-dollar company. Tesla could have and should have made it right a long time ago.

Any time there are internal messages in the record that say essentially "let's skip town rather than try to make this right", it's a tough lift to make a jury think that everything was aboveboard.

The question that strikes me is whether this may also rise to the criminal level, since the CEO was apparently involved in the decision.

The problem sanction might not survive the Court of Appeal. Courts don’t love deciding fraud through discovery orders, and Tesla’s due process argument isn’t frivolous. But even if it gets reversed, Tesla has still admitted it breached the contract and was negligent, and the jury will see how this customer was treated.

This also says a lot about how Tesla ran the Solar Roof business. It sold a product it knew was hard to install, on homes it knew were complex, while the people running the program kept leaving. Conroy’s house was one of the worst cases, but installers are still dealing with the fallout of Tesla walking away from the product earlier this year.

It has been revealed that the real question is what’s in those Teams messages and texts Tesla fought so hard to keep out of this case. If this goes to trial in December, we might find out.

Solar Roof was supposed to make going solar effortless. For most homeowners, conventional panels from a reputable local installer are the safer bet. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Trezor said Monday that a data breach at Skladon, one of its shipping partners, exposed personal information tied to about 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, and that some customers have already reported scam calls.
  • 15 of unauthorized access to systems that held customer shipping data.
  • Industry observers note that the exposed records included full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, order dates, and the products purchased and their prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Trezor said Monday that a data breach at Skladon, one of its shipping partners, exposed personal information tied to about 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, and that some customers have already reported scam calls. The company’s own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved.

Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15 of unauthorized access to systems that held customer shipping data. The breach itself took place on Nov. 7. Trezor believes the attacker exported records for orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7. An investigation is ongoing.

Industry observers note that the exposed records included full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, order dates, and the products purchased and their prices. Trezor mentioned neither it nor Skladon ever holds wallet backups, PINs or passphrases, so the breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer’s bitcoin. It does give a stranger a home address and proof that the person bought a device designed to store crypto.

Anyone who received Trezor’s incident email and ordered in that window was affected. A small number of customers who ordered between Aug. 9 and 14 may also be included, but the firm cannot email them because those details had already been anonymized under its 90-day retention policy. It is reaching those buyers through its blog and posted the same warning on X. Skladon does not ship to the United States, Trezor said, so U.S. customers were not affected by this incident. The company added that Skladon delivers to many countries, and that the leak is not limited to one region.

Recent findings suggest that trezor told customers to treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about their order as suspicious, and to be alert to potential risks to their physical security. Scammers may quote real order details, including what was bought and what was paid, to make a message look genuine. Some customers have already reported scam calls.

Sources indicate that “Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup,” the company stated. Customers should contact support only through the company’s website, never through a link, QR code or number in an unsolicited message, and should never enter a wallet backup anywhere except on their device. If a message contains a threat or makes someone feel unsafe, Trezor said to contact local police first.

Sources indicate that this is not the first time a Trezor contractor has lost customer data. In August, a breach at shipping provider ShipMonk exposed records from 13,689 customers, including 11,742 with full names, emails, phone numbers and shipping addresses. Trezor later mentioned another approximately 67,000 U.S. customers who ordered between November 2019 and August 2021 were also affected, after ShipMonk failed to delete records it had assured the organization were gone.

Industry observers note that in September, a breach at marketing platform Brevo let an attacker send a phishing email through Trezor’s account and, the company later confirmed, export 347,149 newsletter addresses. Trezor took down the malicious domain within 20 minutes, but about 2,500 people had already clicked the link.

In a recent development, “We know this is not the first time customer contact details and addresses have been exposed in an incident involving one of our partners,” Trezor mentioned Monday, adding that it is sorry, especially to anyone affected again. Hardware-wallet makers have faced this risk before. In 2020, an unauthorized party accessed Ledger’s e-commerce and marketing database, leaking over 1 million email addresses; Bitcoin Magazine later reported that more than 200,000 people also had home addresses exposed, and that some victims were later mailed fake devices.

In response, Trezor said anonymous pickup is now available in 18 European countries, so a name and home address need not reach the organization, and that it is working to launch the option in the United States. It is also cutting how long it keeps order data from 90 days to 45, with prepares to reduce that period further, and it has informed the data protection authority. The company said it is reviewing its relationships with third-party partners and the security requirements it places on them.

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Did MARA Sell $3B in Bitcoin in 2026?

On-chain data and Q3 filings reveal a major shift in the mining giant’s treasury playbook.

On-chain alerts lit up after Bitcoin mining giant MARA Holdings moved another 366 BTC ($23.33 million), capping off a massive 2026 sell-off totaling 40,581 BTC worth $3.03 billion.

While a multi-billion-dollar miner sell-off sounds like a bearish warning sign for retail investors, MARA’s third-quarter 2026 financial disclosures reveal a calculated financial reset: the manufacturer sold near market highs to wipe out $1.4 billion in debt and unlock 17,477 BTC in collateral.

According to on-chain tracking data shared by Lookonchain, MARA transferred 366 BTC worth roughly $23.33 million out of its wallets while Bitcoin traded near the $63,700 level. The transfer immediately drew market scrutiny toward MARA’s broader 2026 treasury activity.

Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings (@MARA) continues to dump $BTC, transferring out another 366 $BTC ($23.33M) 8 hours ago.According to official disclosures, #MARA sold 40,581 $BTC ($3.03B) in 2026 at an average price of $74,446.https://t.co/fTOd8FQMxR pic.twitter.com/SQgTLUdrve.

Per firm disclosures and on-chain tallies, MARA has offloaded 40,581 BTC in 2026 for approximately $3.03 billion. The miner executed those sales at an average price of $74,446 per Bitcoin.

In a recent development, for years, publicly traded Bitcoin miners adhered to a strict “HODL everything” playbook, borrowing cash against their Bitcoin reserves to fund operations and hardware expansion. In 2026, MARA aggressively reversed that strategy.

In an official statement on X accompanying its Q3 2026 earnings release, MARA confirmed that it deployed $750 million from post-quarter Bitcoin sales to fully repay its Bitcoin-backed debt.

Clearing those credit facilities released all 17,477 BTC that had been pledged as collateral, bringing MARA’s total debt reduction since the beginning of 2026 to $1.4 billion—a 37% cut to its overall debt load.

After quarter-end, we used bitcoin sale proceeds to fully repay $750 million of bitcoin-backed debt, releasing all 17,477 bitcoin pledged as collateral.Since the beginning of 2026, we have reduced total debt by $1.4 billion, or 37%.Q3 letter: https://t.co/CQ2hTXcEV4 pic.twitter.com/CsnmtN2k0b.

The company also highlighted its ambition to evolve from a pure-play Bitcoin miner into an integrated, energy-backed AI and digital infrastructure platform.

According to MARA, Bitcoin mining built the physical footprint, access to low-cost power created the opportunity, and AI/HPC and cloud services offer higher-margin, longer-duration, and more predictable returns. The firm is now shifting from building capacity to commercializing it as an integrated “energy-to-compute” operator.

MARA’s energized hashrate reached 71.2 EH/s in Q3 (up 18% year-over-year from 60.4 EH/s), cementing its position as the largest publicly traded Bitcoin miner by computing capacity.

The firm captures roughly 5.4% of all global Bitcoin miner rewards, producing 2,247 BTC and winning 644 blocks during the quarter—a slight dip from 5.9% in Q2 as overall network difficulty grew faster than MARA’s deployments.

At the end of Q3 2026, MARA held $3.8 billion in total liquidity, consisting of 34,012 BTC (valued at ~$2.8 billion) and $946.5 million in unrestricted cash.

Industry observers note that MARA’s Bitcoin sales could add further downward pressure on the price in the short term, particularly as demand remains weak and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded nearly $240 million in outflows yesterday.

Sources indicate that however, the move could be positive from a longer-term perspective. By repaying $750 million in debt, MARA freed up 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral, significantly reducing the risk of forced liquidations if Bitcoin falls further.

In a recent development, MARA’s move reflects a broader shift across the Bitcoin mining industry. Publicly traded miners are no longer simply holding Bitcoin; they are actively managing their treasuries, reducing debt and expanding into energy and AI infrastructure. This could make the sector more resilient during market downturns and reduce the risk of forced Bitcoin selling.

#29504. Everyone wants an electric pickup truck. I want more electric 125cc motorcycles

📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1936 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Everyone wants an electric pickup truck. I want more electric 125cc motorcycles

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you follow the EV industry in North America, you’d be forgiven for thinking that the future of transportation revolves around electric SUVs and pickups.
  • It has been revealed that don’t get me wrong – I hope they succeed.
  • Because while the West keeps trying to electrify pickup trucks and SUVs, much of the world has already settled on a far more sensible transportation appliance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you follow the EV industry in North America, you’d be forgiven for thinking that the future of transportation revolves around electric SUVs and pickups. Every week seems to bring another teaser from a startup promising to reinvent the family car or truck. The latest electric SUVs, “coming soon” tiny trucks, lifestyle trucks, modular trucks, etc. Companies like Slate, TELO, and countless others have generated plenty of excitement, even if many of them still have everything left to prove.

It has been revealed that don’t get me wrong – I hope they succeed. We need more affordable electric vehicles. But after spending nearly two decades covering a specific part of the electric-vehicle space and a good chunk of that time traveling around the world to see how people actually get around, I can’t help but wonder if we’re chasing the wrong prize here.

Because while the West keeps trying to electrify pickup trucks and SUVs, much of the world has already settled on a far more sensible transportation appliance.

It’s the humble 125cc motorcycle.

Western readers often think of a sedan as the world’s “normal” or “sensible” vehicle.

But go traveling almost anywhere in Asia, and that illusion disappears in about five minutes.

Sources indicate that the roads are filled with Honda Clicks and CG125s, Hero Splendors, Yamaha NMAXs and YBR125s, and countless other small-displacement motorcycles. They carry workers to jobs, students to school, families to dinner, and every imaginable cargo in between.

They’re the delivery vans. They’re the commuter cars. They’re grocery getters, family transportation, and work trucks. And perhaps more importantly, they transport hundreds of millions of people every single day.

You don’t have to spend long in places like the Philippines before realizing something else: these aren’t really “motorcycle cultures.” They’re just transportation cultures. People ride these machines because they make sense.

And I’ve done it myself to see what all the fuss was about. Sure, I’m an e-motorcycle guy through and through. But I’ve been there to ride a mile in their motorcycle sandals, and so I get it.

Even so, having had one cheek on each saddle, I still have to think there’s a better way than the tried-and-true 125cc combustion engine motorcycles that have become the workhorse of much of the world.

The extreme proliferation of small motorcycles is what makes the current electric motorcycle market feel so strange. If there were ever a class of gasoline vehicle that batteries are already capable of replacing, it’s the 125cc combustion engine motorcycle.

These bikes aren’t demanding. They generally produce a modest 10-15 hp (8–11 kW) of power. They cruise comfortably around 45-60 mph (70-100 km/h). Most riders travel relatively short daily distances measured in dozens of miles, not hundreds.

A modern electric motorcycle with a 4-6 kWh battery can comfortably accomplish those same tasks while offering smoother acceleration, quieter operation, lower maintenance, and dramatically lower operating costs.

Sources indicate that unlike replacing a heavy-duty pickup truck that tows livestock trailers across Montana, replacing a 125cc commuter bike is already well within today’s battery technology. In many ways, it’s one of the easiest transportation sectors to electrify.

Instead, North America’s electric motorcycle market developed in an odd direction.

We have electric bicycles, and those are great for urban commuters. But then we jump almost straight to premium electric motorcycles costing $15,000 to $25,000. The practical middle has remained surprisingly sparse.

Thankfully, that seems to be changing.

The ONYX RCR became something of a cult favorite by proving there was genuine demand for lightweight, motorcycle-like electric transportation without superbike performance.

Ryvid’s Anthem pushed further, adding highway capability while still remaining approachable and relatively affordable.

The upcoming LiveWire S4 Honcho also feels like an encouraging step toward a lighter, more practical electric motorcycle instead of another oversized premium machine.

Even Infinite Machine’s Olto, while occupying a slightly different category, demonstrates growing interest in practical urban electric two-wheelers that prioritize transportation over headline horsepower.

According to recent reports, these companies are proving something key: People don’t necessarily need 100 horsepower. Many simply need transportation.

Don’t misunderstand me. Electric pickup trucks absolutely have their place. Electric SUVs do too.

But we’ve spent the last decade pouring enormous engineering effort into electrifying some of the least energy-efficient passenger vehicles on the road.

Meanwhile, we’ve largely ignored one of the most efficient gasoline vehicle classes humanity has ever created.

It has been revealed that A typical 125cc combustion engine motorcycle can already achieve fuel economy approaching or exceeding 100 mpg (2.35 liters/100 km). An electric equivalent becomes almost absurdly efficient.

Sources indicate that we’re talking roughly 4-6 kWh per 100 kilometers (62 miles) – just a fraction of the energy consumed even by many compact electric cars. I once did the math, and a light electric motorcycle can travel 10,000 km (roughly 6,000 miles) for around $160 in electricity. Basically, your electrical bill doesn’t even notice when you own an electric motorcycle. Charging it simply doesn’t move the needle.

Instead of asking how we can fit ever-larger battery packs into increasingly larger SUVs and trucks, perhaps we should also be asking how many trips don’t need a large vehicle in the first place.

Transportation statistics across much of the developed world tell a familiar story.

Industry observers note that most trips involve one person. Maybe there’s also a backpack in the mix. Maybe there are some groceries getting picked up on the way home. Occasionally, there’s another passenger.

Those things are exactly what small motorcycles have been doing around the world for decades.

It has been revealed that I recently spent some time in the Philippines, where I watched motorcycles carrying impossible-looking loads every day. Entire families would ride together. Construction materials. Furniture. Livestock. I saw two pigs on a 125cc bike, I kid you not. I’ve seen even crazier things in Thailand.

Again, I’m certainly not advocating that we adopt some of those practices in the West – there are obvious safety considerations – but it demonstrates just how incredibly capable these machines can be.

Even within normal Western expectations, a 125cc-class motorcycle is capable of handling an astonishing percentage of daily transportation needs.

This is where discussions about motorcycles often become unnecessarily polarized.

Industry observers note that no, motorcycles aren’t ideal in every situation. Yes, heavy rain exists. Snow exists. Families with multiple children exist. Long interstate road trips exist.

Nobody is suggesting a 125cc electric motorcycle should replace every car.

If a household can replace even half of its daily driving with a lightweight electric motorcycle, that’s already a massive reduction in energy consumption, congestion, parking demand, and transportation costs.

Transportation doesn’t have to be all-or-nothing. So enough with this “but what if it rains?” stuff. Either put on a jacket that day or drive your car. But for the majority of the trips each year you take where it’s not raining, you could have done it in a much more efficient (and fun) way.

Sources indicate that one of the biggest conversations surrounding EV adoption is charging. But smaller electric motorcycles barely participate in that problem. A 4-5 kWh battery charges overnight from an ordinary household outlet. The outlet you plug your laptop charger into is basically the equivalent of a Level 2 public charger for an e-motorcycle – that’s how fast it is.

DC fast charging isn’t really necessary on a light electric motorcycle. There’s no need for an expensive home charger. There’s no massive battery pack. Just plug it in before bed and wake up with a battery that’s been fully charged and waiting on you for hours already.

The simplicity is almost refreshing.

And if you want to go wild, there are swappable battery networks like Gogoro in Taiwan or Vammo in South America that can make charging unnecessary.

In a recent development, another advantage rarely discussed is intimidation. Many people don’t want a 600 lb (270 kg) motorcycle producing superbike acceleration. They want something approachable, something lightweight, maneuverable, easy to park, and easy to live with.

That’s exactly why 125cc motorcycles became so successful globally.

It has been revealed that electric versions preserve all of those advantages while making them even easier to ride thanks to instant torque and the absence of clutch work. Many of them even come with reverse mode, making them easier to park and wiggle around even on hilly terrain.

One reason Europe has seen more progress here is that the regulatory framework already exists.

Manufacturers regularly market bikes as “125cc equivalents,” and consumers immediately understand what that means.

Licensing systems and insurance companies recognize the category. It’s a mature transportation class.

North America, by comparison, often treats motorcycles as either recreational toys or large-displacement touring machines. We’ve largely forgotten that much of the world simply sees them as transportation.

Ironically, younger riders may already be showing us the way forward.

The explosion in popularity of Sur Ron-style electric motorcycles and lightweight e-motos demonstrates that younger generations are perfectly willing to embrace two-wheeled electric transportation.

Not everyone buying those bikes is looking for motocross. Many simply enjoy the freedom, accessibility, affordability, and fun that come with traveling on two wheels.

Sources indicate that rather than dismissing that trend, perhaps we should recognize it as an opportunity. Today’s recreational rider often becomes tomorrow’s commuter.

If someone discovers they enjoy getting around on an electric two-wheeler, moving from a lightweight e-moto to a practical 125cc-equivalent commuter becomes a much smaller leap than convincing someone to abandon their car entirely.

Industry observers note that one observation has stuck with me after so many years of covering the electric vehicle industry and traveling through countries where motorcycles dominate daily life. The West has spent years trying to electrify the largest, heaviest, and least efficient vehicles on our roads. Meanwhile, we’ve paid surprisingly little attention to electrifying the vehicle that already moves much of humanity every single day.

Sources indicate that in Europe at least, there's a cliff between a pedal ebike, which anyone can ride without any pre planning, and a motorcycle which needs passing a specific test, taxing, taking out insurance and wearing safety gear. Even people with car licences need to take driving lessons and the test. It means you can't just step on a motorcycle when it makes sense you need potentially months of planning. It's much easier just to take a car you're already licensed for.

I’m not arguing that everyone should ride a motorcycle. And I’m certainly not arguing that cars no longer have an important place.

But perhaps we’ve underestimated just how many people could benefit from something in between.

Industry observers note that not just an electric bicycle, and not just a $25,000 electric motorcycle. Just an honest, practical, affordable electric equivalent of the vehicle that already keeps much of the world moving.

Because if we’re serious about accelerating electric transportation, maybe the future isn’t another electric pickup truck. Maybe it’s finally giving the world’s favorite motorcycle an electric motor.

Monument Bank’s Tokenised Saver records customers’ deposits on the Midnight blockchain, but savers cannot transfer the token, sell it to another customer, or pledge it to an outside lender.

In a Nov. 17 post, Charles Hoskinson celebrated the bank’s launch, quoting Midnight's congratulations to Monument and its partners:.

Sources indicate that “250 million pounds on-chain! That's some serious TVL.”.

Monument’s March 27 announcement described a target of up to £250 million in client deposits, so the immediate test is what a customer can do with the record today. Monument’s blockchain record leaves withdrawal and collateral rights governed by the bank’s account terms.

It has been revealed that the Tokenised Saver summary states the token mirrors the deposit, while Monument’s records remain the official account of the savings. If the two differ, the bank’s records apply, subject to correcting errors. Customers retain the right to query or challenge an error.

Neither the account nor its token record may be transferred, sold, or assigned, including to another Monument customer. Monument’s FAQ also claims the bank owns and controls the wallet, so customers do not manage a private key or seed phrase.

The token record cannot be used as security, while the savings account can serve as security only in Monument’s favor, with the bank's written agreement. That leaves room for an agreed bank arrangement, but supplies no right to take the token to another lender.

Monument’s savings contract supplies the rights. Its Midnight token record mirrors the deposit without adding transfer or collateral rights.

The bank controls the token record. The underlying deposit and its agreed terms remain authoritative.

Monument may pause or stop tokenization. The deposit, interest, maturity and FSCS treatment remain unchanged.

The token feature can stop while the bank deposit continues on its agreed terms.

Current product summary and FAQ as read November 17, 2026. A paused feature is a possible contractual state, not a reported outage. FSCS cover applies to eligible deposits under aggregate limits. No issued balance or flow size is depicted.

Schematic of the contractual relationship between a deposit and its mirrored record, not a transaction sequence. The selectable pause/stop state illustrates a power described in current terms.

It has been revealed that current product summary and FAQ as read November 17, 2026. A paused feature is a possible contractual state, not a reported outage. FSCS cover applies to eligible deposits under aggregate limits. No issued balance or flow size is depicted.

Monument can also change, pause or stop the tokenization feature. Its summary warns that the record can be delayed, unavailable, or wrong, while saying the deposit, interest rate, interest, maturity date, and FSCS protection remain the same.

The bank deposit continues independently of whether its digital copy is functioning.

Sources indicate that the product currently advertises a 12-month term at 5.2% annual equivalent rate, or 5.08% gross, with interest calculated daily and paid monthly. Interest can go to the customer’s linked account or back into the saver.

Eligibility is limited to existing Monument clients who are UK residents aged 18 or older. Accounts are held in one person’s name and require a personal UK bank account linked to the account.

Customers must hold at least £25,000 across Monument savings accounts, while the Tokenised Saver maximum is £100,000, excluding interest.

Sources indicate that customers have 14 days from account opening to fund the account and can cancel without penalty during that window. Otherwise, withdrawals and early closures are prohibited during the term, which begins with the first deposit.

Monument says eligible deposits are protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme up to £120,000 per person, aggregated across eligible deposits with the bank.

In March, Monument noted deposits were the first phase and that it would explore tokenized investments and fresh lending options within its app afterward.

Recent findings suggest that the current saver’s published terms do not provide an investment-backed lending facility. For investment-backed lending, the relevant terms would need to identify the collateral, establish the lender’s rights over it and explain how customers obtain spendable funds.

Customer-controlled transfers or external token collateral would also require rights and arrangements beyond this saver’s present restrictions.

In a recent development, for savers today, the concrete offer is fixed interest and an additional bank-controlled record, while future customer liquidity depends on latest product rights and operating arrangements. Disclosure of the funded and tokenized balance would answer the separate question of the program’s scale.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinbase rolled out an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets customers connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order.
  • The organization said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Consumers can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop.
  • Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase rolled out an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets customers connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order.

The organization said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Consumers can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.”.

Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them.

The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview.

In a recent development, the official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account.

Recent findings suggest that armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is presently available to U.S. Coinbase people, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. In a disclaimer attached to Tuesday’s announcement, it said product availability, eligibility and Coinbase entities “vary by jurisdiction,” that trading can result in a total loss, and that “AI agents may fail.”.

In a recent development, the same post said users direct all AI activity and assume full responsibility. The developer documentation adds that agents can misinterpret instructions or produce inaccurate output, and that the user is responsible for reviewing and authorizing trades. Access can be revoked later in an account’s security settings, under connections.

OpenAI’s help pages describe a distinct Finances feature in the United States that can connect bank and credit-report data but cannot place trades, and note that third-party plugins that support transactions are a separate product.

Recent findings suggest that tuesday’s plugin is the most visible version of work the company has been shipping for months. In June, it introduced Coinbase for Agents, a login and a command-line tool that let an AI app trade inside limits set by the user, including a gradual rebalancing toward a bitcoin-heavy portfolio. On Nov. 11, it added Agent Controls, server-side caps on trade size and 24-hour volume, plus an auto-stop if a portfolio falls by a set percentage. Those controls live on the company’s servers, so an agent cannot switch them off.

The official plugin is meant for people who want to stay in the loop. The company also documents a custom ChatGPT connection for automated workflows that does not add a confirmation card before each trade, though sign-in, consent and authorization for financial actions still apply. For the official plugin, every bitcoin, stock or derivatives order still needs a human yes.

Volkswagen built its global empire on the promise of affordable, accessible transportation, embodied by the iconic Type 1 Beetle. Now facing an existential crisis after a decades-long push upmarket, the automaker faces a reckoning – and a retreat back into affordable, mass-market electric sedans like the fresh FAW-VW ID. AURA L5 (and the software that powers it) might be exactly what VW needs to reach a new generation of buyers.

According to recent reports, like the Ford Model T, the original VW Type 1 Beetle was an engineering-led answer to a basic problem: making family transportation affordable and accessible to the masses. And regardless of how you feel about Elon Musk, the Tesla Model 3 has become the spiritual successor to those cars, bringing electric transportation to millions of mainstream drivers. As the Model 3 approaches its 11th year in public view, the recently revealed all-electric ID. AURA L5 and VW JETTA looks like it could be a compelling rival to the mainstream M3.

Recent findings suggest that co-developed by Volkswagen’s Chinese and German design teams and set to be built by the FAW-VW JV, the ID. AURA L5 is an Accord/Camry-sized electric family car a practical fastback-style rear hatch, frameless doors, and a claimed “84.4% usable floor-area ratio.” The power-operated hatchback opens its maw more than 70 degrees, revealing a 39″ wide opening that can handle groceries, luggage, golf clubs, pets, bodies – whatever you got.

Industry observers note that don’t take my word for it, though. This is the original text from the manufacturer’s press release (translated from Chinese by Google):.

In a recent development, the ID. AURA L5 is a pure electric family sedan, jointly designed by Chinese and German design teams, and highly replicates the design essence of the ID. AURA concept car shown at the 2025 Shanghai Auto Show. Its short overhang and long wheelbase proportions create a sleek and flowing coupe-like stance, achieving a “usable floor area ratio” of 84.4%. The sides feature true frameless doors, semi-concealed door handles, and an electric hatchback tailgate with an opening angle exceeding 70°, and an opening width exceeding 1000 mm, greatly improving the convenience of loading and unloading large items, deeply integrating fastback aesthetics with practicality. Some models will be equipped with LiDAR and feature the Hyper Sense 8 end-to-end large model, making daily travel easier and more convenient for customers.

The production version of the ID. AURA L5 is expected to pack the same 155 kW (~208 hp) electric motors unveiled when the concept AURA L5 was first shown last year (battery specs were not released), and was shown as part of a broader product announcement of what VW Group China would be showcasing at this year’s China International Import Expo (CIIE). These include the first two models fully equipped with Volkswagen Group’s locally developed VEGA “integrated technology matrix” (read: software), and the Volkswagen Anhui intelligent pure electric “coupe” crossover.

The announcement coincides with reports from outlets like Autocar and Reuters that Volkswagen is evaluating whether to deploy its China-developed electrical architecture across the majority of its European markets.

“According to internal discussions confirmed by Group board member and Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer,” reports Autocar’s Greg Kable, “up to 75% of the firm’s core models in Europe could eventually use the China Electronic Architecture.”.

In a recent development, the Volkswagen Group has been struggling to deliver a software experience that resonates with customers. To their credit, they’re looking for outside help, spending billions of dollars on a software collaboration with EV startup Rivian for its upcoming electric truck brand Scout rather than going it alone. With billions of dollars and potential future of the company at stake, then, this seems like the most interesting bit of the announcement:.

During the event, the immersive interactive experience exhibit “Digital Magic Cube,” which made its debut at last year’s China International Import Expo, will undergo an iterative upgrade to showcase the core strength of CEA (China Electronic Architecture), the software pillar of Volkswagen Group’s integrated self-developed technology matrix VEGA, to the attendees.

To date, CEA has enabled five fresh models from three joint ventures within the Volkswagen Group on a large scale, and software iterations have already been completed this year. CEA brings three core advantages to the Group’s new model lineup in China: intelligent accessibility, continuous upgrades, and safety redundancy. Through immersive interactive presentations, it provides consumers with the most intuitive experience. Empowered by the new AI R&D toolchain “C-Brain,” CEA introduces AI agents into software development, design, and engineering verification, enabling more flexible and efficient integration and innovation of vehicle intelligence capabilities, giving vehicles powerful thinking and perception abilities. Intelligent vehicles powered by CEA can better understand consumer needs, more efficiently create in-vehicle intelligent application scenarios, and better enhance digital intelligent safety redundancy, bringing Chinese consumers a new generation of intelligent mobility experience defined by Volkswagen standards.

Sensible looking average car which should appeal to VW buyers provided the price, charging speed and range are right. Especially like that it has a hatch without being SUV shaped.

The show runs through November 10th, and we’ll be keeping an eye out for more details on the ID. AURA lineup and the Anhui intelligent pure electric coupe, including its powertrain, battery, and software specifications, as they become available.

XRP’s dip below $1 has revived hopes of a roughly 70% rebound, with one analyst citing a similar August rally.

Recent findings suggest that XRP could repeat a roughly 70% rebound from below $1, according to a crypto commentator who points to an August rally as the template. In a newly introduced YouTube episode, Zach Rector argues that another sharp recovery is possible, though the case rests largely on a historical chart comparison rather than a confirmed catalyst.

The chart discussion puts XRP’s latest low near $0.89. The analyst claims an earlier slide to $0.98 in August was followed by a rise toward $1.70 within four or five days.

According to recent reports, “I’m not here to guarantee that that’s coming again,” Zach Rector notes, before overlaying the earlier price pattern onto the latest decline. The analyst also suggests XRP could revisit $2 promptly, without committing to a date.

Recent findings suggest that the explanation centers on leverage: the host argues that downside liquidations have largely cleared, leaving market makers an incentive to drive prices higher. The transcript provides no liquidation figures, order-book data or positioning metrics to substantiate that view.

It has been revealed that that distinction matters. A previous bounce illustrates how sharply XRP can recover, but it does not establish that selling pressure is exhausted or rule out another decline.

The more consequential adoption discussion concerns the analyst’s claim that 1,700 institutions, corporations and enterprises use Ripple solutions. Rector explicitly acknowledges that there is no breakdown showing how many use products involving XRP.

Zach Rector also defends Ripple’s emphasis on its RLUSD stablecoin, arguing that greater stablecoin liquidity could attract activity to the XRP Ledger.

A statement attributed to Old Glory Bank supports offering both XRP and stablecoins, with regulated stablecoins potentially better suited to payments where businesses require certainty of value.

Still, stablecoin issuance on the ledger should not be confused with evidence that every payment requires XRP as an intermediary. The YouTube video does not establish that connection, despite the host’s bullish interpretation.

Zach Rector also identifies a proposed lending protocol as a potential source of collateral demand.

For crypto enthusiasts, these are separate propositions to track: a short-term rebound based on chart resemblance, and a longer-term investment case that depends on measurable network activity, liquidity and actual XRP usage.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard defended the blockchain's future as his organization sought nearly 25 million ADA to promote adoption.

According to recent reports, in a Nov. 15 statement, Gregaard argued that Cardano had become technologically stronger and more decentralized, pushing back against growing concerns about the network's future following controversial remarks by founder Charles Hoskinson.

The comments followed a backlash against Hoskinson's declaration that Cardano's original development roadmap was complete, with some investors questioning whether the network had delivered on its broader ambitions.

Hoskinson later clarified that he meant the completion of Cardano's original engineering roadmap, not that development or his involvement with the ecosystem had ended.

Sources indicate that however, Gregaard argued that Cardano's future should not depend on any single individual or organization. He remarked:.

“Decentralization means that no single individual gets to decide when Cardano is finished.”.

Gregaard pointed to several developments he believes have strengthened Cardano's competitive position, including decentralized governance, alternative node implementations and new infrastructure for financial institutions.

He highlighted Amaru and Dingo, alternative implementations of Cardano's blockchain software written in Rust and Go, respectively, as advances that could reduce reliance on a single technology stack.

The executive also cited the introduction of ADA futures on CME Group and the launch of CIP-0113, a programmable token standard designed to support regulated financial assets.

According to Gregaard, the fresh standard has already enabled the tokenization of 850,000 shares in Veridian, a Swiss company spun out of the Cardano Foundation, structured as legally recognized securities under Swiss law.

The development lets companies embed compliance requirements, investor eligibility, and transfer restrictions directly into blockchain-based assets.

Recent findings suggest that gregaard believes these capabilities could position Cardano to compete in the growing market for tokenized stocks, bonds and other traditional financial instruments. He noted:.

“The Cardano I see today is fundamentally stronger, more decentralized, and more capable than the Cardano I came into over five years ago.”.

However, the executive also acknowledged that technological progress alone would not determine Cardano's long-term success. Gregaard noted:.

“Of course, we need to translate more of these initiatives into production deployments, recurring transactions and sustainable economic activity.”.

He added that Cardano needs to become more competitive, even as he defended the progress made across its ecosystem.

That challenge has become particularly relevant as the Foundation seeks additional community funding to expand Cardano's presence at major industry events.

On Nov. 16, the Cardano Foundation submitted a governance proposal requesting 24,995,775 ADA from the network's community treasury.

The request carries an estimated value of nearly $5 million based on an assumed ADA price of $0.20 and would finance Cardano's participation in 12 international conferences throughout 2027.

The proposed spending includes approximately $2 million for sponsorships, $1 million for exhibition infrastructure and $702,000 for travel support. Another $695,000 would finance accompanying events, including four hackathons.

The Foundation argued that coordinated participation in industry conferences gives Cardano developers access to businesses, investors and regulators they might otherwise struggle to reach.

It cited results from its previous events program, which generated 8,191 booth contacts, engaged 1,169 developers and initiated discussions around 219 potential collaborations between August 2025 and July 2026.

The program also supported 79 ecosystem projects and generated 1,045 Cardano wallet registrations, according to the Foundation.

However, the latest proposal highlights the distinction between attracting industry interest and establishing sustainable blockchain activity.

Its 2027 targets include 9,520 booth contacts, 955 developers, and 184 potential collaborations. While the Foundation also promises to track on-chain transactions generated through event contacts, the proposal sets no numerical target for that activity.

The Foundation seeks 24,995,775 ADA for 12 conferences in 2027. Its proposed budget is $4,999,155 at an assumed $0.20 per ADA.

The Foundation sets numerical outreach targets and plans to track transactions from event leads without setting a transaction target.

According to recent reports, the spending blueprint and 2027 targets depend on proposal approval and delivery. The previous program and proposed program differ in event scope. The $0.20 ADA price is a budgeting assumption.

In a recent development, budget bars use a common $2 million scale and exact proposal inputs. Other costs add merchandise ($82,000), local partners ($233,100), and audit, taxes and other fees ($238,055), totaling $553,155, displayed to the nearest $1,000.

In a recent development, the spending plan and 2027 targets depend on proposal approval and delivery. The previous program and proposed program differ in event scope. The $0.20 ADA price is a budgeting assumption.

The organization has committed to publishing spending reports, monitoring performance through a public dashboard, and returning unused funds to the treasury.

Sources indicate that the proposal also acknowledges financial risks associated with ADA's price. Should the token fall below the assumed $0.20 valuation, the Foundation says it would reduce or cancel planned activities rather than exceed its funding allocation.

Industry observers note that the funding request is now before Cardano's delegated representatives, who have until Dec. 20 to vote on whether to approve the withdrawal.

Their decision will determine whether the Foundation secures another year of treasury-backed international outreach as it attempts to translate Cardano's technological progress into more measurable economic adoption.
