💡 Key Takeaways
  • Forget what your Fox News-addicted uncle told you about cheese-eating surrender monkeys.
  • Co-developed by the EV experts at Renault Group and the defense experts at Belgian electronics firm John Cockerill, the new Forefront concept previews a new, modular ground vehicle that can be rapidly industrialized at a controlled cost, with unique mobility and off-road performance, and capable of autonomously navigating complex terrain.
  • Industry observers note that “Forefront Concept … demonstrates the contribution that Renault Group’s industrial and technological expertise can make to a strategic sector such as unmanned ground vehicles with multiple applications expected across both civilian and military sectors in the years to come,” explains François Provost, CEO, Renault Group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Forget what your Fox News-addicted uncle told you about cheese-eating surrender monkeys. The French military has centuries of storied military victories and traditions behind it, and Renault wants in on that action with a latest, autonomous electric vehicle platform designed to tackle the Armée de Terre’s most demanding missions.

Co-developed by the EV experts at Renault Group and the defense experts at Belgian electronics firm John Cockerill, the new Forefront concept previews a new, modular ground vehicle that can be rapidly industrialized at a controlled cost, with unique mobility and off-road performance, and capable of autonomously navigating complex terrain. The result is a machine that could front-line logistical capabilities for both defense and civilian applications, enabling missions to be carried out remotely in very high-risk and hard‑to‑reach environments.

Industry observers note that “Forefront Concept … demonstrates the contribution that Renault Group’s industrial and technological expertise can make to a strategic sector such as unmanned ground vehicles with multiple applications expected across both civilian and military sectors in the years to come,” explains François Provost, CEO, Renault Group. “This innovative project brings together two complementary areas of expertise: Renault Group’s in the rapid, large-scale and cost-effective development and production of high-performance, reliable technological products and John Cockerill’s in the defense industry.”.

It has been revealed that renault is quick to point out that its new concept isn’t just suitable for military work. Although it’s worth pointing out that the Renault-provided image, above, isn’t just AI slop: it would be impractical if it was real, with no real obvious way to get those RCP pipes on or off the thing. That said, presenting their military killbot as a construction mule is at least more credible than the “ambulance” and “troop transport” use cases we’ve seen touted by similar concepts on the American side.

Call me cynical but military contracts are the best and last refuge for a tech giant that cannot compete in the open market. With no / limited international competition, a famously slow procurement process that favors "proven" (read 3+ generation old) technology, and equipment that is rarely used in a competitive environment and whose failures are cloaked behind national security classifications, it is the perfect place to hide. (C.f. Oshkosh and AM General).

Forefront seems to be little more than a rendering at this stage, with the first of the Forefront concept prototypes set to take part in a number of exercises and trials in the months ahead to further refine the concept.

#29484. Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bitcoinmagazine ↗ Open Full Page

Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Situational Awareness, the artificial intelligence hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut its bitcoin miner holdings sharply in the third quarter, leaving about $80.8 million across three stocks and exiting three others, a Monday filing reveals.
  • It has been revealed that the San Francisco firm still held 3,019,029 CleanSpark shares, worth $38.9 million at Sept.
  • Industry observers note that the deepest cut was IREN.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Situational Awareness, the artificial intelligence hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut its bitcoin miner holdings sharply in the third quarter, leaving about $80.8 million across three stocks and exiting three others, a Monday filing reveals.

It has been revealed that the San Francisco firm still held 3,019,029 CleanSpark shares, worth $38.9 million at Sept. 30, 1,934,618 Bitdeer shares, worth $20.3 million, and 527,864 IREN shares, worth $21.6 million. Those are the only miner lines left, a sliver of the $1.83 billion in six miner stocks the fund listed at June 30.

Industry observers note that the deepest cut was IREN. The fund held 9,474,099 IREN shares, worth $433.3 million, at midyear. The Sept. 30 stake is about 94% smaller by share count. CleanSpark was trimmed about 75%, from 12,276,139 shares worth $178.6 million. Bitdeer was reduced about 44%, from 3,439,450 shares worth $54.6 million. Bitdeer’s reported value fell further than its share count, to $20.3 million, as the stock also declined.

Three names disappeared from the filing entirely. The fund had held 26,008,473 Core Scientific shares, worth $665.6 million, 17,100,000 Riot Platforms shares, worth $468.2 million, and 9,133,726 Hive Digital shares, worth $33.2 million, at June 30. None of those lines appear in the fresh report. The filing does not say whether those sales were part of a late-July portfolio sale, later trades, or both.

Sources indicate that aschenbrenner published a long 2024 essay, “Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead,” arguing that artificial general intelligence was approaching faster than most investors appreciated, and that computing power and electricity would be the tight constraints. He founded the fund that September around that view, looking at technology and energy companies that AI would help or hurt.

The miner stakes fit the same idea. A March profile described the fund as betting that electricity and computing capacity may be the most valuable assets in the AI build-out, pointing to miners that were turning high-density facilities and power contracts toward AI workloads. IREN has signed a multiyear cloud contract with Microsoft. CleanSpark has struck a $6.6 billion data-center lease. Listed miners have also been operating under tight economics this year, with bitcoin often trading below estimated production costs.

It has been revealed that the cuts landed after a brutal July. The fund sold the bulk of the fund’s public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel late that month after heavy losses on AI-related holdings, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources remarked the fund was forced to unwind most of its public book. In a letter to investors, Aschenbrenner said the portfolio was down an estimated 67% in July, that the fund had come “closer to permanent capital impairment than is acceptable,” and that it had sold a portion of its public holdings in a block trade to remove all leverage and close its shorts. The unaudited letter still put year-to-date performance at plus 80%. Aschenbrenner said the fund was not shutting down and had preserved its private investments.

The fresh 13F shows how much of the public book was left by Sept. 30. Reported long holdings fell from $20.24 billion, across 26 lines, at June 30, to $1.58 billion, across 23 lines, three months later. That decline should not be read as the fund losing 92% of its capital. A 13F reports only long positions in U.S.-listed stocks and certain options. It leaves out cash, shorts and private investments, and option lines are valued at the underlying shares, not the premiums paid. Reuters’ sources said that after the Citadel deal the fund would hold a book of roughly $10 billion, including stocks and private investments such as a stake in Anthropic.

What remains is concentrated. The largest common-stock line is now SharonAI, 8,070,950 shares worth $440.7 million. Aschenbrenner also listed call options on Bloom Energy, SanDisk, Nebius and a memory ETF. The three leftover miner stakes are a stub of the midyear book. Whether those positions were trimmed further after Sept. 30 will only be clear when the fourth-quarter 13F arrives in mid-February.

  • CoinGecko described the arrangement as “backing” when it declared the news at Breakpoint in London on the 17th of November.
  • Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted independent ownership as a reason to choose its data service over Binance-owned CoinMarketCap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Solana Foundation now holds a “majority interest” in CoinGecko, its Chief Product Officer Vibhu Norby stated on X.

CoinGecko described the arrangement as “backing” when it declared the news at Breakpoint in London on the 17th of November. Neither announcement gave the exact stake, price, or governance terms.

Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted independent ownership as a reason to choose its data service over Binance-owned CoinMarketCap. It now prepares to explore trading alongside its market data.

The Foundation noted it planned to bring Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko’s website, app, and GeckoTerminal. Notably, CoinGecko said it was still exploring trading features.

It has been revealed that for Solana, that could mean reaching traders where they already look up prices. CoinGecko draws well over 50 million monthly sessions, according to the Foundation.

On the 17th of November, Solana [SOL] recorded $50.44 billion in 30-day DEX spot volume, whereas Ethereum [ETH] recorded $53.86 billion.

Industry observers note that norby also flagged broader coverage of stocks and real-world assets [RWAs]. AMBCrypto reported that Solana’s RWA value reached $5 billion in October.

By the 12th of November, tokenized equity supply stood at $607 million, with xStocks accounting for 75%.

In a recent development, coinGecko’s API guide warned that exchange ownership could raise questions about bias in rankings and trading volumes. AMBCrypto covered similar concerns when Binance bought CoinMarketCap in 2020.

After Norby’s disclosure, an X user called the latest arrangement “a credibility problem.”.

CoinGecko said its methods would stay “transparent, publicly accessible.” Readers can check how it calculates prices, but the announcements leave open who can approve changes to those rules.

In a recent development, brera Holdings disclosed board rights in a separate 2025 deal involving Solmate. A later filing specified that the Foundation could nominate up to two directors, depending on board size. For CoinGecko, board seats and approval rights remain undisclosed.

In a recent development, the largest Shiba Inu traders and investors moved more than 6 billion SHIB to exchange addresses out of the blue, potentially chasing liquidity instead of holding. Sources indicate that it could be a sign, though: according to historical data, whale activity quite often corresponds to market improvements for SHIB. Those whales might have certain data that we don't.

According to recent reports, whenever the price moves up, whales who accumulated previously liquidate their holdings and successfully move on. However, it's not a paramount rule that can't be broken. We might always see a flip in that tendency.

From a holder perspective, acting immediately on transfers like this is most likely not the go-to decision right now. The current composition of the market is far from bullish, but a mere 6 billion transfer isn't going to change the course of SHIB right here and right now.

Retail investors aren't moving on par with those 6 billion, data suggests, as inflow and outflow data show neutrality rather than leaning in one direction or the other.

The timing of the transfer is somewhat interesting: the market isn't recovering, SHIB is losing the ground it has gained in the last few days, and, unfortunately, the SHIB sent to exchanges might contribute to a further price drop.

SHIB is oversold, clearly, but the presence of supply just sitting elsewhere essentially enables the possibility of a quick drop way sooner than we might think.

The key here is the lack of proper psychological and technical levels that might help the price recover or at least form a range.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve spent countless hours here at Electrek doing detailed hands-on testing of hundreds of electric bikes.
  • Below are some of the top e-bikes I’ve hand-tested for every price range, current as of November 2026.
  • This list is divided into several price ranges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve spent countless hours here at Electrek doing detailed hands-on testing of hundreds of electric bikes. Through thousands of miles of riding, I’ve been fortunate to learn these e-bikes inside and out, top to bottom and front to back. That long-term experience with real-world e-bike testing has helped me find the best electric bicycles on the market for just about any budget.

Below are some of the top e-bikes I’ve hand-tested for every price range, current as of November 2026. These are probably the best deals you’ll find all year on electric bikes, meaning this is the best time ever to get a new model! Check out the awesome e-bikes below, any one of which could become your next electric bike.

This list is divided into several price ranges. We’ll start with the best e-bikes under $1,000, then move on to the under-$2,000 category, under-$3,000 category, etc. The goal is to highlight some of my favorite models in various budget ranges to help you make the right decision based on your needs and budget.

The sub-$1,000 electric bike category is critical for a few reasons.

First, it’s pretty hard to produce a quality e-bike and sell it for under $1k. Most of the options in this price category make too many sacrifices in quality or longevity to earn a spot on this list as one of “the best.”.

Second, many newly curious e-bike buyers just aren’t prepared to drop several thousand dollars on a brand-newly introduced concept, making this price range critical for many new e-bike shoppers.

Fortunately, we’ve found some excellent options for cheap electric bikes that can still save you some serious dough.

The Lectric XP LITE 3.0 was recently updated and is now quite likely the king of bang-for-your-buck electric bikes.

Recent findings suggest that for a while now, the $999 Lectric XP 4 has reigned supreme in the budget electric bike category. That’s still a great bike, and we’ll discuss it next, but the more affordable $799 Lectric XP LITE3 is an even more wallet-friendly electric bike.

That new e-bike offers some great riding at under 800 bucks.

It has been revealed that it’s a throttle-enabled Class 2 folding electric bike with 20″ wheels, a max speed of 20 mph (32 km/h), and a motor rated for 300W continuous and 819W peak. It’s not going to be the strongest hill climber in this list, but it does get going quickly on flat and modestly hilly terrain.

It has been revealed that and the biggest features include quality hydraulic disc brakes, color LCD screen, turn signals, and even an optional Gates carbon belt drive system for an extra $100. Riders can also opt for a nearly double-sized battery for an extra $200.

This is the only e-bike in this price range that I know of with a 48V electrical system. All the other budget e-bikes under $800 use a 36V system and thus suffer from weaker power.

There are some things that you give up with this model, such as that the fenders aren’t included free. But for just $799, you’re still getting built-in lights, a hidden battery, large color LCD display and a lightweight folder. Plus it comes in lots of fun color options.

The Lectric XP4 is the undisputed best-selling electric bike in the US. The bike has racked up massive sales figures as riders flock to its extreme bang-for-your-buck. Simply put, it’s hard to find any other e-bike that offers this level of value!

The XP4 can get riders up to 28 mph (45 km/h) and now comes in either a 500W or 750W version, with respective battery sizes of 48V 10.4Ah and 48V 17.5Ah. The long-range version’s premium price tag ($1,299 vs the standard range model at $999) is perhaps even higher value than the already impressive base model.

Other upgrades include a upcoming stronger rack design, torque sensor for smoother pedal assist, and improved hardware like the 8-speed transmission, hydraulic disc brakes, updated urban/trail hybrid-style tire tread, and a beautiful new TFT color screen.

The XP4 is hands-down the highest value e-bike I’ve ever tested and it’s quite obvious just how much time and effort went into building such a potent e-bike designed to fit so many different riders and tasks.

It’s hard to find a better combination of low cost and high performance anywhere in the e-bike market right now.

According to recent reports, when Ride1Up introduced the original Portola, it was pretty obvious what the game plan was: fire a shot across Lectric Ebike’s bow with a direct competitor to the Lectric XP line. By all accounts, Ride1Up nailed it with an impressive competitor. Now the tech giant has come back with the next generation of the bike, this time attempting to take on both the XP line and XP Lite from Lectric. That’s thanks to two models, the Portola 02, and the stripped-down Portola 02 Lite.

The Ride1Up Portola 02 has a lot more going for it than just the attractive starting price of $895 for the Lite or $995 for the full-size bike with frame-integrated rack. The models offer great performance with a maximum speed of 28 mph (45 km/h) and good quality components including hydraulic disc brakes, torque sensor, front suspension, a built-in rear rack (except for the Lite), and a 750W motor.

There are two battery options available, either a 48V 10Ah or a 48V 15Ah, and the larger battery only costs an extra $100, so it’s quite worth the extra 50% range.

I love the sleek-looking frame and apparently, I’m not alone. Those who are on the hunt for a good-looking folding fat tire e-bike that doesn’t break the bank will likely find this to be one of the more fashionable options.

Once you bump up above the $1,000 limit, you start to see many more great options for e-bikes in a wide range of categories.

From electric cargo bikes to cruisers and even electric mopeds, there’s something for everyone in this price range.

The $1,249 JackRabbit OG2 is in one of these fuzzy areas between e-bikes and other e-rideables. In this case, it straddles the line between an electric bike and an electric scooter.

It more or less feels like an electric bike based on its ride geometry. However, the lack of pedals means that it could also be classified as an electric scooter, albeit a large-wheeled e-scooter.

It has been revealed that but with those 20-inch wheels and bicycle seat, the JackRabbit OG2 rides much more like a small folding e-bike than an e-scooter. And its electronics match that of a light e-bike, too.

The 300W motor gets the little runabout up to 20 mph (32 km/h). The small 158 Wh battery only offers around 10 miles (approximately 16 km) of range, but is also conveniently small enough to easily keep a spare battery in a cargo pocket or even a small purse.

According to recent reports, the biggest benefit of the JackRabbit is that it is so simple that the lack of frills keeps the weight down to just 25 lb (11.3 kg)! For an e-bike, that’s almost so light that it floats.

It has been revealed that the organization also released a higher power and larger battery capacity version too, which might be good for riders who want to push harder and go farther. For those that want to see a few more upgrades on this minimalist e-bike, the JackRabbit OG2 and XG might be more your size.

See my full review of the JackRabbit OG2 here.

We called the Lectric XPedition e-cargo bike a runaway success right from the start, and that’s exactly what it turned into. Now with the latest Lectric XPedition 2.0 on the road, it’s better than ever.

With heavy-hauling weight capacity, the option for one or two batteries for extra long range, hydraulic disc brakes and torque sensor-based intuitive feeling pedal assist, this e-bike is dragging electric cargo bikes into the future.

The $1,399 Lectric XPedition 2.0 has turned the electric cargo bike market upside down, bringing a heavy-hitting cargo e-bike to market for an ultra-affordable price.

While it’s not the fanciest cargo e-bike on the market (you’ll find those in the $4,000-$6,000 price range further down this article), it’s definitely the best bang for your buck thanks to a combination of high value parts and reasonable pricing.

Lectric XPedition 2.0 quick specs:.

According to recent reports, the Heybike Ranger 3 Pro is probably one of the best deals in full-suspension folding e-bikes right now. With a combination of a powerful motor, comfortable geometry, front & rear suspension, and a high-tech interface that includes NFC card unlocking, the Heybike Ranger 3 Pro is punching above its weight class.

In fact, that’s its main drawback, its weight. It’s a heavy bike, but the speed and power mean heavier motors and batteries, so you know you’re going to be carrying a more robust powertrain around with you.

But between the performance and the looks, this is one awesome comfortable ride that just doesn’t break the bank! I had a blast reviewing it, and I’ll bet you’ll have a blast riding it!

Heybike Ranger 3.0 Pro quick specs.

The $1,399 Aventon Soltera.2 is the latest version of Aventon’s beautiful city bike that offers some of the best quality fabrication that I’ve seen in this price range – or even in higher price ranges. It is offered in either a single-speed or seven-speed format.

The bike rolls on narrow tires for that efficient city ride, while still packing in a 500W motor.

The battery is a bit smaller at 36V and 10Ah, but the bike makes up for a smaller battery by being able to integrate it into the frame in a sleek and attractive package.

In a recent development, the beautiful color display also adds to the bike’s charm, as do the powerful headlight and frame-integrated tail light. There’s even an awesome companion app that lets your phone track your bike’s important stats. Basically, you’re getting a lot for $1,199 here!

Check out my in-depth Aventon Soltera.2 review here.

In a recent development, ride1Up has proven itself as a high-value electric bike brand, focusing largely on efficient and speedy commuter e-bikes. While the company has many models in the $1,000 to $2,000 range, the $1,295 Ride1Up Roadster V3 is one of the best bang-for-your-buck options in the lightweight category.

Industry observers note that this 500W-rated e-bike offers Class 3 performance, meaning you can hit speeds of up to 28 mph (45 km/h), or a still impressive 20 mph (32 km/h) if using the throttle. But sticking to pedal-assist means you get to enjoy that quality torque sensor for smoother pedaling. The bike even comes with an option for either a belt drive or a 10-speed Shimano transmission, and three frame sizes to choose from.

In a recent development, the V3’s design was updated with many newly introduced features, including a now-removable battery for even more convenient charging both on and off the bike. And with a sub-40 lb weight, it’s hard to beat this one on a pound-for-pound basis!

Ride1Up Roadster V3 quick specs:.

Check out my full review of the Ride1Up Roadster V3 here:.

Lectric Ebikes expanded into larger territory with the launch of the Lectric XPeak2. It was the tech giant’s first e-bike with a larger than 20″ wheel size, bringing some chunky 26×4.0″ tires into the company’s inventory.

In a recent development, the XPeak takes the form of a typical adventure-style fat tire electric bike. It features a hardtail design with a suspension fork, high-volume tires, hydraulic disc brakes, and a relatively large battery that is certified by the Swiss testing agency SGS to meet UL 2849 standards.

According to recent reports, the bike is also tested to higher standards for ruggedness of the frame and fork than most e-bikes in this price range, meaning it’s likely going to last longer too. As far as fat tire adventure-style e-bikes go, there’s no better bang for your buck than the Lectric XPeak2.

The $2,295 Ride1Up Prodigy V2 Eco has brought newly introduced meaning to the phrase “low-cost mid-drive electric bike”, updating an already impressive e-bike with a new next-gen setup.

This e-bike sports a high-end German-manufactured Brose mid-drive motor and can hit speeds of up to 28 mph (45 km/h), yet is price similarly to much cheaper hub motor-based electric bikes.

It’s a perfect commuter e-bike for someone who wants high-quality parts like that German mid-drive motor with 90Nm of torque, hydraulic disc brakes, bright LED lights, included fenders, rear rack, and a very comfortable saddle. Plus, there’s a choice between a step-over or a mid-step frame to better fit a wider variety of riders.

Sources indicate that this e-bike is easily worth another $700 more than the price tag, if not more. In fact, you’ll find many of these same components on e-bikes with $2,000-$3,000 price tags all over the place. So if you’re looking for a higher quality e-bike that doesn’t cost as much as a fancy bike shop e-bike, this is the one to consider.

Ride1Up Prodigy V2 Eco quick specs:.

The Ride1Up Vorsa is Ride1Up’s most versatile “SUV‑style” e‑bike yet, designed to transition seamlessly from commuting through city streets to loaded errands and light gravel or park paths. With a standard price around US $1,495, it delivers an exceptionally high‑value riding experience that often outperforms models far above its price range.

It has been revealed that with a powerful 750 W rear‑hub motor producing a hefty 95 Nm of torque (and peaking over 1,400 W in real-world tests), the Vorsa accelerates comfortably and can maintain Class 3 speeds of up to 28 mph via pedal assist or 20 mph throttle thanks to its dual-sensor system and customizable display. Whether you’re hauling cargo or cruising commute lanes, the Vorsa delivers smooth, responsive power that feels natural and planted.

Industry observers note that I love how well‑rounded the package is. Ride1Up outfits the Vorsa with a 100 mm suspension fork, comfortable ergonomic bars, multiple colors/frame styles (step‑thru or standard), and a modular rear rack rated for 440 lb total payload, which is expandable via Connect+ accessories. Hydraulic disc brakes, full fenders, integrated lighting, and passive features like UL‑certified batteries and Apple FindMy integration round out the build.

At just $1,695, the Ride1Up Vorsa is priced way below fair market value, which makes this an absolute steal of a deal.

Check out my Ride1Up Vorsa review here, and also check out the latest expansion to the Vorsa line with lighter and heavier duty models built on the Vorsa platform.

The Marker is the first model unveiled by the e-bike brand spun out of Lectric eBikes, known as Monarc. The brand leverages Lectric’s size and buying power to bring higher end bikes than we typically see in the budget space – complete with higher shelf components – but at better prices and with better customer service.

The Monarc Marker is a powerful, Class 3-capable fat tire adventure e-bike with powerful four-piston brakes, a quality reverse arch suspension fork, Shimano CUES transmission, and comes with two batteries, all for an incredible reasonable MSRP of US $1,999.

Monarc also made waves by offering a 5-year warranty as well as 12-hour customer service five days a week, ensuring customers feel comfortable knowing they are buying from a company that will stick around to support riders long after the purchase is complete.

Learn more about the Monarc Marker here, or check out its current sale price here.

When Juiced returned with a vengeance after being saved by Lectric, the brand did so with two impressive fresh Scrambler models: a hard tail and a full-suspension bike. They’re both awesome moped-style e-bikes and handle great, but the full-suspension version definitely kicks things up a notch and allows for even wilder riding.

Sources indicate that but since they share the same features and performance outside the rear suspension, either would make an awesome addition to your e-bike fleet. Basically, it’s a powerful yet street-legal e-bike that is designed for real-world riding, thanks in no small part to its designer, Austin Homes, being a seasoned competitive bike racer across multiple disciplines and bringing that keen eye to the Scrambler’s development.

By the time you surpass the $2,000 mark, you’re starting to get into serious e-bikes with serious performance or build quality.

If you’re spending this much, you’ll want to ensure you’re buying from a reputable company with top-notch products and service.

The Ride1Up TraiRush is the first actually quite good electric mountain bike that comes in at a budget price. It gives you a real German-made Brose motor, which offers good power matched with whisper-quiet performance. You get a dropper seat post and Maxxis Minion tires, Tektro Orion quad-piston hydraulic disc brakes, and a 120mm Rockshox Judy Silver TK Air Fork.

The first time I took a ride on the Ride1Up TrailRush, I couldn’t believe just how good the bike felt, especially from a company known for its wide array of commuter and street-oriented electric bikes. But Ride1Up was founded by cyclists at heart, and so they know what it means to build a good bike, regardless of category. At $2,095, this is a steal for just great parts.

In a recent development, I love the $3,299 Priority Current electric bike so much that it has become one of my daily riders. It’s the one I grab when I’m doing city riding and I know I want to be pedaling.

While the original version was already a great bike, the upcoming Current Plus adds some key improvements, such as an included throttle and a nearly 50% larger capacity battery for more range. The throttle is great in a pinch, but the bike is also just so much fun to pedal thanks to a torque sensor-based pedal assist that provides natural-feeling assistance up to a fast 28 mph top speed.

The internally geared rear hub combined with a Gates belt drive system and powerful hydraulic disc brakes make this a very nice e-bike for the price. Plus that mid-drive motor offers tons of torque (140 Nm!) for climbing hills or accelerating quickly.

I’m also a fan of the built-in lights and included fenders, not to mention the punchy hydraulic disc brakes and Goodyear tires.

Mid-drive electric bikes aren’t cheap, but the price is definitely a fair one for this e-bike.

Priority Current Plus quick specs:.

Recent findings suggest that I’m not normally a carbon fiber, drop bar, race bike kind of guy. But then again, that’s usually because those types of bikes are way out of my price range… until now.

The Ride1Up CF Racer1 brings carbon fiber road e-bikes to the common man, offering both a traditional road bike and a gravel bike edition.

At under 29 lb (13 kg), these e-bikes are some of the lightest around. I picked one up with my index finger and was shocked at how easily it left the ground.

Industry observers note that to get there, that meant a relatively low-power motor and a smaller battery were required. But for the folks that ride these types of bikes, a major motor and heavy battery probably aren’t on their wishlist anyway. Instead, a simple extra boost, as if you’ve always got a tailwind, helps augment your own pedaling.

For just $2,295, there’s no better deal out there for a budget-friendly carbon fiber road e-bike.

This full-suspension electric moped-style e-bike is a masterclass in high performance electric bike design. Sure, it’s an obvious SUPER73 imitation, but it’s a really well done imitation.

It handles well, it’s got great rubber between you and the road, the suspension gives a comfortable ride, and it’s got plenty of extra power.

In a recent development, despite the 750W label, the e-bike can be unlocked to make use of nearly 1,500W of peak power. I was able to reach a top speed of 37 mph (59.5 km/h) during my testing (not on public streets!).

But the bike ships in Class 2 mode with a 750W limit and 20 mph (32 km/h) maximum speed, meaning you’ll have to contact the firm to request an unlock for the bike to be used above Class 2 speeds and power levels.

All in all, the $2,395 Ride1Up REVV1 FS is an amazing e-bike for anyone who wants a moped-style ride with full-suspension, high quality 4-piston hydraulic disc brakes and a design that rides almost like a motorcycle, yet in a bike form factor.

Check out my complete Ride1Up REVV1 FS review here.

Recent findings suggest that the Tern Quick Haul is an electric cargo bike from the famed cargo e-bike manufacturer Tern. It holds the distinction of being the most affordable model in Tern’s lineup.

Recent findings suggest that that states a lot, because Tern is known for its high-quality e-bikes that are built to be ridden every day for real-world errands, carpool duty, and more. These e-bikes are meant to replace cars, and they do just that for many riders. With a huge list of accessories, you can outfit a Quick Haul for just about any job.

The Tern Quick Haul features a mid-drive Bosch motor, hydraulic disc brakes, Tern’s vertical parking rack, and a relatively lightweight but high utility design that is meant to carry just about anything in your life.

We had the chance to test a pair of Quick Hauls at Eurobike in Frankfurt last year, which you can learn more about here.

Motor: Bosch Active Line Plus mid-drive motorTop speed: 20 mph (32 km/h) with pedal assist (no throttle)Range: Up to 60 miles (96 km), less when riding in highest powerBattery: 400Wh, removable/lockableWeight: 50 lb (22.8 kg)Price: $2,999.

When it comes to fast, powerful electric mopeds on a budget, it’s hard to compete with the $2,399 Ariel Rider X-Class. This is the e-bike I usually recommend when someone simply wants the most power and speed for the least amount of money.

It has been revealed that the impressive performance comes from a powerful 1,000W motor that actually puts out closer to 2,000W of peak power. It can be limited to 20 mph if you’d like, but I got it up to 36 mph in unlimited mode.

The bike rolls on 20″ moto-style wheels and comes with nice parts including hydraulic disc brakes, a bench seat, dual suspension, and a big moto-style headlight.

You can see my full review of the Ariel Rider 52V X-Class here.

The Xtracycle Hopper is something of a Goldilocks cargo bike, in my opinion. It’s not as substantial as a traditional long tail cargo bike, but it’s still big enough to carry multiple kids or a week’s worth of groceries.

It’s also not as pricey as the expensive $5-7k bike shop cargo e-bikes, yet it’s much higher quality than the typical direct-to-consumer cargo e-bikes.

I’ve tested it for all sorts of cargo jobs and even put my friends and family on it to take their kids to school and let me know how it works for them. Everyone has come away impressed with the ride feel, which seems much more like a traditional bike than a bulky cargo bike.

For the money, the Xtracycle Hopper offers incredible value and much higher quality construction than you’d get with entry-level brands.

Check out my full Xtracycle Hopper review here.

Above $3.5k, you’re entering some seriously dedicated e-bike territory.

These e-bikes either feature top-shelf components like drivetrain and brake parts, or pack in so much power that they couldn’t possibly be priced any lower.

Either way, you’re not in Kansas anymore. You’re heading down the e-bike rabbit hole.

Tern is renowned for building high-quality electric bikes that double down on utility features. The newly updated Tern HSD is the company’s more affordable utility e-bike, offering many features you’ll find on its higher-end GSD but at a price that more riders can stomach.

Recent findings suggest that the HSD uses small 20″ wheels and includes a folding stem, making it nice and compact. But taking it one step further, Tern outfitted it with its innovative rack that lets you park the bike on its tail, meaning it takes up barely more space than a coat rack in the corner of a room.

The bike’s Bosch mid-drive and high capacity batteries provide a high-end e-bike drive, and they are matched with a variety of performance drivetrain options that you can select from, depending on how high you want to spec the bike.

Whether you’re ferrying around kids or buying a week’s worth of groceries, the HSD is a solid option.

Check out my detailed first ride experience on the Tern HSD here.

The Xtracycle Swoop ASM is one of those electric cargo bikes that makes you rethink the entire category.

Not only does it include high-quality components and fancy features like automatic shifting paired with a high-end Shimano mid-drive motor, but it also just feels like you’re riding a normal-sized bike instead of a long and awkward cargo e-bike.

Sources indicate that I found I can even ride it without my hands on the bars because it tracks so straight and rides so stable. That’s a feat you can’t pull off with most budget cargo e-bikes since they aren’t designed with proper bicycle geometry. But Xtracycle is a true cyclist’s cargo e-bike tech giant, and so they understand proper bicycle design.

Check out my full review of this incredibly high-end and comfortable-to-ride cargo e-bike here.

Xtracycle Swoop ASM quick specs:.

When it comes to all-wheel-drive electric bikes, the $3,299 Ariel Rider Grizzly is one of my favorites.

This incredible e-bike is really more of a small electric motorcycle. It uses two high-power motors – one in each wheel – to offer speeds in the mid-30s and acceleration that will get you there in the blink of an eye.

Recent findings suggest that full suspension and hydraulic disc brakes make this an e-bike that handles well at any speed, and the bright red paint job looks as aggressive as the e-bike feels. It even comes with footpegs pre-installed so you can carry a passenger with you.

Plus it’s got double batteries to feed those two power-hungry motors, so you’ll be able to ride this e-bike pretty darn far too, as long as you aren’t too demanding from the throttle.

Check out my full in-depth review of the epic Ariel Rider Grizzly e-bike here.

Ariel Rider Grizzly quick specs:.

The Priority Skyline builds upon Priority Bicycles’ legacy of creating high-performance, low-maintenance e-bikes and ups the ante with more premium parts than we’ve ever seen on a Priority e-bike before.

It has been revealed that the show stopper here is the inclusion of Pinion’s 12-speed automatic gearbox, which smartly shifts gears without the rider ever having to think about it. You can personalize your shift points to dial in the ride, and let the centrally-mounted gearbox do the rest. The carbon belt drive transfers your pedal power while a 750W rear hub motor brings the extra power riders need.

There are also high-quality hydraulic brakes, a great suspension fork, and a substantial battery for long range in the city. Rear rack and complete fenders come standard, as do the built-in LED lights and adjustable handle-bar stem.

See my full review of the Priority Bicycles Skyline here.

Priority Bicycles Skyline quick specs:.

You just couldn’t stop, could you? I indicated you plenty of awesome e-bikes that didn’t cost most of a paycheck. But you just haaaaaaad to keep going.

Fine, here they are. These are some of the most expensive e-bikes out there that we’ve tested and that I’d actually recommend someone buying, if you can pony up the cash.

When it comes to ultra-premium folding electric bikes, there’s only one name that comes to my mind: GoCycle. These are the most impressive folding e-bikes I’ve ever seen. And they better be – they were designed by a former McLaren engineer.

Between the carbon fiber work, single-sided wheels, high-tech tires, trippy LED dot display, innovative rear suspension, and completely enclosed drivetrain, there’s a lot of high-end stuff going on here.

In a recent development, the speed will vary from 15-20 mph depending on which country you buy the bike in, but the performance is only part of the equation. The quick folding and light, compact design of the e-bike is the real winner here.

Check out my full review of the GoCycle G4i+ here.

Industry observers note that the FREY EX Pro is a high-end electric mountain bike with crazy high power. It uses the same motor as the CSC FT1000MD we featured above (the Bafang M620 mid-drive), but cranks up the current to provide closer to 1,500W of power.

In a recent development, it’s enough to destroy chains if you aren’t careful. We know. Several of us here at Electrek have done it.

The FREY EX Pro not only features high-end parts like a RockShox Lyric fork and Magura MT5e hydraulic brakes, but it even comes with dual batteries so you can ride farther and stay on the trails longer.

I’ve personally taken this e-bike back UP a downhill mountain bike course – that’s how powerful it is.

It may be expensive, but it saves you several thousand dollars compared to many European electric mountain bikes with similar components but a fraction of the power in the FREY.

See my full review of the FREY EX Pro here.

Sources indicate that the Tern GSD improves upon the Tern HSD with even more capability and even nicer components. There are multiple versions that can take you up to nearly $10k, but even the lower-tier versions are not “low tier,” if you know what I mean.

Parts like automatically engaging electric locks, 10-speed Shimano Deore transmissions, Magura MT5e quad-piston hydraulic disc brakes, and more set these e-bikes apart from the rest of the pack.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re getting a Tern GSD, you’re getting a fully qualified car replacement. There are many people who use these instead of buying a second car. When you look at it like that, the price suddenly seems pretty reasonable.

Check out our full review of the Tern GSD here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin climbed to about $64,600 after Nvidia beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations Tuesday, then gave back most of the gain within 35 minutes.
  • In its first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s departure, Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, up 103% from a year earlier, and topping the $109.1 billion Bloomberg analyst consensus.
  • It has been revealed that nvidia projected $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3%, above the $125.2 billion analyst estimate Yahoo Finance reported.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin climbed to about $64,600 after Nvidia beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations Tuesday, then gave back most of the gain within 35 minutes.

In its first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s departure, Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, up 103% from a year earlier, and topping the $109.1 billion Bloomberg analyst consensus.

It has been revealed that nvidia projected $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3%, above the $125.2 billion analyst estimate Yahoo Finance reported. The forecast covers a quarter with an extra week and assumes zero data center compute revenue from China.

Nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation effective Nov. 11 and disclosed it Nov. 12, according to the company’s SEC filing. Colette Kress took over as interim CEO while retaining her job as chief financial officer.

Nvidia released the figures at 4:20 p.m. ET, and Bitcoin traded close to $64,000 at the end of the one-minute interval before the report. It touched $64,602.98 during the 4:33 p.m. minute and was back to $64,246.47 by 4:55 p.m., still about $244 above its pre-release level.

According to recent reports, separately, Nvidia traded at $157.83 at 4:56:47 p.m. ET, up 1.52% from its $155.46 regular-session close.

Coinbase BTC/USD one-minute closing trades on Nov. 17, 2026. The first point is the trade immediately before Nvidia’s 4:20 p.m. ET release. Intraminute highs are outside this closing-price series.

Source: Coinbase Exchange BTC/USD candles · Coinbase Exchange candle definitions · Nvidia release timestamp.

In research published before Nvidia’s earnings, Glassnode found that losses from coins sold below their purchase price had reached levels seen around previous market lows, relative to profits over the preceding year.

Sources indicate that its model estimated that the Nov. 13-14 liquidations had cleared most leveraged long positions stacked above $62,000, leaving fewer of those previously mapped positions vulnerable to forced closure.

Sources indicate that glassnode estimated that about 20% of short-term holders’ coins had been acquired between $62,000 and $66,000. Within 5% of Bitcoin’s market price, the Binance and Coinbase order books highlighted about 2.3 times as much buy-side as sell-side liquidity.

Recent findings suggest that traders can withdraw those orders, so order book size only indicates how much buying might materialize. If the lower edge of the range gives way, Glassnode pointed to the June low near $58,500 and the aggregate realized price near $53,700, based on the prices at which coins last moved.

Bitcoin traded near $64,246 on Coinbase 35 minutes after Nvidia’s release, inside Glassnode’s $62,000–$66,000 cost-basis band for recent buyers.

At 4:55 p.m. ET, Bitcoin still sat well below the $74,100 level where short-term holders as a group would break even.

Industry observers note that the spot marker shows one exchange. The levels below the band are conditional references from Glassnode’s Nov. 17 analysis.

According to recent reports, glassnode’s Nov. 17 Bitcoin levels share a linear USD scale. The highlighted spot marker is the $64,246.47 close of Coinbase’s 4:54 p.m. ET bucket, rounded to the nearest dollar and displayed as of 4:55 p.m. ET.

It has been revealed that the spot marker demonstrates one exchange. The levels below the band are conditional references from Glassnode’s Nov. 17 analysis.

Glassnode also reported that the Coinbase premium, the difference between Bitcoin’s price on the exchange and its global price, turned positive around the weekend low before slipping back to a small discount.

Stablecoin supply fell 4.2% over 90 days while three-month Treasury bill yields rose about 45 basis points over that same period, making bills a more attractive place to hold cash.

US-traded spot Bitcoin ETFs also saw substantial withdrawals in the run-up to the report, as Glassnode reported $2.6 billion in net outflows over ten sessions.

Farside Investors’ daily totals added about $2.35 billion in withdrawals over that period, followed by a $7.9 million net inflow on Nov. 16. A longer run of ETF inflows and buyers consistently paying a premium on Coinbase would give the bounce more support.

At $74,100, Glassnode estimates that short-term holders as a group would break even, and Bitcoin’s initial move after Nvidia’s report left it well below that level.

  • Customers on MEXC’s global exchange can’t use their platform-issued debit cards following an issuer problem.
  • It has been revealed that the exchange announced that its Global Card service ends today, November 18, 2026, at 15:30 UTC after its third-party card issuer made service adjustments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Blitz news » MEXC Pulls The Plug On VISA Card Months After Launch.

Customers on MEXC’s global exchange can’t use their platform-issued debit cards following an issuer problem.

It has been revealed that the exchange announced that its Global Card service ends today, November 18, 2026, at 15:30 UTC after its third-party card issuer made service adjustments. Existing cards will no longer process transactions and fresh applications are suspended.

The virtual Visa card introduced on August 31 with features that included up to 10% USDT cashback and high spending limits. It lasted under three months.

MEXC Global Card Service Update We regret to announce that, following service adjustments by our third-party card issuer, MEXC Global Card services will be discontinued on Nov 18, 2026, at 15:30 UTC. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. We remain… pic.twitter.com/QXLFMeRvd7.

The shutdown follows the earlier discontinuation of MEXC’s APAC Card on November 11 over similar issuer complications, and it comes after a temporary maintenance pause that began on November 14.

Cardholders can still withdraw their remaining balances to their MEXC Fiat account before the cutoff.

Any funds left on the card will be snapshotted on November 21 at 15:30 UTC and credited to Spot accounts within three business days.

Refunds for prior transactions will go to Fiat accounts once received, pending cashback continues on schedule, and people are advised to cancel or switch any recurring payments tied to the card.

MEXC has not identified the card issuer or detailed the exact nature of the adjustments. Funds are not frozen; they are being returned to owners’ exchange accounts.

In a recent development, XRP’s price dipped under $1, and most of the market looks ready to walk away. Not the whales, though. At least not yet.

Is that enough to stop the fall?

According to recent reports, according to recent data, XRP whales have taken out more than $127 million in XRP off Binance since 10th November. Net outflows went between $12-$33 million over the past week, including about $21 million on the 16th alone!

Not too long ago, it was the other way around.

Recent findings suggest that in August, XRP went up by about 72% and back above $1.50. Whales were dumping as much as $75 million on Binance in a single day!

According to recent reports, if you look further back, you’ll see that XRP hit $3.55 in the summer of 2025. In that time, some days saw more than $100 million flood in.

One day even hit close to $270 million.

When coins leave an exchange, people usually want to hold. However, don’t get excited yet. Some of this might just be Binance moving its money around.

Remember when it was topping up its reserves after the October hack?

The rest of the market isn’t seeing it the way the whales are yet.

XRP closed last week at about $0.97 on the charts. That hinted at its lowest weekly close in two years. It even dipped as low all the way down to $0.89 during the week.

Recent findings suggest that still, it’s worth thinking. This is where XRP broke out in 2024, right before it sprinted past $3.60.

Futures traders don’t seem to want to be here. The OI dropped from about $1.05 billion on the 9th to around $752 million at press time. Funding went from red on the 14th and to a slim green at 0.0013%.

ETFs haven’t been helping either; $19.1 million in outflows between 9th and 13th November.

Everyone except whales have been heading for the door.

So, here’s the thing. If whales keep taking XRP out of Binance, there isn’t enough of them to be sold. That could help turn $1 into a floor.

Sources indicate that or the rest of the market could drag XRP down anyway. Only time will tell.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The Single Asset Vault amendment on the XRP Ledger is getting closer to activation on the mainnet as validator support builds for the network’s preparation to enable better DeFi functionality.

According to data from XRPScan, the SingleAssetVault amendment, or XLS-65, has received yes votes from 25 of 35 trusted validators, currently standing at 71.43% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of 35 votes (29) to start its 14-day countdown to activation. That means it needs four more votes to get there and could reach the magic number before the end of 2026.

The XRP Ledger’s amendment process requires a proposed amendment to be approved by more than 80% of trusted validators for 14 days before it is implemented. Validator support may shift during this time, and if the required 80% threshold is lost, activation may be delayed.

The Single Asset Vault amendment creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. The amendment introduces a Vault object that defines the state of a tokenized vault, and the Vault entry is one of the ledger entry types it provides.

The Vault object holds vital information such as available assets, shares, total value, and other relevant information. Consumers can create a Vault object with the VaultCreate transaction; the Vault object is tracked in an Owner Directory owned by the Vault Owner account.

The XRP Ledger lending amendment has gained additional yes votes. According to XRPScan, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, also known as XLS-66, has received 24 yes votes out of 35 trusted validators, meaning it has 68.57% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of the 35 votes (29) to trigger a 14-day activation countdown.

This implies that there are five votes left for it to reach this threshold, with the possibility of it securing the required number of votes before the end of 2026 as well.

According to XRP enthusiasts, LendingProtocolV1_1 represents the biggest amendment for unlocking capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger and is anticipated by institutional and retail people.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ripple contributed 126.8 million XRP to Evernorth at a recorded value of zero, according to a Nov. 17 SEC filing.

The disclosure adds another wrinkle to the valuation of Evernorth's XRP treasury, which has already suffered roughly $505 million in cumulative write-downs.

In a recent development, the zero-cost lot reflects the basis inherited from Ripple, while the impairment reflects reductions in the carrying amount of Evernorth's historical XRP position. Neither figure establishes what the combined business is worth today.

According to recent reports, evernorth's Sept. 30 financial statements report 346.3 million XRP with an original cost of $846.6 million and a carrying amount of $341.9 million.

Only $6.9 million of impairment was recognized in the third quarter. The nine-month charge was $271 million, while the rest of the cumulative reduction predates 2026.

Under the policy disclosed in the filing, later price recoveries do not reverse the written-down basis, so the gap between book value and market value can persist.

The latest amendment clarifies the distinction by adding financial statements for Pathfinder, Evernorth's XRP-holding subsidiary, and updated combined pro forma accounts.

Industry observers note that pathfinder's statements remarked Ripple contributed 126,791,458 XRP on Oct. 19, 2025. Because the transfer was a transaction between entities under common control, Pathfinder recognized the tokens at Ripple's historical carrying value, which was zero.

The statements also report a merger-related transfer of 346.5 million XRP from Evernorth to Pathfinder. Adding that transfer to Ripple's historical contribution reconstructs approximately 473.3 million XRP from the two disclosed transactions.

It has been revealed that the combined pro forma accounts continue historical-cost-less-impairment treatment without a fair-value adjustment. They show $342.2 million of net digital assets, a carrying amount based on that accounting policy.

In a recent development, A cumulative write-down reduces one historical lot's recorded cost. Ripple's separate contribution inherits a zero carrying basis.

Book value and current market value require separate measurements.

Historical dates differ: Evernorth balances at September 30, 2026; Ripple contribution October 19, 2025. Zero means inherited book value. No current inventory, NAV or per-share figure is calculated.

Sources indicate that reported cost $846,575,043 less carrying value $341,887,231 = cumulative impairment $504,687,812. Blue bar width is 341887231/846575043 (40.3848%); remainder 59.6152%. Display rounds to USD millions and XRP millions. The separate Ripple contribution is shown as a process, not on the dollar scale.

Historical dates differ: Evernorth balances at September 30, 2026; Ripple contribution October 19, 2025. Zero means inherited book value. No current inventory, NAV or per-share figure is calculated.

It has been revealed that the 10-Q describes Evernorth's ownership of Pathfinder common units as approximately 71.5%. For the Oct. 9 closing, the pro forma table separately reports 55 million Evernorth shares across both classes and 23 million outside Pathfinder units.

As of Nov. 9, Evernorth reported 58.4 million Class A and Class C shares. Evernorth defines its XRP-per-share KPI as tokens attributable to the public parent divided by the combined number of shares in both classes.

According to recent reports, the pro forma balance sheet reports $76 million in cash and $46.3 million in total liabilities, including a $30 million convertible note. It also presents $229.5 million of redeemable noncontrolling interest separately.

The balance sheet presents that outside interest separately from debt, and the note is already included in total liabilities.

The 10-Q subsequently reports $35.3 million in gross warrant proceeds through Nov. 9, plus 8.7 million warrants still outstanding at an $11.50 exercise price. The convertible note can also accrue 4% payment-in-kind interest and has conversion provisions.

The next useful valuation comparison needs a common date for XRP inventory, Evernorth's economic ownership, cash, liabilities, and the share count, with potential dilution shown separately.

The amendment explains why a large write-down and a zero-book-value XRP lot can coexist, while a current market valuation still requires the dated financial bridge.

Data reveals that the XRP ETFs managed by Canary Capital and Grayscale recorded combined withdrawals of $6.14 million during their latest trading session on November 17.

Notably, the fund recorded over 5 million XRP, worth about $5.01 million, in daily outflows, while Grayscale's XRP ETF followed with just $1.12 million in outflows.

Although Bitwise did not record any inflow or outflow on this day, the firm still stands as XRP’s biggest ETF manager as it controls over $392.64 million in net assets as of this date.

Despite its dominance in the XRP ETF market, Bitwise has remained muted all week, showing zero daily participation since November 9, when it posted its highest-ever daily outflow of $9.40 million.

Bitcoin miners found a way to profit without mining BTC, but the advantage may not last

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Surging Texas electricity prices made shutting down more profitable than mining Bitcoin for some operators in early November.
  • The disruption contributed to Bitcoin's 9.13% mining difficulty reduction on Nov.
  • 17 analysis, mining services firm Luxor found that West Texas electricity prices exceeded the mining revenue of a machine operating at 25 joules per terahash during 45% of the hours between Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surging Texas electricity prices made shutting down more profitable than mining Bitcoin for some operators in early November.

The disruption contributed to Bitcoin's 9.13% mining difficulty reduction on Nov. 14, its largest since June, as expensive electricity forced miners to reconsider whether keeping their machines running was worthwhile.

In a recent development, in a Nov. 17 analysis, mining services firm Luxor found that West Texas electricity prices exceeded the mining revenue of a machine operating at 25 joules per terahash during 45% of the hours between Oct. 29 and Nov. 14. That compares with just 9% during the preceding difficulty period.

It has been revealed that the pressure intensified between Nov. 7 and Nov. 11, when average daily electricity prices ranged from $64 to $122 per megawatt-hour. Meanwhile, the modeled mining equipment generated approximately $54 in revenue for every megawatt-hour consumed, before electricity and other operating costs.

Luxor estimated that higher electricity prices alone accounted for roughly four-fifths of the increase in unprofitable mining hours, suggesting energy costs drove the disruption rather than Bitcoin's declining price.

The resulting shutdowns reduced the computing power securing Bitcoin's network, contributing to the difficulty adjustment that lowered the measure to 134.82 trillion from 148.36 trillion.

While miners exposed to wholesale electricity prices could avoid losses by shutting down, companies with favorable power contracts had another opportunity.

Bitcoin mining company Riot Platforms, for example, can temporarily suspend operations and return contracted electricity to the grid in exchange for credits when market prices exceed its fixed electricity rates.

According to its third-quarter SEC filing, Riot earned $24.7 million in power curtailment credits during the three months ended Sept. 30, including $22.9 million from voluntarily reducing electricity consumption.

Those earnings preceded November's electricity surge but demonstrate how the arrangement works.

Consider a miner generating $54 in Bitcoin revenue per megawatt-hour while paying a fixed electricity rate of $35.

In a recent development, continuing operations would produce $19 after electricity costs. However, if wholesale electricity prices reached $100 and the operator could return its contracted power, it could receive a $65 credit instead.

Under those assumptions, switching off would generate $46 more per megawatt-hour than continuing to mine.

The same power price can make a wholesale miner stop to avoid a loss and give a miner with resale rights a reason to collect a credit.

With a fixed electricity price and resale rights, giving up $19 in mining margin can earn a $65 credit in this example.

Illustrative operating economics before other costs. $100/MWh and $35/MWh are scenario assumptions. Real credits depend on the contract and applicable market price. This does not estimate Riot’s rates or actions in November.

According to recent reports, per MWh, subtract $100 from $54 for wholesale mining, $35 from $54 for fixed-rate mining and $35 from $100 for the return credit. The credit is $46 above the fixed-rate mining margin. All bars share a zero and use the same dollars-per-MWh scale within each view.

Industry observers note that illustrative operating economics before other costs. $100/MWh and $35/MWh are scenario assumptions. Real credits depend on the contract and applicable market price. This does not estimate Riot’s rates or actions in November.

That difference helps explain why electricity markets can influence Bitcoin mining activity independently of cryptocurrency prices.

However, the relief from November's shutdowns may prove short-lived.

Luxor estimated that Bitcoin's computing power recovered to approximately 1,100 exahashes per second as West Texas electricity prices eased between Nov. 13 and Nov. 15, even as Bitcoin's price continued falling.

The recovery accelerated block production after the difficulty reduction, raising the prospect of another substantial adjustment.

Through Nov. 17, Bitcoin blocks had averaged approximately 9.11 minutes since the reset, faster than the network's targeted 10-minute interval.

Recent findings suggest that if that pace persists throughout the current difficulty period, the next adjustment could increase difficulty by approximately 9.85%, reversing nearly all the previous reduction. Even if block production slows to 10 minutes for the remaining period, the early acceleration would still produce an estimated 2.72% increase.

The extent of that rebound will depend partly on whether Texas electricity prices remain low enough to keep miners operating.

In a recent development, bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low.

Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99.

It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121.

Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%.

In a recent development, bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%.

Recent findings suggest that hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower.

The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was recently down about 1.7%, after falling as much as about 1,000 points, or 2%, at its session low.

The S&P 500 was down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite about 1%.

It has been revealed that nvidia shares were recently down about 1.4%, after falling more than 3% earlier in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role.

Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, mentioned he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America.

Industry observers note that sources told CNBC on Monday that the board is not considering bringing him back. The bitcoin price bounced from its low as Nvidia shares pared some of their losses, and was recently near $64,000.

Recent findings suggest that new York Fed President John Williams noted Tuesday that the AI investment boom could mean “we may need to raise rates more.” He played down a half-point hike in December. “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said.

It has been revealed that fed Governor Christopher Waller did not address the December decision in a payments speech Tuesday. Last week, he said a half-point hike should be considered if October’s core inflation ran at 0.3% or higher, and it did.

Markets still point to a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. Minutes from the October meeting are due Wednesday. The dollar was little changed, still near the 19-month high it touched on Monday.

Sources indicate that U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $7.9 million on Monday, ending a seven-session outflow streak. Wells Fargo more than doubled its bitcoin ETF stake to $2.35 billion, and Goldman Sachs did the same, lifting its holdings to $1.28 billion.

In a recent development, anthropic is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday, with shares set to start trading Thursday. A move back above $65,000 would reverse Tuesday’s decline, while a break of the weekend low near $62,000 would put last week’s flush back in view.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $64,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that bitcoin's plunge toward $62,000 on Nov. 15 coincided with a sharp increase in coins concentrated around the selloff low, potentially strengthening a key support zone.

It has been revealed that in its Nov. 17 report, Glassnode estimated that approximately 66,000 BTC entered the $62,000 to $66,000 short-term-holder cost-basis band during the two heaviest days of selling.

The price range, which initially formed around Bitcoin's August low, now accounts for roughly 20% of short-term holders' coins, making it an important level to watch if selling pressure returns.

Exchange trading data suggests buyers have begun absorbing some selling pressure after the crash.

Sources indicate that glassnode reported that sellers dominated trading during the selloff before buyer-initiated volume overtook seller-initiated activity in the 24 hours preceding its Nov. 17 snapshot.

According to recent reports, standing buy orders within 5% of Bitcoin's market price also outweighed sell orders by approximately 2.3 to 1 across Binance and Coinbase. The largest single Binance buy level since August was near $60,000.

According to recent reports, bitcoin fell to about $62,000 on Nov. 15, the lower edge of the cost-basis band. Two days later, Glassnode put Binance’s largest bid level since August near $60,000.

In a recent development, the price band and the open orders measure different things. A retest would show how much selling buyers actually absorb.

The 66,000 BTC figure estimates change in the short-term-holder cost-basis band. The $60,000 marker identifies a Binance order-book level. Orders can be canceled, and the depth ratio measures open orders rather than executed volume.

Glassnode data as of Nov. 17 at 13:00 UTC. The price axis is linear. Bars encode the reported approximate ratio of resting buy to sell size within 5% of spot across Binance and Coinbase, using sell size as one unit.

However, the recovery in buying demand has been uneven.

Sources indicate that bitcoin briefly traded at a premium on Coinbase during the Nov. 15 crash, but that advantage disappeared by Nov. 17. A separate Coinbase Premium Index from Axel Adler Jr. revealed Bitcoin trading at a 0.110% discount on Coinbase relative to Binance that day.

More recent trading activity nevertheless suggests renewed buying interest.

With Bitcoin trading as high as $65,365 in the last 24 hours, Blockmetric data revealed aggressive buying on Binance's spot market exceeded selling by about $5.5 million during the six hours ending at 07:54 UTC.

The platform also recorded $12.7 million in standing Binance buy orders between $62,500 and $62,600, reinforcing the evidence of demand around the lower end of Glassnode's support zone.

The combination of growing holder concentration and stronger exchange buying suggests the $62,000 to $66,000 region could play an important role in Bitcoin's next price move.

If Bitcoin retreats toward $62,000, the critical test will be whether buyers can absorb renewed selling pressure. Sustained buyer-led trading and a recovery in Coinbase's premium would strengthen the case for the support zone holding.

Going the distance: these electric semi trucks cover over 600 miles EVERY DAY

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that “Sure, diesel is high, but electric trucks don’t work.” It’s a common refrain these days – especially from people selling diesel trucks.
  • Over the course of the last year, Hendrik Müller, managing partner of DEFRU Logistik GmbH has transformed his manufacturer’s shipping fleet, switching thirty of their HD prime movers (semi trucks) to electric power and immediately putting the Mercedes-Benz eActros 600s to work, covering 1,000 km (~620 miles) of German highways each and every day.
  • Benjamin Budick, a Senior Manager, Own Retail Mercedes-Benz Trucks Dortmund & Haan, took to LinkedIn to announce the successful deployment, and posted some great pictures of the handover showing the significant Mercedes trucks in full DEFRU livery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “Sure, diesel is high, but electric trucks don’t work.” It’s a common refrain these days – especially from people selling diesel trucks. Perception lags reality, however, and the reality is that these electric semi trucks are covering more than 600 miles per day, seven days a week.

Over the course of the last year, Hendrik Müller, managing partner of DEFRU Logistik GmbH has transformed his manufacturer’s shipping fleet, switching thirty of their HD prime movers (semi trucks) to electric power and immediately putting the Mercedes-Benz eActros 600s to work, covering 1,000 km (~620 miles) of German highways each and every day.

Benjamin Budick, a Senior Manager, Own Retail Mercedes-Benz Trucks Dortmund & Haan, took to LinkedIn to announce the successful deployment, and posted some great pictures of the handover showing the significant Mercedes trucks in full DEFRU livery.

Mercedes’ eActros 600 packs a whopping, 621 kWh battery that helps the trucks cover 500 km per charge, allowing fleets to move goods between ports and regional fulfillment centers, charging along the way, or while they’re getting loaded and unloaded at their destination, all the while saving the fleet serious money – even before the latest Iran War sent diesel prices skyrocketing.

In a recent development, that big battery sends electrons to Mercedes-Benz’s proprietary electric drive axles, which deliver 1.61 kWh / mile efficiency while rolling out at an average of 36 metric tons (~79,400 lbs.) combined vehicle weight – specs that rivals the theoretical efficiency claims of the Tesla Semi. Except in the real world. And in winter.

Industry observers note that the eActros is a serious beast. As mentioned there are many configurations and they seem to work well in Europe. I've seen one that was configured with 620kWh battery, on one side a MCS port plus a CCS2 port (so thats either 1.2MW or 600kW charging options) and on the other side a CCS2 port.

#29448. Electric dirt bikes keep getting called e-bikes. The bicycle industry wants that to stop

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1092 w)
