Electric dirt bikes keep getting called e-bikes. The bicycle industry wants that to stop

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The line between electric bicycles and electric motorcycles has been getting increasingly blurry – though perhaps not because the vehicles themselves are actually that hard to tell apart.
  • Instead, much of the confusion comes down to terminology.
  • According to recent reports, now the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The line between electric bicycles and electric motorcycles has been getting increasingly blurry – though perhaps not because the vehicles themselves are actually that hard to tell apart.

Instead, much of the confusion comes down to terminology. High-powered electric dirt bikes capable of reaching motorcycle-like speeds are increasingly being referred to as “e-bikes,” despite sharing relatively little with the low-speed electric bicycles millions of Americans use for commuting and recreation.

According to recent reports, now the U.S. bicycle industry is asking federal regulators to make that distinction much clearer.

According to recent reports, peopleForBikes, the bicycle industry’s leading trade association, recently testified before the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), calling for stronger federal regulations that specifically distinguish electric bicycles from higher-powered e-motos and electric dirt bikes.

“E-bikes and e-motos are fundamentally different products, and federal safety regulations need to reflect that distinction,” explained PeopleForBikes Policy and General Counsel Matt Moore. “When high-powered electric dirt bikes are marketed as e-bikes, it creates confusion for consumers and puts the credibility of legitimate e-bikes at risk.”.

In a recent development, there’s a real nomenclature problem hiding underneath all of this. The term “e-bike” is widely used as shorthand for “electric bicycle,” but it isn’t exclusively used that way. Motorcycles have been called “bikes” for generations, and motorcycle media and riders will sometimes casually refer to electric motorcycles as “e-bikes” too, just in the way a biker refers to his Harley as his “bike”. In fact, it all comes from the same root. We don’t call motorcyclists “motorists”, do we? No… we call them “bikers”.

All of that makes phrases like “legal e-bike” and “legitimate e-bike” that were even used by PeopleForBikes in its arguments somewhat problematic when discussing proposed regulation. The term “e-bike” simply doesn’t mean anything specific, at least not legally.

What actually matters from a legal standpoint is whether a vehicle meets the codified definition of an electric bicycle, not whether someone calls it an e-bike – especially when the term e-bike is practically applied so broadly. In other words, perhaps part of separating electric bicycles from e-motos is being more precise with the terminology ourselves: “electric bicycle” has a specific regulatory meaning, while “e-bike” has increasingly become a much fuzzier colloquial term. As much as some would want the term “e-bike” to mean something with pedals, it simply doesn’t – at least not in North America.

I’m certainly guilty of this myself in my writing and videos, falling back on the commonly used phrasing instead of the technical legal terminology, but keeping them separated could help with the growing misunderstanding in the industry.

That distinction has become increasingly important as lightweight electric motorcycles and dirt bikes have exploded in popularity. Many feature bicycle-like frames and components, and some even include pedals, but their performance can extend far beyond what federal law defines as a low-speed electric bicycle.

The concern goes beyond mere semantics. When a 50-60 mph (80-100 km/h) electric dirt bike gets lumped into the same category as a 20-28 mph (32-45 km/h) commuter e-bike, crashes and reckless riding involving the former can rapidly become part of the public conversation surrounding the latter. That can ultimately influence how lawmakers, regulators, police departments, and the general public view e-bikes as a whole.

In fact, many of the supposed electric bicycle crash figures we’ve seen touted in the news aren’t from electric bicycles at all, but rather from e-moto accidents that have been lumped in with electric bicycles, making the latter appear more dangerous than they truly are.

If street-legal electric bicycles were separated from e-motos in crash statistics, the category would be revealed to be much safer than conventional reporting would have us believe.

All of this and more has led to PeopleForBikes pushing federal regulators to draw a clearer line.

Sources indicate that as part of its CPSC testimony, the organization recommended retaining the existing federal definition of a low-speed electric bicycle while creating a separate definition for e-motos, including machines capable of speeds up to 60 mph (96 km/h). It also called for mandatory electrical safety standards for off-road e-motos, which it says currently fall into a regulatory gap, as well as greater scrutiny of conversion kits capable of turning conventional bicycles into vehicles operating beyond their original structural design limits.

It has been revealed that well, if its not an electric bicycle, it should be treated as a moped, registration and insurance at least, possibly a VIN and a title. So it must carry a plate if it rides on the street.

Personally I think even the level-3 electric bicycle standard (28mph with pedal assist) is to permissive, even gas mopeds have pedals, and few exceed 30mph.

But I'll lose that argument most of the time.

Now, suggestion, in the USA: a newly introduced category for "light motorcycle".

HP limit at about 15, weight limit at about 250lb(or less), speed limit at about 60, not allowed on freeways and interstates. Gas or electric does not matter. License, registration, title, insurance, they all depend on the state mostly. Helmet required, if rider is younger?

A great entry point for younger riders, much of Europe does it like this.

Best of all, they would be pretty cheap.

It has been revealed that the testimony came as the CPSC considers new mandatory federal battery safety standards for e-bikes and other electric mobility devices. PeopleForBikes claims it supports stronger battery standards, while recommending that regulators rely on existing UL standards without modification.

PeopleForBikes is also asking the CPSC and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to coordinate enforcement against e-motos that evade federal requirements.

None of this means e-motos are inherently bad. They’re incredibly fun machines, and there’s a rapidly growing market for them. But a 60 mph (96 km/h) electric dirt bike isn’t an electric bicycle simply because it looks vaguely like one.

And increasingly, the bicycle industry wants regulators to make sure everyone understands the difference.

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (808 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Architecturaldigest ↗ Open Full Page

Jensen Huang’s Houses: Exploring the Former Nvidia CEO’s $38 Million San Francisco Mansion and Other Properties

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it’s been a big week for Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang.
  • It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, the tech titan hasn’t strayed too far from Silicon Valley, where Nvidia has been based since it was founded in the mid-’80s, with his real estate purchases.
  • One thing that will presumably change about Huang’s home life in the immediate future: footing the bill for his security team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s been a big week for Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang. The billionaire confirmed he is stepping down as CEO of the AI hardware giant following reports that he had at least two extramarital affairs: one with a suspected Chinese spy, and another with one of his company’s senior executives (other reports allege a third affair with another Nvidia employee). Huang will reportedly testify before Congress later this month to discuss his relationship with the alleged spy. We can only assume that the Taipei City native is weathering the storm at home, but where are Jensen Huang’s houses? Even Huang himself may be wondering about the answer to that question, if a recent Upcoming York Times interview is any indication (more on that later).

It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, the tech titan hasn’t strayed too far from Silicon Valley, where Nvidia has been based since it was founded in the mid-’80s, with his real estate purchases. After graduating from Oregon State University, where he met his wife, Lori Huang, Huang began buying properties in California’s Bay Area, and he and Lori still own two of them. So far, the superbillionaire’s only exception to that rule has been an estate on Maui in Hawaii. Time will tell if the scandal spurs any real estate changes for him.

One thing that will presumably change about Huang’s home life in the immediate future: footing the bill for his security team. Nvidia has, until now, covered the cost of its former CEO’s private security. The manufacturer spent about $4 million in 2026 on “home security, protection during personal travel, consulting, and drivers” for Huang, per the Latest York Post. Though that arrangement is likely coming to an end, that shouldn’t be too big a problem for Jensen; the scandal has put Nvidia’s stock—and therefore Jensen’s net worth—in a slight flux, but he is still worth an estimated $144.7 billion at the time of publication.

Read on for a rundown of Jensen Huang’s houses dating back to his arrival in Silicon Valley.

Recent findings suggest that according to The Upcoming York Times, Huang married Lori shortly after his 1984 graduation from Oregon State University, where they met as lab partners in an electrical engineering class. The newlywed graduates hightailed it to Silicon Valley to start their careers as microchip designers, and Jensen bought his first house: a 1,500-square-foot three-bedroom home in San Jose, California. It’s unclear exactly when or for how much he bought the property, but Jensen sold it in 1988 for $185,000.

That same year, Huang and Lori moved into a larger San Jose home that they bought for $338,000. With 2,300 square feet of interior living space, it had four bedrooms. Huang lived here when he co-founded Nvidia in 1993; he sold the house in 2002 for $500,000, the Wall Street Journal reports.

From there, the Huangs moved into an even more upgraded residence: a 7,000-square-foot home in Los Altos Hills, a tony area about 15 miles from the Nvidia headquarters. They paid $6.9 million for the newly built six-bedroom dwelling in 2003. According to Realtor.com, the two-story house hosts a resort-worthy swimming pool. The Huangs still own this house.

A year after buying his house in Los Altos Hills, Huang paid $7.5 million for a Hawaiian estate. The oceanfront property is located within Wailea Resort, an exclusive gated community on the south side of Maui, per the Wall Street Journal. The contemporary-style mansion reportedly has seven bedrooms across about 8,000 square feet. The Huangs still maintain this residence too.

In 2017, Huang made his most recent real estate purchase: a newly completed $38 million mansion in the high-end Pacific Heights neighborhood on San Francisco’s Gold Coast. The residence is modern in style, with a curved roofline and a limestone exterior. It boasts 11,400 square feet of interior living space, with seven bedrooms, seven full bathrooms, three half-baths, a wine cellar, an outdoor kitchen, an elevator, a home theater, a gym with a sauna, a library, numerous fireplaces, and a fifth-floor observation deck with views of the Golden Gate Bridge. The house took four years to construct, its developer told the WSJ.

San Francisco’s famous Golden Gate Bridge.

Industry observers note that this seems to be Huang’s primary residence—although, according to a September 2026 Upcoming York Times interview, he could not tell you where it is. “There are a lot of skills that don’t matter,” Huang told the outlet in response to a question about AI weakening students’ basic math skills. “My first confession, I actually don’t know my address.… One day I had to pump gas—it was a few years ago. They needed my ZIP code, and I panicked. I didn’t know my ZIP code. I don’t know my telephone number. I forget these things. I can live with it.”.

US data center construction fell 28% in the third quarter of 2026, marking its first quarterly decline in more than a year as questions mount over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom.

According to data released by Cleanview, developers began construction on facilities representing 8.4 gigawatts of power capacity between July and September, down from a record 11.7 GW in the preceding quarter.

The number of buildings starting construction also fell to 65 from 96, although the quarter still ranked third-highest in Cleanview's records and was up 55% from the same period last year.

US buildings that began vertical construction in October 2026.

Three buildings accounted for about 35% of the second-highest month in Cleanview’s series.

According to recent reports, cleanview rounds the monthly total. It dates each start to the beginning of vertical construction.

Add the three reported October building contributions (720 + 461 + 450 = 1,631 MW) and divide by 4,600 MW. The resulting share, 35.46%, is shown as about 35% because the monthly total is rounded. The rows use a common scale to compare the building values.

Cleanview rounds the monthly total. It dates each start to the beginning of vertical construction.

The slowdown raises questions about an industry whose expansion has become central to the global AI investment boom.

Sources indicate that michael Thomas, founder of Cleanview Energy, estimated that data centers whose construction began this year will cost approximately $1 trillion to build and equip. He stated:.

“A lasting slowdown would reach the utilities planning new power plants, the companies making chips and turbines, and a stock market that has bet heavily on AI.”.

The findings are based on Cleanview's analysis of thousands of satellite images tracking construction activity at more than 1,300 data center buildings across the United States.

Despite the third-quarter slowdown, construction activity rebounded sharply in October, with developers starting facilities representing 4.6 GW of capacity.

That was the second-highest monthly total Cleanview has recorded and nearly double the capacity that began construction in October 2025.

Three major projects accounted for approximately 35% of the month's activity. These included 720 megawatts at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia, 461 MW at Related Digital's Stargate Michigan campus and 450 MW at Crusoe's Abilene campus in Texas.

Together, the projects represented approximately 1.63 GW of new construction starts, highlighting the scale of investment still flowing into AI infrastructure.

In view of this, Thomas said it was too early to conclude that the third-quarter decline signaled a lasting slowdown.

This is because October's strong rebound could push fourth-quarter construction starts to a record 14 GW if the pace continues through November and December.

Industry News: Musk indicates Cybertruck isn’t dying from weak sales — the numbers disagree

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that elon Musk now claims Cybertruck orders “far exceed” Tesla’s production rate, and that the truck isn’t being killed because it’s unprofitable.
  • It has been revealed that the problem is that Tesla’s own numbers say the opposite.
  • Industry observers note that “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that elon Musk now claims Cybertruck orders “far exceed” Tesla’s production rate, and that the truck isn’t being killed because it’s unprofitable. It’s his second explanation in three days for ending the pickup.

It has been revealed that the problem is that Tesla’s own numbers say the opposite. The Cybertruck line has been running at roughly a quarter of its installed capacity, and Tesla spent all of 2026 discounting, re-trimming, and repricing the truck to find buyers.

Here’s what Musk posted on X overnight:.

Industry observers note that “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people. This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.”.

The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported… https://t.co/rGmNKV3ILs.

He was quote-tweeting a Tesla fan telling people to “get it while you can.” So yes, this is also a sales pitch.

Industry observers note that on Friday, Musk announced Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027 “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” That was the first story. Now it’s about “complexity” and “opportunity cost.” Let’s go through it.

Industry observers note that tesla controls its production rate. That’s the flaw in this claim.

Industry observers note that tesla built the Cybertruck supply chain for 250,000 units a year, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. In Q3 2026, it delivered 8,295 “Other Models.” With Model S and Model X out of production, we estimated 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks. That’s a 30,000-a-year pace, down 48% year-over-year in that category.

It has been revealed that if orders had been outrunning production at any point this year, Tesla had about 95,000 units of idle annual capacity sitting right there. It didn’t use it.

And companies with a backlog don’t behave like Tesla did. In February, it offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.” It pulled a single-motor RWD version after just 173 sales. It leaned on Musk’s own companies too: SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, about 19% of US registrations that quarter once you add his other firms.

According to recent reports, cox Automotive estimates US Cybertruck sales fell from 14,416 in Q3 2024 to 3,519 in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2. It’s a demand problem everyone could see.

According to recent reports, so if orders spiked this weekend, there’s an obvious reason: Musk told the world on Friday that the truck is going away. A last-call rush on a discontinued vehicle is not proof that it was selling.

Tesla has been sitting on Cybertruck deposits it was never going to fill for years.

Musk touted more than a million reservations, and crowdsourced tallies put the list near 2 million by 2023. Its best US quarter, by Cox Automotive’s estimate, was 14,416 trucks. The reservation book was a vanity number, not an order book.

Two weeks ago, Tesla cancelled the Cybertruck for Australia and Fresh Zealand and refunded deposits people had paid in 2019. Returning deposits is something Tesla was already doing because it couldn’t sell the truck in those markets, not because it was swamped.

This one is a straw man. Our reporting, and most of the coverage Friday, was about sales, not margins. The truck sells at about 12% of the volume Tesla planned for.

Recent findings suggest that tesla doesn’t disclose Cybertruck margins, so Musk can say whatever he wants here and nobody can check it. But he’s the one who stated in 2023 that Tesla had “dug our own grave with Cybertruck” because of how hard it was to build profitably.

And look at what Tesla did the same day it unveiled the end of production: it raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the cheapest trim. The cheapest orderable Cybertruck went from $69,990 in early August to $92,490. You do that to squeeze margin out of the last trucks, not because the line was printing money.

Follow Musk’s logic to the end. If the Cybertruck were profitable and orders really outran production, killing it would mean walking away from guaranteed profit for a robotaxi that had 463 units registered in Texas as of late October and no proven business yet.

The only way that trade makes sense is if the Cybertruck’s profit at 30,000 units a year is small. Which is another way of saying it doesn’t sell enough.

Giga Texas also has more than 10 million square feet of floor space, and the Cybercab runs on its own “unboxed” line. Tesla can’t make use of the Cybertruck line and floor space was never the constraint. To further adapt his logic for shutting down Cybertruck production, Musk shifted his argument from “space” to Cybercab’s line needing some “smart people”, who he implied work on the Cybertruck.

Sources indicate that musk wrote on Saturday that “there are a very limited number of smart, dedicated people”, but Michael So, who led Cybercab latest product introduction and was Giga Texas employee #1, left in April for nuclear startup Aalo Atomics. Last month, Tesla lost its Cybercab general assembly lead to Rivian’s R2 program just weeks after the launch. If talent is the bottleneck, it’s the Cybercab team that’s bleeding it.

Musk doesn’t want the Cybertruck to go down in history as a flop, and we get it. It’s his truck. He approved the controversial design, hyped it for four years before it shipped, and boasted that 1 million reservations could translate to 500,000 units a year.

Sources indicate that but you can’t run a line at a quarter of capacity, run “10 days only” discounts, pull trims after 173 sales, and sell trucks to your own rocket manufacturer, then turn around and tell people demand was never the concern. The data is public. Tesla’s own delivery reports are public.

It has been revealed that our read on what happened is simple. Demand collapsed in 2025 and never came back. Tesla tried every pricing trick it had. When nothing worked, it found a future-facing reason to end it, and now it’s spinning the inevitable end-of-life rush as proof the truck was a hit all along.

In a recent development, musk loves a big TAM. SpaceX’s IPO filing put its total addressable market at $28.5 trillion, and last month he went further, writing that he sees “a path to SpaceX being worth orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy.”.

So apply the same lens to Tesla. Pickups are one of the biggest and most profitable vehicle markets on the planet. Ford sold 801,525 F-Series trucks in the US last year, GM sold 925,656 Silverados and Sierras combined, and Ram moved 374,059. That’s more than 2.1 million trucks from three automakers, easily north of $100 billion a year at today’s transaction prices.

Its funny that such a "free speech absolutist" won't disclose something as simple as auto only OpMargins...proving my point that Tesla post-Musk buyout simply existed to make products that were eligible for EV and green tax credits.

Robotaxis? Waymo, by far the leader, is doing about 500,000 paid rides a week, and analysts estimated its revenue run rate at roughly $355 million earlier this year. Tesla doesn’t even break out robotaxi revenue and we expect it to be a fraction of Waymo’s.

Industry observers note that maybe that flips one day. But that’s the bet here: Tesla is walking away from a giant market it can sell into today for one that only gets major if autonomy is solved in the next couple of years. Musk has made that exact bet before. He promised a million robotaxis on the road by 2020 and has stated unsupervised self-driving was a year away almost every year since 2016. He’s lost every time.

Industry observers note that and that rush is real, for what it’s worth. Some people want the last of a weird, genuinely impressive truck. That doesn’t make it a business.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Surrounded by trees, this small wooden house in Denmark blends seamlessly with nature.
  • Sources indicate that named the EcoNeo House, the home was designed by the Danish architectural firm SAGA Space Architects, both as a family home and as a prototype for tiny house-style vacation homes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mini vacation home in Zealand, Denmark, is a particularly appealing retreat, no matter the season. With its rugged coastlines, forests, and small villages, the western side of Zealand offers an ideal setting for a break from everyday life. Nestled among trees is a tiny house that was designed to be as unobtrusive as possible. Its compact shape, natural color palette, and large windows allow it to blend almost seamlessly into the forest. Here, nature isn’t just right outside the door—it’s always present inside as well.

Surrounded by trees, this small wooden house in Denmark blends seamlessly with nature.

Sources indicate that named the EcoNeo House, the home was designed by the Danish architectural firm SAGA Space Architects, both as a family home and as a prototype for tiny house-style vacation homes. Although originally conceived as a summer house, the cottage has been insulated and heated, allowing it to be used even during colder weather. At only 377 square feet, it combines the essential features of a vacation home, sleeping up to six people. The design prioritizes a thoughtful use of the available space and forward-thinking architecture that blends into the landscape.

The spacious terrace is perfect for sunbathing and dining outdoors, especially in the summer.

According to recent reports, inside, the living and dining areas flow seamlessly into one another. Thanks to the large windows that offer views of the surrounding trees, there’s a connection between indoors and outdoors. The kitchen is set slightly apart, but opens up into the dining area, blending smoothly into the floor strategy. Designed with functionality in mind, it’s still fully equipped with all the necessary appliances.

The dining area flows seamlessly into the kitchen. Additional storage space was created below the stairs on the left, which lead to the sleeping lofts.

Instead of breaking up the floor plan with additional walls, the architects made use of the home’s height: Stairs next to the kitchen lead to two sleeping lofts that offer a private retreat for up to four people. Storage was also a priority in the design. Items not needed on a daily basis can be stowed under the stairs, a clever solution that again makes the most of the small space.

Sources indicate that large windows let in plenty of natural light and create a connection between indoors and outdoors. Despite its compact size, the kitchen has all the necessary appliances.

It has been revealed that there’s even a sauna, which can be converted into a sleeping space for two additional guests if needed. The generous window front offers a view of the surrounding landscape, while a cold plunge pool on the terrace is waiting for a refreshing dip afterward.

Through the sauna’s large window, you can enjoy the surrounding nature even while relaxing. It’s an appealing retreat, especially on chilly days. There’s also a cold plunge pool on the terrace.

Sources indicate that the choice of materials complements the understated architecture. The floor’s wide Douglas fir planks introduce a warm color and vibrant grain. The use of wood is consistently carried through to other areas of the house, creating a visual connection between the living space and the sauna. Natural materials are also used in the bathroom, including Kolmården marble, a Swedish stone distinguished by its characteristic green hue.

Wood defines the interior and lends the rooms a natural warmth. Large windows bring the surrounding nature into the home, while the dining area is spacious even within the compact layout.

In a recent development, together with the stones and the greenery outside, the result is a design that deliberately avoids contrasts and excess. “When designing the summer house, every detail was intended to reflect the harmony between sustainable innovation and timeless craftsmanship,” explains Niklas Munk-Andersen, architect and partner at SAGA Space Architects.

Beanbag chairs provide extra seating and blend harmoniously into the interior with their colors.

According to recent reports, the Douglas fir floorboards also give the clean design a natural, tactile quality. The material is more than a surface design choice, instead it shapes the way that the rooms feel.

The bathroom features natural materials and Swedish marble finishes.

The sauna can also be converted into a sleeping area for two additional guests.

The compact design also has a positive impact on the home’s carbon footprint. According to calculations by SAGA Space Architects, the EcoNeo House produces approximately 386 pounds of CO₂ annually, whereas an average vacation home for six people is estimated to emit about 2,282 pounds. This means emissions are approximately 83% lower. In addition to the small living area, bio-based materials are the primary factor contributing to this difference.

The boundary between indoors and outdoors blurs, bringing nature into focus.

In a recent development, the architects also designed the construction process to be as efficient as possible by digitally planning the house, precisely prefabricating its individual components, and then assembling them on-site in a modular fashion. This approach not only simplified assembly but also minimized the impact on the site.

In a recent development, thanks to its small footprint, this vacation home’s emissions are 83% lower than those of the average vacation home that can accommodate six people. In addition, the modular construction minimizes the impact on the natural environment.

The EcoNeo House demonstrates that sustainable construction isn’t just a matter of the materials used. The size of a building and how the available space is utilized also play a crucial role. Though it may sound small, 377 square feet can be perfectly sufficient for a getaway home—provided the floor proposal, storage space, and amenities are all carefully designed.

Although primarily intended as a summer home, this small vacation home can also be enjoyed in colder months.

A skylight lets light into the upper sleeping lofts.

The small vacation home has two separate sleeping lofts accommodating four people.

South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Indicates

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that south Korea’s Financial Services Commission prepares to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday.
  • The FSC itself has not publicly unveiled a date for either release.
  • Recent findings suggest that that blueprint opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that south Korea’s Financial Services Commission prepares to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report. The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release.

The FSC itself has not publicly unveiled a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025.

Recent findings suggest that that blueprint opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit.

It has been revealed that exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived.

The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate.

Recent findings suggest that the Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week.

Sources indicate that lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party mentioned at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.”.

Industry observers note that the report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. In January, *Seoul Economic Daily* reported that a draft would cap a organization’s annual crypto investment at 5% of equity capital and limit purchases to the top 20 coins by market value. The FSC responded the next day that key items, including investment limits and eligible assets, had not been finalized.

In a recent development, analysts said at the time that corporate flows would likely concentrate in bitcoin, the largest crypto asset by market value, even with a wider menu of coins. Jeonbuk Bank said in October it would offer bitcoin-backed loans. Korea has also pushed back its 22% crypto tax to 2029, the fourth delay, while the Bank of Korea has lobbied to write stablecoins into foreign exchange law.

Retail investors in Korea have been able to trade crypto for years. Domestic demand has at times pushed local bitcoin prices above global levels, a gap known as the kimchi premium. Corporate money has been the missing piece. Under the roadmap, about 3,500 companies would become eligible once the guidelines take effect.

It has been revealed that the guidelines’ release would not on its own open trading. The FSC still has to say when listed companies can place their first orders.

Tesla launches Robotaxi in San Antonio with a 274 sq mi geofence on paper

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles.
  • According to recent reports, but if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a substantial chunk of that area won’t be bookable.
  • Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles. That’s the biggest day-one map Tesla has ever posted, and more than four times the size of Waymo’s San Antonio service area.

According to recent reports, but if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a substantial chunk of that area won’t be bookable. In Austin, an independent check found the Robotaxi app only accepted pickups and drop-offs in about 59% of the zone Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.

According to recent reports, robotaxi Tracker, which measures operator maps and logs fleet sightings, puts the zone at 274 square miles. That covers about 1.0 million residents (51% of the metro) and 721,000 jobs. San Antonio International Airport sits inside the polygon, but it isn’t served.

It has been revealed that waymo started driverless rides in San Antonio in February with more than 60 square miles and opened to all riders in October, airport trips included. Robotaxi Tracker presently lists Waymo’s San Antonio area at 59 square miles.

Sources indicate that what Tesla didn’t say is how many cars will cover its 274 square miles. As of Monday morning, Robotaxi Tracker hadn’t logged a single Tesla Robotaxi in San Antonio.

The launch landed the same day Tesla expanded Austin again. The tracker now measures Tesla’s Austin zone at 443 square miles, up 178 square miles since mid-September.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve seen this movie. Last month, Tesla expanded its Houston geofence into the shape of a rocket, and within two days the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app refusing downtown pickups inside it.

Since then, Koby Pierce, who tracks Tesla’s service on X, has done the tedious work of checking city after city. He searched thousands of real addresses in the Robotaxi app on an emulator and mapped only the ones where Tesla allows a pickup or drop-off, then compared that with the map Tesla advertises. Here’s the share of Tesla’s advertised land area that actually works:.

Austin's dropoff/pickup Geofence is ~41% smaller than advertised.Seems mostly the East side of town is inaccessible. Unsure the cause. Any ideas?Dallas is next and should be done by noon tomrrow. pic.twitter.com/WvU99sJlJh.

Austin is the one that matters. It’s Tesla’s flagship market, with 453 unsupervised vehicles in service according to Robotaxi Tracker. Yet about 41% of the advertised map Pierce tested, mostly on the east side of town, wouldn’t take a ride request. Pierce points to railroad crossings as a big factor in several cities, which lines up with the strange downtown routing we saw in Houston.

To be fair, Pierce says Waymo is next on his list, and he expects “they’re no better.” Robotaxi Tracker already had to trim Waymo’s Orlando area last month after finding the airport, inside Waymo’s published map, wasn’t selectable. We’ll look at those numbers when they’re out. But it doesn’t change what Tesla is doing with San Antonio today.

It has been revealed that credit where it’s due. A 274-square-mile launch in a fresh city is progress, and Tesla now runs unsupervised rides in eight cities. At the start of this year, it had no unsupervised rides anywhere.

Sources indicate that but we need to stop taking Tesla’s geofence numbers at face value, and that includes us. We used Tesla’s 254-square-mile figure for Houston, and it turned out to be overstated. In all six cities Pierce has checked, the real service area is between 59% and 78% of what Tesla posts. In Austin and Miami, it’s about 60%.

According to recent reports, so the honest way to read the San Antonio announcement is “up to 274 square miles.” In practice, expect something closer to 160 to 210 square miles, with an unknown number of cars, and the airport already off the table. That’s still bigger than Waymo’s 59 square miles in the city.

It has been revealed that these maps are mostly fiction. I live inside the Houston map but the app says I am outside. If you drive to where the app allows, no vehicles are ever available. Waymos are a routine site and are available on a short notice. This is smoke and mirrors to shore up the firm value ahead of the SpaceX merger.

The problem is that square miles are the metric Tesla fully controls. Drawing a polygon costs nothing, and the numbers were all over X within hours of the post. Cars per square mile, wait times, and rides completed are much harder to inflate, and nationally Waymo still runs over 4,000 driverless vehicles to Tesla’s 666, per Robotaxi Tracker.

I still consider this a small pilot by any standard, and safety remains the bottleneck. Tesla is still forcing riders through hour-long rides that should take 15 minutes because they have to take routes that avoid areas that Tesla can’t safely navigate without supervision.

Until that’s fixed, robotaxi won’t be able to meaningfully scale beyond these limited demonstrations in geo-fenced areas.

Robotaxi or not, most EV charging still happens at home, and pairing it with rooftop solar can cut your cost per mile to nearly zero. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, US prices for imported capital goods such as computers and machinery rose 1.5% in October from September, the biggest monthly increase since the Bureau of Labor Statistics began monthly publication in December 1988.
  • Sources indicate that the two reports, released November 17, matter for Bitcoin traders who finance positions with borrowed dollars.
  • The BLS reported that computers, peripherals and semiconductors, electrical equipment and machinery drove the increase in capital-goods prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, US prices for imported capital goods such as computers and machinery rose 1.5% in October from September, the biggest monthly increase since the Bureau of Labor Statistics began monthly publication in December 1988. Industrial production fell 0.4% in the Federal Reserve's preliminary estimate.

Sources indicate that the two reports, released November 17, matter for Bitcoin traders who finance positions with borrowed dollars. Softer output can make a case for lower rates, while rising equipment costs show that price pressure extends beyond fuel. Before the Fed minutes, interest-rate futures pointed to higher rates into early 2027.

The BLS reported that computers, peripherals and semiconductors, electrical equipment and machinery drove the increase in capital-goods prices. Nonfuel import prices rose 0.8%, up from 0.5% in September. Fuel import prices rose 3.6% after rising 6.3% in September, and overall import prices rose 1.1% in October.

How much of the equipment price increase will reach consumers remains uncertain. The BLS also left some annual comparisons blank because the 2025 federal shutdown prevented the agency from collecting the year-earlier survey data.

The Fed's preliminary industrial production estimate put October's drop in output at 0.4% after a 0.7% rise in September. Utilities output fell 4.3% and mining fell 0.8%. Manufacturing rose 0.3% but edged down 0.1% excluding motor vehicles and parts. Overall production was still 2.1% higher than a year earlier.

October’s monthly changes in two import-price indexes and the Federal Reserve’s industrial production index.

The 1.5% equipment rise was part of a broader 0.8% increase in nonfuel import prices.

The import indexes track prices at the import stage. Industrial production measures the volume of output.

Industry observers note that bars encode the published October 2026 percentage changes from September on a common signed scale. Capital goods are part of the nonfuel import basket.

The import indexes track prices at the import stage. Industrial production measures the volume of output.

Sources indicate that the Fed held its policy target range at 3.75% to 4% in October, with two officials favoring a quarter-point increase. In its November 17 commentary, CME Group put the FedWatch odds of a quarter-point December hike at 95% and the odds of a half-point hike at 5%.

Sources indicate that at 3:01 a.m. ET on November 18, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%, Frenzy Capital's estimates from CME fed funds futures put the expected effective rate at 4.14% after the Fed's December 9 decision, 4.32% after January 27 and 4.48% after March 17.

According to recent reports, at 3:01 a.m. ET on Nov. 18, 2026, CME futures implied an effective rate of 4.141% after Dec. 9, 4.320% after Jan. 27 and 4.486% after Mar. 17. The observed rate was 3.880%.

Source: Frenzy Capital, November 18 snapshot.

The Fed explains how expected short-term rates can influence borrowing costs across the economy. For traders who borrow dollars to finance Bitcoin positions, that higher expected path can keep financing expensive even as parts of the economy slow. For crypto-backed borrowers, comparing loan rates and fees also means checking collateral requirements and repayment terms.

The Fed scheduled its October minutes for release at 2 p.m. ET on November 18. The October meeting took place before either November 17 report came out. The next test for traders is whether January and March rate expectations move after the minutes and before the Fed issues updated economic projections in December.

007 Off Duty: 10 Photos of Former James Bond Actors at Home

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a secret agent, James Bond generates a remarkable amount of public discussion.
  • In a recent development, whoever takes over will join the small group who have played the part since Sean Connery’s debut in Dr.
  • Sean Connery relaxing in his ground-floor basement flat in NW5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a secret agent, James Bond generates a remarkable amount of public discussion. Barely a day goes by without fresh speculation about who will be the next actor to take on the role of 007. Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, and Josh O’Connor are among the names linked to the role, with recent reports suggesting the search has reached final screen tests.

In a recent development, whoever takes over will join the small group who have played the part since Sean Connery’s debut in Dr. No in 1962. Away from the screen, the homes of these former James Bond actors reveal more about the men in the dinner jackets. These archival photographs find them settling into family life and indulging interests that occasionally followed them onto set. Below, find a little domestic distraction while we wait for the next Bond to introduce himself.

Sean Connery relaxing in his ground-floor basement flat in NW5.

It has been revealed that photographed at home in England in 1955, Connery is still around seven years away from his first appearance as James Bond in this shapshot. His surroundings are modest, with little suggestion of the polished interiors his screen alter ego was about to frequent. Connery established the role of Bond across six films in during the 1960s and early 1970s.

Landing the role of James Bond required a little wardrobe planning on George Lazenby’s part. According to the official Bond website, the former model bought an unused suit made for Connery, then visited his predecessor’s barber at the Dorchester to request the same haircut. Producer Cubby Broccoli happened to be in the neighboring chair.

George Lazenby pictured at his home in Kensington, London, 1973.

His only appearance as 007 was in the 1969 film On Her Majesty's Secret Service. It gave Bond one of his most personal storylines, with Diana Rigg playing his ill-fated bride, Tracy. By the time of the Kensington photograph shown above in February 1973, Lazenby had already left the role. Seated with papers in hand, he is surrounded by books, records and a guitar propped beside the sofa. The glass-topped coffee table is crowded with objects, including a decorative horse’s head, while a substantial wooden cabinet provides storage behind him. Later that year, Roger Moore made his Bond debut in Live and Let Die.

Roger Moore reading the dictionary at his home in Los Angeles, circa 1955.

Roger Moore had yet to order his first on-screen Bond martini when he was photographed at home reading a dictionary, while working as a television actor.

Roger Moore kissing his wife, Welsh singer Dorothy Squires, outside their home in Bexley Heath, London, in 1957.

He married Welsh singer Dorothy Squires in 1953, and they lived primarily at The Mount—a mansion on Wansunt Road in Old Bexley, Kent.

Moore and Squires at home in Kent, 1958.

The couple divorced in 1968, and a year later, Moore married Luisa Mattioli. Sherwood House in Denham, located close to Pinewood Studios, served as the couple's base during Moore's first three Bond films. In his autobiography, he described the property as “near London and perfect for a growing family.”.

Its appeal extended to 11 acres of grounds, which included a tennis court, heated swimming pool and greenhouses when the house was advertised for £5 million in 2015.

When he finally took on Bond's on-screen persona, Timothy Dalton was well-prepared for the role.

Industry observers note that producers considered Timothy Dalton for Bond early in his career, but he felt too young for the role. When he eventually signed on for The Living Daylights in 1986, he reread Fleming’s novels to prepare for a more serious interpretation of the character.

Pierce Brosnan at home in Los Angeles in 1983.

It has been revealed that pierce Brosnan was making his name in Remington Steele when he posed at his Los Angeles home in June 1983, but his introduction to the world of Bond had come through his first wife, actress Cassandra Harris. She appeared in For Your Eyes Only, and visiting her on location in Corfu brought him into the producers’ orbit. Brosnan was offered the role in 1986, but was prevented from taking it due to his television commitments at the time. His debut in GoldenEye came almost a decade later, in 1995.

Pierce Brosnan playing pool with his son, Sean, at their Los Angeles home in 1992.

This 1992 photographs show Brosnan playing guitar on the sofa, shooting pool with his eight-year-old son Sean, and entertaining two dogs in the garden. Cream sofas and floral upholstery adorn the living room, while arched windows and white shutters open the space to the surrounding greenery. Taken the year after Harris died of ovarian cancer, the photographs capture Brosnan bringing up their family before Bond transformed his career.

Pierce Brosnan with his dogs outside of their Los Angeles home in 1992.

Painting had become a creative outlet for the star during Harris’s illness. Having trained as a commercial artist before acting, Brosnan returned to it in the late 1980s, recalling on his website: “I started painting again and out came every colour.” By the time he became Bond, painting was so sufficiently embedded in his life that his dressing room at Leavesden doubled as a studio during GoldenEye.

Daniel Craig attends the Bond 25 film launch at Ian Fleming's Home, GoldenEye, in Montego Bay, Jamaica, 2019.

For this final entry, the front door stays closed. Of all the former James Bond actors, Daniel Craig represents a more guarded approach to sharing domestic life. His wife, actress Rachel Weisz, explained the couple’s position in a 2012 conversation with British Vogue: “I think it’s pretty ordinary to think that marriage is private and sacred.”.

Speculation over who will inherit Craig's martini glass keeps his name in the headlines even after his departure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine data, as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller remarked a half-point rate hike is probably needed in December.
  • The bitcoin price is down about 21% from a month ago, when it traded above $81,000.
  • Waller told CNBC in a live interview that the Fed probably needs a half-point increase at its Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine data, as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller remarked a half-point rate hike is probably needed in December. The bitcoin price had slipped below $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon. It climbed back to about $65,000 that evening after Nvidia beat earnings estimates, then faded through the U.S. morning.

The bitcoin price is down about 21% from a month ago, when it traded above $81,000.

Waller told CNBC in a live interview that the Fed probably needs a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He said the central bank should reverse its three quarter-point cuts from last year and may need to do more. “You might need to, like, shock people,” Waller said.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” he said. Waller said the Fed should deliver the larger move if it is not prepared to signal a faster pace of hikes in the coming months. He also said about 70% of items in the core services basket are running above 3%, which has nothing to do with oil.

The 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 4 basis points to 4.83% after his comments. The dollar hit a 19-month high, and gold dropped 2.5% to its lowest level in more than a year. Futures markets fully price a quarter-point hike in December and another increase in January, CNBC reported. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested Tuesday that as many as four hikes could come by spring.

Minutes from the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting are due Wednesday afternoon. Policymakers held rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike.

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion after the bell Tuesday, more than double a year earlier and above the $109.1 billion analysts expected. Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, and the company guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will remain “disciplined in how we commit capital.” The board said it would not reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week.

Nvidia shares were up about 2.6% in premarket trading. Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.8% and S&P 500 futures rose 0.3%, but the bitcoin price did not follow tech higher. IREN (IREN), the bitcoin miner turned AI cloud provider, rose between 8% and 10% in extended trading along with CoreWeave and Nebius, and was recently up about 3% premarket. Strategy (MSTR) closed down 6.3% at $96.50 on Tuesday and was little changed before the open, while Coinbase (COIN) closed down 4% and was up about 0.5% premarket.

Recent findings suggest that U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed a net $239.9 million on Tuesday, a day after snapping a seven-session outflow streak. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $209.5 million of that. Anthropic is expected to price its IPO Wednesday evening, with shares set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. The firm marketed 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, and sources told CNBC on Tuesday that the deal will likely price above that range.

President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. AI chip exports are a key issue.

A break of the weekend low near $62,000 would put last week’s flush back in view for the bitcoin price.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $63,800.

  • According to recent reports, liveWire has spent the last few years expanding beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
  • I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the company had everything from its upcoming lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.
  • It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a firm that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, liveWire has spent the last few years expanding beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off. But seeing the manufacturer’s latest machines all together at EICMA in Milan really drives home just how much broader LiveWire’s ambitions have become.

I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the company had everything from its upcoming lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.

It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a firm that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.

I also had a chance to spend several hours test-riding the S4 Honcho Street in Milan, so be on the lookout for that article and video to experience it with me.

But for now, let’s see what was at the LiveWire booth.

Perhaps the most important bikes at the booth were the S4 Honcho models, LiveWire’s newly introduced lightweight and lower-cost electric motorcycles.

According to recent reports, the production S4 Honcho Street made its European debut at EICMA alongside the dirt-oriented S4 Honcho Trail. The Trail version recently began reaching customers in the US, with the Street now en route to dealerships, and European sales are beginning around the EICMA launch.

According to recent reports, these bikes represent a significant departure from LiveWire’s earlier strategy. Instead of trying to compete directly with full-size gasoline motorcycles on outright performance, the Honcho platform is aimed at riders looking for something smaller, simpler, and more approachable.

And now the family is getting even bigger.

Also on display was the fresh S4 Honcho Skate, making its first public appearance.

The Skate is planned for 2027 and further expands the modular Honcho platform with a stripped-down, playful design.

For those who have followed H-D’s electric ambitions for as long as I have, you might even remember the original Harley-Davidson electric moped prototype that seems to have served as inspiration for the Honcho Skate’s design.

In a recent development, seeing the various Honcho versions together also makes LiveWire’s strategy with the platform much clearer. Rather than creating one small electric motorcycle, the manufacturer is building an entire family around the concept.

The other major attraction at LiveWire’s booth was the DUST lineup.

In a recent development, liveWire acquired the assets of DUST Moto earlier this year, bringing the lightweight electric dirt bike tech giant under its umbrella. EICMA marked the first public showing of the production-intent DUST Hightail under LiveWire ownership.

Recent findings suggest that the Hightail had already generated plenty of interest before the acquisition as a lightweight, high-performance electric dirt bike. Now we’re getting our first look at how that machine fits into LiveWire’s broader plans.

The firm is targeting a 2027 introduction for the production Hightail.

LiveWire also showed the fresh DUST Spur, another model planned for 2027 and intended to expand the newly formed DUST family.

The DUST acquisition is particularly interesting because it gives LiveWire an immediate foothold in the rapidly growing lightweight electric off-road motorcycle space without having to develop an entirely new platform from scratch.

In what could be a hint at faster charging to come, there was an interesting S2 Alpanista Corsa motorcycle that had been outfitted with a NACS plug and DC fast-charging capabilities.

LiveWire claimed a 20-80% charge in under 10 minutes, which would revolutionize the ability to do long-distance motorcycle touring, or just make it more convenient to get a quick charge and head back to your apartment.

There’s on word on whether the concept will make it to production, but the specs are enticing!

The most interesting part of LiveWire’s EICMA display may not have been any individual motorcycle, but rather what happens when you stand back and look at the entire booth.

Sources indicate that on one end you’ve got STACYC electric balance bikes. LiveWire says the brand has already introduced more than 250,000 riders to two wheels.

Recent findings suggest that then you’ve got the lightweight S4 Honcho family. Above that sit the DUST machines for more serious off-road riding, while LiveWire’s existing S2 motorcycles continue to cover the higher-performance street end of the spectrum.

That’s becoming something of an electric two-wheeler ladder.

A kid can theoretically start on a STACYC, graduate into increasingly capable electric two-wheelers, and eventually wind up on a proper electric motorcycle – all within the same corporate family.

And that feels particularly relevant at a show like EICMA, where much of the motorcycle industry is still trying to figure out exactly where electric motorcycles fit.

LiveWire seems increasingly convinced that the answer isn’t simply to build electric replacements for existing gasoline motorcycles.

Instead, the company is spreading out into categories where electric drivetrains can create different kinds of motorcycles altogether.

I’ve been following LiveWire’s evolution for years, and the organization standing in front of me at EICMA looks considerably different from the one that started out selling a single expensive flagship electric motorcycle.

The substantial, high-performance bikes are still vital, but machines like the S4 Honcho and DUST Hightail are arguably more interesting to me because they can bring entirely different riders into electric motorcycling.

According to recent reports, they’re smaller. They’re simpler. And perhaps most importantly, they’re targeting the kind of fun, accessible riding that doesn’t require superbike levels of performance.

There’s still plenty we need to learn about several of these latest models, particularly final specifications and pricing for the 2027 machines.

But seeing the Honcho, Honcho Skate, Hightail, Spur, and STACYC machines together at EICMA makes one thing pretty clear: LiveWire isn’t just trying to sell a few electric motorcycles anymore.

It’s trying to build an entire electric two-wheeler ecosystem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there’s no universally correct way to decorate a Christmas tree, though everyone seems to have an opinion about it. Some people swear by coordinated color palettes and perfectly spaced ornaments. Others treasure the funky glass baubles that have graced their family trees for decades, a hand-carved wooden figure picked up at a German Christmas market, or the lopsided ornament made in elementary school. The sentimental ones usually come with better stories. A Christmas tree, after all, is as much a collection of memories as it is a decorating opportunity.

And yet, there’s always room for one more. Maybe it’s a handblown glass ornament, a miniature version of your favorite food, or a decoration that’s so uniquely you it somehow feels essential. Your tree doesn’t need a theme, and your ornaments certainly don’t need to match. We’ve rounded up our favorites, including sculptural glass baubles, handwoven treasures, cheerful little oddities, and keepsakes you’ll look forward to unpacking every December.

According to recent reports, these 3D-printed ornaments have the nostalgic glow of vintage Christmas lights, even when the tree is unplugged. Designed by Austrian architecture firm Sheyn, their sculptural shapes give the classic holiday bauble a whimsical, modern twist. The watermelon and grapefruit hues are a refreshing departure from the usual red and green.

Industry observers note that sleek, understated, and not the least bit fussy, this Villeroy & Boch set deserves a moment beyond the tree. Tuck a few into a wreath or garland, where they won’t have to compete with a tree’s worth of tinsel and twinkling lights.

Recent findings suggest that trade sparkles for natural texture with these ornaments handcrafted by Colombian artisans in the Andes. They bring a well-traveled touch to your tree, and the best part is that each one is a surprise, with its color combination chosen by the maker. They’re also far less fragile than glass when your dog’s tail inevitably sends one flying.

In a recent development, if you’ve ever rearranged a vase just to catch the afternoon light, you’ll appreciate the way these ornaments from il Buco Vita play with it. Handblown in Italy from recycled glass, each one has subtle irregularities and shifting blue-green hues that take on a upcoming life among the twinkling lights on a Christmas tree. This delicate floral shape is pretty enough to keep out long after the tree comes down.

Here’s a new tradition for the little ones: Unwrap one of these miniature porcelain ornaments each day like an advent calendar as you sing your way through the Twelve Days of Christmas. The set from Lenox includes all the familiar characters, like the partridge in a pear tree and the twelve drummers drumming. Apologies in advance for the song getting stuck in everyone’s head.

It has been revealed that balsam Hill’s expertise with high-quality trees extend to their collection of decorative baubles. Don’t underestimate the power of classic shapes—like a set of metallic orbs in varying sizes.

Recent findings suggest that your love of rattan doesn’t have to stop at your furniture. These woven bell ornaments bring a little natural texture to the festivities, with warm, honey-colored tones that look right at home among your Christmas tree’s evergreen branches.

Industry observers note that you don’t need an Eichler home to have a very merry, midcentury Christmas. With their geometric silhouettes and gold detailing, these glass ornaments bring a dose of vintage glitz to the tree.

According to recent reports, leave it to Alessi to make Grinch green look downright elegant. These blown-glass ornaments, designed by Nika Zupanc for Alessi, dress up the famously mischievous shade with graphic stripes, playful polka dots, and touches of gold. Even the Grinch might reconsider his stance on Christmas.

According to recent reports, playing with sizing is key to adding dimension to your Christmas tree and these darling miniature ornaments offer a rainbow of colors to dial up the saturation on your tree. They come with mini ribbons that you’ll need to hand knot, but we think they add an extra personal touch.

According to recent reports, nostalgia looks best in a brass frame. With its braided border and antique-inspired finish, this ornament from McGee & Co. makes a thoughtful gift—just print a favorite photo and tuck it inside before wrapping.

Sources indicate that when in doubt, put a bow on it. These delicate velvet bows are slightly understated; pin them to the tree in lieu of ornaments for a charming coquettish vibe or have the two join forces for maximum drama.

Industry observers note that since your order for the table is always a dozen oysters on the half shell, why not dish out the same for your Christmas tree? And if you’re trying to nail down a fête-themed tree, you’ll probably want some Champagne to go with it as well.

According to recent reports, our love of gnomes is no secret, and a set of ten might just be enough for a holiday fix. Each fabric gnome measures 5.7" x 2.2" and can be hung from your tree or placed around the house as holiday decor.

In a recent development, pescatarian or tinned fish enthusiast, this glitter-flecked glass Christmas ornament is a lighthearted way to tell your favorite “girl dinner” guest how much you appreciate them. Coming in at 4" tall and 1.5" in diameter, it’s the perfect size for anchoring a branch.

In a recent development, you’ll thank us when you’re looking back at photos of the tree in January and admiring how dimensional it looks even from a phone screen. This set includes a collection of matte, metallic, and flocked ornaments so you don’t have to over think the process and you don’t have to go crazy buying individual ornaments.

Recent findings suggest that this French bread is made of glass, so it will really shine against your tree lights. It’s got a kitschy yet vintage vibe, and it will stand out from other icicle-style ornaments.

Recent findings suggest that vintage-inspired with wintery botanical etchings, these glassy ornaments have some rustic appeal but still feel elegant. We’d pair them with some silver tinsel to really bring the sparkle.

Handblown from clear, silver glass, these finials and spheres add some metallic elegance to your tree, especially if your inspiration is a disco ball.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD unveiled the Yangwang Altior, its newly introduced ultra-luxury EV with coach doors, over 1,000 km of CTLC range, a 1,000V fast-charging platform, and plenty of premium extras.

The “super-luxury executive flagship sedan,” as BYD calls it, made its official debut in Abu Dhabi, UAE, over the weekend.

For those who don’t know, Yangwang is BYD’s ultra-luxury sub-brand, sitting at the very top of its brand hierarchy.

The Atrio is Yangwang’s largest and most luxurious sedan, set to compete with high-end brands like Rolls-Royce, Bentley, and Mercedes-Benz Maybach.

Measuring 5,600 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, and 1,590 mm tall, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase, BYD’s flagship sedan sits squarely between the Rolls-Royce Ghost and Phantom (standard wheelbase) in length.

BYD said the “Golden Body Proportions” are designed to maximize interior space for both front and rear passengers.

Its meticulous front-end design is inspired by “Ding,” a traditional ancient Chinese cauldron, featuring “diamond-cut” headlights, a 137-gemstone dot-matrix grille, and, to top it off, a 24K pure gold car emblem sits up front and center.

The coach doors create a grand entrance, with the front doors opening at an 80-degree angle and the rear doors opening to a 90-degree angle.

Inside, the flagship sedan takes luxury up a notch with a massive, full-length panoramic center infotainment screen that extends from the driver to the passenger side.

The “Wrap-around cockpit” is designed to create an immersive, premium experience, with four executive seats and a central island for rear passengers that includes vehicle controls, storage, and even a champagne glass holder.

In a recent development, BYD noted it offers the most second-row space in its class, but didn’t reveal specifics. The zero-gravity “cloud-like” rear seats feature a four-ball mechanical massage head, you know, for those longer trips.

Meanwhile, the front passenger seat can fold at the push of a button to open up more space for rear passengers.

The interior features premium materials, including full-grain genuine leather seats, diamond-cut detailing, real wood trim, and natural lambswool foot pads.

And that’s not all. It also has a 39-speaker Dynaudio Platinum Evidence high-end sound system that creates an immersive 360-degree “hall-level” sound experience.

The Yangwang Altio is packed with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including a high-speed tire-blowout stability system, emergency float mode, and in-place U-turn or tank-turn control using its quad-motor e4 platform.

It's main rival is the Maextro S800, which wasn't in the list.

It also uses BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Fast Charging Technology, which provides a CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles).

Sources indicate that the flagship sedan features “extremely fast flash charging,” BYD stated, thanks to its 1000V ultra flash charging tech. It takes just five minutes to charge the vehicle’s battery from 10% to 70%. To go from 10% to 97% it takes just nine minutes.

BYD opened orders for the limited-edition “Mountain and River Rhyme” Yangwang Altrio model, which will be extremely exclusive with just 399 units.

Sources indicate that buyers can place a reservation with a 300,000 yuan ($45,000) deposit. BYD didn’t reveal final prices, but the global version is expected to start at around 2 million yuan ($300,000).

Tech Report: Fresh York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10%

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Newly introduced York State Common Retirement Fund raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than 10% in the third quarter, to 352,850 shares worth $54.0 million at Sept.
  • According to recent reports, that is an increase of a little more than 10%.
  • It has been revealed that the fund is one of the largest public pension prepares in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Newly introduced York State Common Retirement Fund raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than 10% in the third quarter, to 352,850 shares worth $54.0 million at Sept. 30. The pension fund disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Tuesday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It added 33,000 shares from the 319,850 it reported at June 30.

According to recent reports, that is an increase of a little more than 10%. The filing does not say why the pension fund added the shares. The reported value nearly doubled, to $54.0 million from $27.8 million. Strategy’s stock closed the quarter at $153.09, up from $86.93 at midyear, so most of the gain in dollar value came from the rally, not from the added shares.

It has been revealed that the fund is one of the largest public pension prepares in the U.S. It holds the assets used to pay retirement benefits for Newly introduced York’s state and local public employees. Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, the fund’s trustee, valued it at an estimated $309.7 billion as of June 30, the latest official figure. There is not yet a published valuation for Sept. 30.

Industry observers note that public equities are only part of the portfolio. As of March 31, they accounted for 39.4% of the fund’s assets, with the rest in cash and bonds, private equity, real estate and other alternatives. The 13F lists 2,975 holdings worth $71.3 billion. The Strategy stake is a small slice of that book, less than a tenth of a percent.

Strategy has made bitcoin its primary treasury asset. The company held 850,849 bitcoin as of Nov. 15, with an aggregate purchase price of $64.20 billion, or $75,452 a coin. Institutional managers have 45 days after quarter-end to file a 13F. Tuesday’s report is the first official look at the pension fund’s third-quarter buying, after the stock had already fallen sharply from the $153.09 price used in the filing.

Strategy closed Tuesday at $96.50, below $100 and about 37% under its Sept. 30 close. At that price, the same 352,850 shares are worth about $34 million, roughly $20 million less than the value in the filing. The common shares also finished under Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, which closed at $98.70. That is the first time they have closed below the preferred since mid-August.

The stock is down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close of $121.07. A 13F is a snapshot. It does not show whether the pension fund bought or sold shares in October or November, when most of that decline took place.

The information table lists no shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust or other spot bitcoin ETFs, and no shares of Strategy’s preferred stock. The pension fund does hold Coinbase (COIN). It reported 109,433 shares at Sept. 30, a little below the 111,633 shares it held at midyear. The reported value still rose, to $20.4 million from $16.3 million, as Coinbase’s stock climbed.

It has been revealed that it also holds a string of bitcoin miners. IREN, listed in the filing as Iris Energy, was the largest of those positions, at 154,600 shares worth $6.3 million, up from 140,100 shares at midyear. The fund trimmed most of its other mining stakes during the quarter. The remaining names included Hut 8, TeraWulf, Riot, Cipher, Core Scientific, MARA Holdings, CleanSpark, Bitdeer and Bit Digital.

Together, the mining shares were worth about $21.6 million at Sept. 30. Even added together, the Strategy, Coinbase and mining positions were worth about $96 million, a thin sliver of the 13F book. California’s public employees’ pension fund, CalPERS, held a slightly larger Strategy position at the same date: 374,740 shares worth $57.4 million, its 13F filed Monday indicates.

The next 13Fs, covering the fourth quarter, are due in February.
